«خِطبة تتمحور حول المسيح» سلسلة من الرسائل عن الخِطبة التقوية، ألقاها بول هيرشبيرغر. وقد ألقى هذه الرسائل مرات عديدة في أماكن مختلفة على مدى السنوات العشر الماضية. ومؤخرًا، قمنا بتفريغها واختصارها لتكون أوضح عند القراءة. بعد طباعة المقالات الست كلها في نبض البقية، سننشرها في كتيّب. هذه هي المقالة الأولى من ست مقالات.

مقدمة

حظيت أنا وزوجتي بامتياز خِطبةٍ بلا ندم أو شعور بالذنب. وقد باركنا الله بوالدين أرشدانا إلى الطريق الصحيح وأتاحا لنا فرصًا لم تتح لهما.

إن لم تكن لديك شهادة أو ذكرى كهذه، فالرجاء ألا تستسلم للشعور بالذنب. لكن صلاتي من أجلك أن يشتعل في قلبك عبء ورؤية لأن تحظى بهذا لأولادك. وقد يكون ذلك مكافأتك.

الخِطبة التي تتمحور حول المسيح فترةٌ بين حياة العزوبية والحياة الزوجية. والقرارات التي تتخذها في هذه الفترة ستؤثر فيك بقية حياتك. وببركة الله على حياتك، يمكنك أن تصل إلى حياة بلا ندم أو شعور بالذنب.

خمسة أهداف لسلسلة الخِطبة التي تتمحور حول المسيح.

الهدف رقم 1. أن تُرَدَّ قلوب الآباء إلى أولادهم.

الهدف رقم 2. أن تُرَدَّ قلوب الأولاد إلى آبائهم.

الهدف رقم 3. أن يحمل الوالدان عبئًا يقودهما إلى إرشاد كل واحد من أولادهما إلى مشيئة الله الكاملة لحياته.

الهدف رقم 4. أن يحمل الشباب عبئًا يدفعهم إلى طلب الله، وإيجاد الإشباع والهدف في السير مع الله، وأن تسعوا إلى النضج في سلوككم وشخصيتكم.

الهدف رقم 5. أن ينهض الشبان والشابات ليكونوا آباءً وأمهات أتقياء، لهم رؤية لتربية جيل آخر تقي، وليستمر إنجيل يسوع المسيح.

خطة الله للرجل والمرأة

يقول سفر الجامعة 12:1: «اذكر خالقك في أيام شبابك، قبل أن تأتي الأيام الشريرة، ولا تقترب السنين التي تقول فيها: ليس لي فيها سرور». أمنيتي أن يذكر كل واحد منكم خالقه في أيام شبابه. وجّه قلبك وتركيزك وحياتك إلى السعي وراء خالقك، الله القدير في السماء.

ماذا يعني بقوله «قبل أن تأتي الأيام الشريرة» و«ولا تقترب السنين»؟ يعني أن تطلب الرب وأنت شاب. خذ طاقة شبابك واطلب الله. أيها الشباب، أنتم شباب وممتلئون بالأفكار والرؤى والخطط والأحلام. لا أظن أن أحدًا منكم يستمتع بمجرد الجلوس في كرسي مريح، ورفع قدميه، والحلم بمدى فظاعة الحياة ورهبتها. نحن لا نفعل ذلك، أليس كذلك؟ لكن إن لم نسِر مع الله ونتبع خطته، فستحل بنا أمور صعبة. وعندما تحل بنا أمور صعبة في الحياة، لن يكون لنا ملجأ نلجأ إليه. نحلم بأن تسير الحياة على ما يرام. لكن القرارات والأفعال التي نتخذها في شبابنا تؤثر فينا بقية حياتنا. والخبر السار أنها قد تؤثر فينا تأثيرًا حسنًا. أما الخبر السيئ فهو أنها قد تؤثر فينا تأثيرًا سيئًا. وهذا يعتمد على القرارات والخيارات التي نتخذها. لكن أيها الشباب، أنتم شباب، ولديكم فرصة للاختيار.

لنذهب إلى بداية سفر التكوين.

«وقال الرب الإله: ليس جيدًا أن يكون آدم وحده، فأصنع له معينًا نظيره. وجبل الرب الإله من الأرض كل حيوان البرية وكل طيور السماء، وأحضرها إلى آدم ليرى ماذا يدعوها. وكل ما دعا به آدم ذات نفس حية فهو اسمها. فدعا آدم بأسماء جميع البهائم وطيور السماء وجميع حيوانات البرية، وأما آدم فلم يجد له معينًا نظيره. فأوقع الرب الإله سباتًا على آدم فنام، فأخذ واحدة من أضلاعه وملأ مكانها لحمًا. وبنى الرب الإله الضلع التي أخذها من آدم امرأة، وأحضرها إلى آدم. فقال آدم: هذه الآن عظم من عظامي ولحم من لحمي. هذه تُدعى امرأة لأنها من امرئ أُخذت. لذلك يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلتصق بامرأته، ويكونان جسدًا واحدًا» (التكوين 2:18-24).

«وقال الله: نعمل الإنسان على صورتنا كشبهنا، فيتسلطون على سمك البحر وعلى طيور السماء وعلى البهائم وعلى كل الأرض وعلى جميع الدبابات التي تدب على الأرض. فخلق الله الإنسان على صورته، على صورة الله خلقه، ذكرًا وأنثى خلقهم. وباركهم الله وقال لهم: أثمروا وأكثروا واملأوا الأرض وأخضعوها، وتسلطوا على سمك البحر وعلى طيور السماء وعلى كل حيوان يدب على الأرض» (التكوين 1:26-28).

«وقال الرب الإله: ليس جيدًا أن يكون آدم وحده، فأصنع له معينًا نظيره» (التكوين 2:18). «أصنع له معينًا ملائمًا له». قال الله إنه سيفعل ذلك.

«فخلق الله الإنسان على صورته، على صورة الله خلقه، ذكرًا وأنثى خلقهم» (التكوين 1:27). الله صنع. الله خلقنا ذكرًا وأنثى. يتطلب الأمر قدرًا كبيرًا من الإيمان الأعمى للاعتقاد بأننا تطورنا على نحو كامل كذكور وإناث. خلق الذكر والأنثى هو خطة الله. وهو أحد البراهين الحية على الخلق. الله صنع. الله خلق. إنها خطة الله. الله هو المؤلف. وخطة الله تجلب البركة.

أود أن ألقي نظرة على عشرة جوانب مختلفة من بركة خطة الله هذه.

1) الله يأتي بحواء إلى آدم.

«وبنى الرب الإله الضلع التي أخذها من آدم امرأة، وأحضرها إلى آدم. فقال آدم: هذه الآن عظم من عظامي ولحم من لحمي. هذه تُدعى امرأة لأنها من امرئ أُخذت» (التكوين 2:22-23).

جعل الله آدم يغرق في سبات عميق. ثم خلق حواء وأتى بها إلى آدم. استيقظ آدم وأدرك: «هذه لي!» كان قد رأى جميع الحيوانات تمر به حين سمّاها. والآن يأتيه الله بشخص ملائم له. وأدرك أيضًا: «أُخذت من جانبي». إنها قريبة من قلبه. «هذه عظم من عظامي ولحم من لحمي». ليست كلبًا ولا زرافة ولا قردًا ولا قردًا من القردة العليا. هذه التي أتى بها الله إليه تشبهه. في خطة الله بركة.

لم يكن لآدم وحواء رفيق من قبل. ولم يسبقا أن أطلقا مشاعر قلبيهما. حدث شيء في قلبي آدم وحواء. كان آدم «رجل امرأة واحدة»، وكانت حواء «امرأة رجل واحد». لم يمنحا عواطف قلبيهما لأي شخص آخر. ولدى الله هذه الخطة لنا أيضًا. خطة الله تجلب البركات.

2) الترك والالتصاق في وحدة مدى الحياة.

«لذلك يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلتصق بامرأته، ويكونان جسدًا واحدًا» (التكوين 2:24).

تقول هذه الآية: «لذلك يترك الرجل أباه وأمه»، لكن آدم وحواء لم يكن لهما أب أو أم. ما يقوله الله هو أنه لا يمكن أن يكون هناك التصاق ما لم يكن هناك ترك. ونقرأ أيضًا في مرقس 10:7: «من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلتصق بامرأته». هذه خطة الله، وخطة الله تجلب البركة.

الترك يعني أن يترك المرء وراءه، وأن يتخلى. وعبارة «من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه» تعني أن يترك الرجل والديه وراءه. فكّر في شاب يعيش حياة منزلية جيدة جدًا. إنه مبارك ولديه كل ما يحتاج إليه. ومع ذلك، حين يأتي الله بحواء إلى حياته، ينهض شيء في داخله ويقول: «سأرحل!» لكن هذه خطة الله، وخطة الله تجلب البركة.

لا يقتصر الأمر على ترك أبيه وأمه، بل يلتصق أيضًا بامرأته. ومعنى الالتصاق هو «أن يلتصق بشيء، أن يرتبط به». نحن نعرف ألواح الخشب الملصقة. وتُصنع أنواع كثيرة من الأثاث المتين من ألواح ملتصقة بعضها ببعض. وإذا أُلصقت على نحو صحيح، فلن تنفصل عند المفاصل. وإذا مزقتها، فستضطر إلى تمزيق الخشب نفسه. وغراء الله يعمل بالطريقة نفسها، إذ يلصق شخصين معًا. والطريقة الوحيدة لفصلهما هي تحطيمهما وتمزيقهما، والله لا يبارك ذلك. أما الترك والالتصاق، والبقاء معًا والارتباط، فهذه خطة الله وتجلب البركة.

3) يكونان جسدًا واحدًا.

«لذلك يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلتصق بامرأته، ويكونان جسدًا واحدًا» (التكوين 2:24). شخصان عازبان يصيران زوجين، ويصبحان وحدة واحدة أمام الله، وأسرة واحدة أمام الله. يصيران جسدًا واحدًا، ويراهما الله معًا كواحد.

«ويكون الاثنان جسدًا واحدًا. إذًا ليسا بعد اثنين بل جسد واحد. فالذي جمعه الله لا يفرقه الإنسان» (مرقس 10:8-9). خطة الله للرجل والمرأة هي أن يأتي بحواء إلى آدم، ثم يحدث الترك والالتصاق، ويجعلهما جسدًا واحدًا. والانفصال لا يجلب أي بركة، بل يجلب العذاب والألم والمشقة والأذى. لا بركة في الانفصال، لكن خطة الله تجلب البركة.

4) لا نير غير متكافئ.

«لا تكونوا تحت نير مع غير المؤمنين، لأنه أية خلطة للبر والإثم؟ وأية شركة للنور مع الظلمة؟» (كورنثوس الثانية 6:14-15). «المرأة مرتبطة بالناموس ما دام رجلها حيًا، ولكن إن مات رجلها فهي حرة لكي تتزوج بمن تريد، في الرب فقط» (كورنثوس الأولى 7:39).

خطة الله أن يكون الزواج نيرًا متكافئًا. لن يأتي الله بحواء إلى آدم في زواج يكون فيه النير غير متكافئ. لنتأمل في الترك والالتصاق والارتباط، وفي صيرورة الاثنين واحدًا. في الزواج يصير الاثنان الآن واحدًا أمام الله. تخيل أن تكون في علاقة زوجية سيئة كهذه، وفي أسرة كهذه تحاول أن تسير أمورها معًا. لن تكون هناك بركة.

لكن النير المتكافئ يجلب البركة! يريد الله أن نكون متحدين جسدًا واحدًا، وقلبًا واحدًا، وفكرًا واحدًا. يريد أن يرانا متحدين في القلب والفكر والكيان كله، كأننا واحد. خطة الله تجلب البركة.

5) خطط الله أن يكون لنا أولاد.

«وباركهم الله وقال لهم: أثمروا وأكثروا واملأوا الأرض وأخضعوها، وتسلطوا على سمك البحر وعلى طيور السماء وعلى كل حيوان يدب على الأرض» (التكوين 1:28). فكّر في الفرح والمعجزة كلما وُلد طفل آخر في بيت مسيحي. لقد خطط الله للأمر هكذا. وإذا أتى الله بحواء إلى آدم، وتركها والتصق بها، وصارا جسدًا واحدًا وقلبًا واحدًا وفكرًا واحدًا، فإذا كانا مرتبطين بنير متكافئ وباركهما الله بأولاد، صار بيتهما ملاذًا مبهجًا يستطيع الله أن يسكن فيه. «وبارك الله نوحًا وبنيه وقال لهم: أثمروا وأكثروا واملأوا الأرض» (التكوين 9:1). «وأما أنتم فأثمروا وأكثروا، وتكاثروا في الأرض وأكثروا فيها» (التكوين 9:7). خطة الله تجلب البركة.

6) ترتيب الرئاسة.

«ولكن أريد أن تعلموا أن رأس كل رجل هو المسيح، وأما رأس المرأة فهو الرجل، ورأس المسيح هو الله» (كورنثوس الأولى 11:3). الله، ثم المسيح، ثم الرجل، ثم المرأة. أقام الله ترتيبًا للرئاسة، وهذا الترتيب بركة. إنها خطة الله، وهي بركة.

«أيها الأولاد، أطيعوا والديكم في الرب لأن هذا حق. أكرم أباك وأمك، التي هي أول وصية بوعد، لكي يكون لكم خير وتكونوا طوال الأعمار على الأرض» (أفسس 6:1-3). طاعة الوالدين في الرب جزء من ترتيب الرئاسة. هذا ليس صعب الفهم، أليس كذلك؟ البيت الذي يتبع خطة الله هو ببساطة بيت مبارك. أيها الشباب، تعلموا أن تكونوا تحت السلطة. اجعلوا ذلك أولوية قصوى. كلما تعلمتم أن تكونوا تحت السلطة مبكرًا، ازددتم استعدادًا لمسؤوليات الحياة.

أتذكر أنني كنت أنظر إلى الحياة الزوجية وأطمح إلى تعليم الأولاد وتربية أسرة تقية. استمعت إلى سلسلة «البيت التقي» وظننت أنني مستعد للانطلاق. لكن جاء اليوم الذي صار فيه الدور دوري والمسؤولية مسؤوليتي، وفجأة شعرت أن قلبي يريد أن يذبل. فالمسؤولية لا تبدو كما يبدو الحلم بها. أنت بحاجة إلى أن تفعل شيئًا! أنت المسؤول. عليك أن تجعل الأمر يحدث. وبالمناسبة، ليس عليك أن تجعله يحدث فحسب؛ بل عليك أن تجعله يحدث على نحو يشبه المسيح. عليك أن تجعله يحدث بطريقة تحل بها مسحة روح الله على أسرتك. وكلما تعلمنا على نحو أفضل كيف نكون تحت السلطة، ازددنا استعدادًا لتلك المسؤوليات. وكلما أدركنا حاجتنا إلى الله، تحسنت حالنا. لنجعل تعلم الخضوع للسلطة أولوية قصوى، كأطفال وشباب. «يا ابني، لا تنسَ شريعتي، بل ليحفظ قلبك وصاياي، فإنها تزيدك طول الأيام وسني الحياة والسلام» (الأمثال 3:1-2).

سيضيف الله بركته إن بقينا في ترتيب الرئاسة هذا. وكلما تعلمت كيف تكون تحت السلطة، ازدادت بركتك حين تؤسس بيتك. لخطة الله بركات.

7) زواج تقي.

تقول أفسس 5:21,22,24: «خاضعين بعضكم لبعض في مخافة الله. أيتها النساء، اخضعن لرجالكن كما للرب... فكما تخضع الكنيسة للمسيح، كذلك النساء لرجالهن في كل شيء».

انظروا أولًا إلى الآية 21: «خاضعين بعضكم لبعض». ينبغي أن يحدث تآلف في البيت التقي. وينبغي أن يحدث هذا التآلف في مخافة الله. فإذا خضعنا بعضنا لبعض في مخافة الله، أطعنا الله لأننا نريد بركاته.

أفسس 5:22,24: «أيتها النساء، اخضعن لرجالكن كما للرب... فكما تخضع الكنيسة للمسيح، كذلك النساء لرجالهن في كل شيء». أيتها الشابات، يمكنكن الاعتماد على هذا: الخضوع للأب يساوي الخضوع للزوج. يمكنك أن تتدربي وأنت عزباء. وهذا يساعد على بناء شخصيتك. لن تجلب المرأة المتمردة والمعاندة بركة الله.

ويتابع في أفسس 5:25,28,29: «أيها الرجال، أحبوا نساءكم كما أحب المسيح أيضًا الكنيسة وأسلم نفسه لأجلها... كذلك يجب على الرجال أن يحبوا نساءهم كأجسادهم. من يحب امرأته يحب نفسه. فإنه لم يبغض أحد جسده قط، بل يقوته ويربيه، كما الرب أيضًا للكنيسة». أيها الشبان، تقول هذه الآيات إن على الأزواج أن يحبوا زوجاتهم. فمن تظنون أن الله وضعه في حياتكم ليهيئكم لمحبة زوجاتكم؟ أمكم! أتريدون أن تتعلموا كيف تحبون زوجاتكم؟ تعلموا كيف تتفاهمون مع أمهاتكم، وأحبوا أمهاتكم واهتموا بهن. أتريدون أن تتدربوا على محبة زوجاتكم في المستقبل؟ فابدؤوا بمحبة أمهاتكم.

الآية 33: «وأما أنتم أيضًا، فليحب كل واحد امرأته هكذا كنفسه، وأما المرأة فلتُكرم زوجها». خطة الله تجلب البركات.

8) وارثين معًا نعمة الحياة.

بطرس الأولى 3:7: «كذلك أيها الرجال، كونوا ساكنين بحسب الفطنة مع الإناء النسائي كالأضعف، معطين إياهن كرامة، كوارثين معًا نعمة الحياة، لكي لا تُعاق صلواتكم». نحن الأزواج نكرم الزوجة. فهي الإناء الأضعف وهي التي تلد الأولاد! وقد مرّت بتغييرات كثيرة وصعبة في حياتها. وهي التي تجهد وتتعب قبل غيرها.

ويقول: «أيها الرجال، كونوا ساكنين معهن بحسب الفطنة».

أيها الشبان، تعلموا أن تفهموا أمهاتكم وأخواتكم. سيساعدكم ذلك بعد أن تتزوجوا. لا تستنتجوا قائلين: «آه، هكذا هن النساء فحسب». لا، أنتم تريدون بركة الله. تعلموا معرفتهن وفهمهن.

«وارثين معًا نعمة الحياة». يريد الله أن نكون وارثين معًا نعمة الحياة. إن لم نكن وارثين معًا نعمة الحياة، فهل يمكننا أن نكون وارثين لنعمة الحياة كلٌّ على حدة؟ لا أظن ذلك. يقول إنه ينبغي أن نكون وارثين معًا لكيلا تُعاق صلواتنا. فإذا كنا وارثين منفصلين، فهل يمكننا القول إن صلواتنا ستُعاق؟ نعم، ستُعاق صلواتنا. أكرموا الزوجة كإناء أضعف. وكل جهد تبذلونه في هذا المجال لن يفعل إلا أن يبارككم لاحقًا. إنه يستحق العناء. خطة الله تجلب البركة.

9) بيت مبارك وآمن.

يأتي هذا جزئيًا من بطرس الأولى 3:7، وكذلك من المزمور 144:12: «ليكن بنونا مثل غروس نامية في صباهم، وبناتنا كأعمدة زوايا مصقولة على مثال قصر». تحل نعمة الله على بيت آمن تسوده الوحدة؛ حيث يفهم الأب الأم ويهتم بها. والأب يخدم ويكون حاضرًا ليساعد ويرشد، ويكون هناك ليقدم التوجيه بقلب رحيم. خطة الله للرجل والمرأة — خطة الله تجلب البركات.

10) كما المسيح والكنيسة.

«فكما تخضع الكنيسة للمسيح، كذلك النساء لرجالهن في كل شيء. أيها الرجال، أحبوا نساءكم كما أحب المسيح أيضًا الكنيسة وأسلم نفسه لأجلها، لكي يقدسها مطهرًا إياها بغسل الماء بالكلمة، لكي يحضرها لنفسه كنيسة مجيدة، لا دنس فيها ولا غضن أو شيء من مثل ذلك، بل تكون مقدسة وبلا عيب. كذلك يجب على الرجال أن يحبوا نساءهم كأجسادهم. من يحب امرأته يحب نفسه. فإنه لم يبغض أحد جسده قط، بل يقوته ويربيه، كما الرب أيضًا للكنيسة» (أفسس 5:24-29).

«أيها الرجال، أحبوا نساءكم كما أحب المسيح أيضًا الكنيسة وأسلم نفسه لأجلها». يبحث الله عن رجال مستعدين لبذل حياتهم. أيها الشبان العزاب، هل أنتم مستعدون لتلبية الدعوة وبذل حياتكم؟ هذه دعوة سامية من الله. إنها خطة الله.

أيها الشبان، هل أنتم مستعدون لبذل حياتكم والتخلي عن خططكم وعن الأمور المستقلة التي تحبون فعلها؟ هل أنتم مستعدون للتحلي بالصبر واللطف والتفهم؟ هل أنتم مستعدون لقلة النوم ومواصلة المسير حتى عندما تكونون متعبين؟ هل أنتم مستعدون للهدوء وعدم الانفعال في الظروف المجهدة؟ هل أنتم مستعدون لقيادة زوجة وأولاد، نفوس أبدية، وإرشادهم في هذه الحياة؟

لكنني أرجوكم أن تتطوعوا وتقولوا: «أنا مستعد أن أبذل جهدي في كلمة الله ومشيئة الله وخطة الله، وسأبذل حياتي. أنا مستعد أن أضعها على المذبح». بذل يسوع حياته من أجلنا، وهو يقارن الزواج بالكنيسة وبعلاقته بها.

وهناك أيضًا حاجة إلى أمهات خاضعات ومسلمات للسلطة، أمهات لا يتبعن حركة تحرير المرأة في أيامنا، بل يكتفين بأن يكنّ حارسات للبيت.

أيتها الشابات، هل أنتن مستعدات للالتحاق؟ هل ستقدمن قلوبكن لتُوجَّهن وتُرشدن؟ هل أنتن مستعدات لاتباع سلطتكن والخضوع لها بفرح؟ هل أنتن مستعدات للخدمة وبذل أنفسكن من أجل أسرتكن؟ هل أنتن مستعدات للخدمة وبذل أنفسكن من أجل أسرتكن أنتن؟ إن تزوجتن يومًا ما، فستكون أسرتكن أنتن هي التي تخدمنها وتبذلن أنفسكن من أجلها. هل أنتن مستعدات لتحمل الألم والمشقة؟ هل أنتن مستعدات لأن تكنّ معينات، وتبذلن أنفسكن من أجل عبئه ورؤيته؟

لكن حين ننظر إلى خطة الله وبركاته، فأنتم تريدون بركة الله، أيها الشباب! وهذا يعني أن عليكم اتخاذ الخيارات المناسبة. انهضوا واتخذوا قرارات تقود إلى النضج. يأتي النضج من خلال السعي وراء الله. اعقدوا العزم في قلوبكم على أن تفتحوا أنفسكم لبركات الله ومبادئه. أشجعكم على السير مع الله، وعلى إقامة علاقة مع يسوع المسيح، وعلى فعل ذلك بتواضع.

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

Jamin, de oito anos, não era muito inteligente. Ou pelo menos era isso que o irmão mais velho lhe dizia. Quase diariamente, o irmão Kenny encontrava maneiras de lembrar Jamin de suas falhas e rir de seus tropeços.

“Jamin, você nunca será inteligente”, dizia Kenny. Lá no fundo, Jamin sentia-se resignado a uma vida de confusos enganos. Será que ele seria sempre desajeitado? Será que sempre diria as coisas erradas? Era o que Kenny dizia.

Jamin acreditava nas lições de Kenny com os olhos arregalados. Kenny era três anos mais velho do que ele, então devia estar certo. Muito bem, então Jamin seria simplório. Kenny seria esperto. A vida não era justa. Papai e Mamãe não gostavam do discurso orgulhoso de Kenny e o puniam sempre que entravam no meio de uma de suas falas. Mas Kenny tinha um jeito de evitar ser ouvido. Assim, continuava zombando de Jamin.

A avó Otto observava essas provações de sua cadeira de balanço na varanda. Era uma senhora quieta.

“Jamin, você sabe onde está Kenny?”, perguntou a mãe com um sorriso. “Está quase na hora do jantar.”

“Ele foi verificar as armadilhas para coiotes. Vou procurá-lo.”

Havia um arrepio no ar enquanto ele atravessava o gramado, e o sol já envelhecia quando cruzou a orla da mata. As sombras fugidias corriam pelas colinas. O frio aumentou à medida que ele avançava. Respirou o ar carregado e seguiu a trilha de Kenny. Por fim, a trilha terminaria em um prado, mas Jamin esperava encontrar Kenny antes de ter de ir tão longe. As várias armadilhas já tinham sido verificadas, então Jamin sabia que Kenny havia passado por ali. Jamin prosseguiu com determinação. Sua cabeça dourada captava os raios cansados que fugiam do sol e tremeluziam por entre as árvores. Logo, eles também haviam desaparecido, deixando para trás o cheiro almiscarado da mata. As lagartas-tecedeiras-do-outono tinham trabalhado, e suas cortinas de teia pendiam dos galhos acima.

Por fim, quando as árvores rarearam e o prado surgiu, Jamin soube que ali terminava o percurso das armadilhas de seu irmão. Se Kenny não estivesse ali, ele não saberia onde mais procurar.

Mas Kenny estava ali. Quando Jamin entrou no prado, viu à sua direita um amontoado frustrado. A voz do amontoado tinha um timbre familiar. O rosto do amontoado estava contorcido de dor. O amontoado era Kenny. “Você está bem? O que aconteceu?” Jamin sentiu-se estranho ao ver Kenny encolhido na terra. Kenny era esperto. “Você pisou numa armadilha?”

“Sim, Jamin. Eu… eu não estava olhando por onde andava. Ajude-me. Por favor.”

Jamin se curvou e encontrou um tornozelo firmemente preso nas mandíbulas de uma armadilha de aço. A escuridão cobria o chão ao redor de Kenny. Rapidamente, os braços fortes de Jamin abriram as mandíbulas. Kenny cambaleou para fora da armadilha. “Você consegue andar?”

“Sim. Acho que sim. Se você me apoiar, consigo mancar.”

“Papai e Mamãe vão ficar preocupados. Perdemos o jantar.”

De fato, enquanto os irmãos mancavam de volta pela mata, ouviram o pai chamando longamente. Jamin respondeu, e em um instante o pai estava ao lado deles; viu o tornozelo e ergueu Kenny como uma ovelha ferida. A estranha turminha apressou-se para casa, e a porta de tela bateu quando o pai atravessou a varanda. Jamin foi até a lavanderia e esfregou as mãos. Dirigiu-se à porta da frente.

“Jamin.” Era a avó. A luz da varanda a mostrava em sua velha cadeira de balanço. Um pesado cobertor repousava sobre seus ombros.

“Sim, vovó?”

“Você acha que não é muito inteligente?”

“É isso que Kenny diz.” Jamin se contorceu.

“Você teve força suficiente para abrir a armadilha, e Kenny não. Você teve coragem de encontrá-lo no escuro. Muitos meninos não teriam.” Jamin ficou em silêncio. A avó Otto balançou mais um pouco a cadeira, depois sorriu. “Deus fez você do jeito que é por uma razão, Jamin. Fez Kenny do jeito que é por uma razão. Ele tem um plano para você e um lugar que só você pode ocupar, sabe.”

Jamin virou-se e entrou na cozinha aquecida. Estava sorrindo.

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Ulimwengu wa Baba yetu ni ulimwengu ambao haujaharibiwa na uvumbuzi na uingiliaji wa binadamu. Ingawa dhambi na teknolojia vimepotosha na kuiba mambo mengi mazuri kutoka kwa wanadamu, bado kuna machache ambayo hayajaharibiwa na ustaarabu. Watoto wadogo, katika kutokuwa na hatia kwao safi ya asubuhi isiyochafuka, wako mstari wa mbele kama kipande cha mbinguni duniani na kuwaelekeza watazamaji wote mbinguni. Jambo jingine ni ndege wa angani kama wanavyotajwa katika Mwanzo. Paulo aliliuliza kanisa la Korintho, “Je, maumbile yenyewe hayawafundishi?” Tunahimizwa kuyatazama maua ya mashambani, kunguru na nyasi za shambani. Kila moja ya hivi hudhihirisha kwa namna ya pekee Mungu wa milele katika uhai wake na kutufundisha kuhusu Muumba wake. Labda maumbile yote yanaweza kutupa taswira za makao ya mbinguni kama tungekuwa na muda na macho ya kuyatazama.

Ndege wana nafasi ya pekee katika uumbaji wa Mungu, kwa maana makao yao yako mbinguni. Mwanadamu anaweza kupaa kwa kutumia mabawa ya ndege na kuepuka dunia ya chini kwa saa chache, lakini mbingu hazitakuwa kamwe mahali pa mamlaka yake ya kawaida. Ndege ni mfano wa jamii ya mbinguni, kwa maana huko ndiko nyumbani kwao. Ni mfano wa kawaida wa watakatifu na malaika wa Mungu, kwa hiyo ni vema kuwapa uangalifu unaostahili. Ingawa kunaweza kuwa na masomo mengi ya kujifunza kutoka kwa viumbe hivi vya neema na uzuri, mojawapo ya sifa zao mashuhuri na zilizo wazi zaidi huonekana katika nyimbo wanazoimba. Wanyama wengi waishio duniani kwa kiasi kikubwa hawatoi sauti. Miongoni mwa wale wanaotoa sauti, mara nyingi hufanya hivyo ili kutisha au kuonyesha malalamiko. “Je, punda-mwitu hulia akiwa na majani? Au ng’ombe huomboleza akiwa na lishe yake?” (Ayubu 6:5). Wanapokuwa na furaha na kuridhika, hawana ujumbe wa kuwasilisha. Mbwa hubweka kwa mvamizi ili kumfukuza, huku paka akilia ili kuvuta umakini. Hutoa sauti wanapotishwa au kutoridhika, kwa hofu au kwa maumivu. Vivyo hivyo, mwanadamu wa duniani hushiriki tabia ya mamalia wa mashambani.

Ndege ni wa aina nyingi. Huimba kwa furaha kiasi kwamba wao ni kielelezo cha furaha. Usemi “mwenye furaha kama ndege aina ya lark” ni wa kawaida sana hata hutumiwa na watu ambao hawajawahi kwenda shambani kumwona au kumsikia lark. Ingawa huenda wengine wakatuambia kuwa nyimbo hizi ni miito tu ya kupandana na hazihusiani sana na hisia zao, hatuwezi kuepuka hisia yetu ya ndani kwamba, wawe wanapandana au la, ndege hawa hufurahia kuonyesha furaha kubwa, nasi tunafanya vyema kuwaacha watufundishe. “Je, kuna mtu mwenye furaha? Na aimbe zaburi” (Yakobo 5:13). Ndege hufanya hivi bila kukoma, na inaonekana haiwezekani kufikia hitimisho jingine lolote isipokuwa kwamba wana furaha wanapoimba. Ukitembea karibu na kiota cha mbayuwayu, utagundua kuwa nao wana njia za kuonyesha kutofurahishwa. Killdeer naye hasiti kuwaonyesha kwa ukali wale wanaovamia eneo lake kwamba hawatakiwi humo, lakini hayo hayapaswi kudhaniwa kuwa nyimbo. Ndege waimbaji ni picha nzuri ya watakatifu na malaika wa Mungu.

Ni kiasi kidogo jinsi gani tunavyoelewa kuhusu mbinguni. Taswira za mbinguni zilizoelezwa na kuwekwa mbele yetu katika Ufunuo haziwezi kuifikisha kwa urahisi akili yetu yenye mipaka katika ulimwengu wake usio na mipaka. Jambo moja tunaloweza kuelewa ni kwamba ni mahali palipojaa nyimbo. Si ajabu, kwa maana huko ndiko mwisho wa safari ya watakatifu wa Mungu walioridhika na kujawa na furaha, nao wataimba wimbo mpya. Karibu kila tukio kwenye kiti cha enzi katika Ufunuo lina sifa ya namna fulani ya kusifu. “Naye ametia wimbo mpya kinywani mwangu, sifa kwa Mungu wetu” (Zaburi 40:3). Katika matukio 22, Maandiko yanarudia maneno haya: “Nitaimba.”

Ni asili ya ndege kuimba. Wazo lao la kwanza wanapoamka huja alfajiri inapopamba anga, na wimbo hutiririka kutoka ndani yao kama chemchemi. Nyimbo zao hazifanani zote. Baadhi ni changamani kwa urefu, kipimo na sauti, huku nyingine zikiwa rahisi. Baadhi yao hutweta tu kwa moyo wa furaha. Robin huanzisha kwaya mwanzoni mwa masika, lakini wimbo wake hufunikwa upesi kwa uzuri na wimbo wa song sparrow, na baadaye tena na rose-breasted grosbeak. Wimbo wa wren unawazidi wote kwa urefu na uchangamfu. Canary huimba ndani ya kizimba, huku nightingale akiimba gizani. Robins huimba mvua inaponyesha. Buntings hujaza anga kwa nyimbo wakati wa joto la mchana, ndege wengine wanapokuwa kimya. Ingawa nyimbo zao hutofautiana, wote hufurikwa na furaha isiyo na kiasi. Hapo ndipo watakapokuwa walimu wetu.

“Mkisemezana kwa zaburi na nyimbo za sifa na nyimbo za rohoni, huku mkiimba na kumwimbia Bwana mioyoni mwenu” (Waefeso 5:19). Kuja kwa Kristo kulidhihirishwa na jeshi la malaika lililotangaza amani na nia njema kwa wanadamu. Wote watakaolibeba Jina lake lazima wapeleke ujumbe huohuo. Katika Yohana 4, tunakuta tukio kwenye kisima cha Yakobo, ambako Kristo anamwomba mwanamke maji ya kunywa. Jibu lake linaonekana kuwa na uchungu kidogo. “Wayahudi hawashirikiani na Wasamaria.” Ingawa alijiona kuwa mtu wa kiroho na alimfuata kwa hiari katika mazungumzo ya kidini, hakuwa na wimbo. Kama kisima walichokuwa wakizungumzia, maji yake yalikuwa yamefukiwa chini kabisa ya uso wa ardhi, na kuyafikisha juu kulihitaji juhudi kubwa kama nini. Kristo anatoa njia nyingine. “Lakini maji nitakayompa yatakuwa ndani yake chemchemi ya maji bubujikayo hata uzima wa milele” (Yohana 4:14).

Kisima cha Kristo ni kisima cha artesian. Hakihitaji mtungi wala juhudi ya kuyateka maji, kwa maana maji yake hububujika kwa wingi yenyewe. Ingawa huenda Kristo alikuwa akizungumza kuhusu Roho, kama ilivyo katika Yohana 7:38, bila shaka jambo hili linaweza kutumika vivyo hivyo kwa moyo uliojaa furaha. Ni jambo gani linalofaa zaidi kutiririka kutoka chemchemi iliyochochewa na Kristo kuliko wimbo wa shangwe? “Tazama, watumishi wangu wataimba kwa shangwe moyoni” (Isaya 65:14). Yote haya yanapaswa kuwa wazi vya kutosha kueleweka na rahisi vya kutosha kutenda, lakini, ole wetu, tunakuta tuna adui anayepinga daima na bila kuchoka, anayetaka kuzuia wimbo wetu. Tunajua hila zake...

Dhambi. Si ndege wote wanaoimba. Wapo ambao sura zao ni nyeusi kama dhambi. Wao huonekana kupiga kelele na kupiga mayowe tu, nao si mfano wa kuigwa na watakatifu wa Mungu. Kelele za vurugu tunazosikia kutoka kwa magari mengi yanayopita zinafanana na nyimbo za ndege wachafu wa namna hiyo. “Babeli mkuu umeanguka, umeanguka, umekuwa makao ya pepo, na ngome ya kila roho mchafu, na tundu la kila ndege najisi na mwenye kuchukiza” (Ufunuo 18:2). Viumbe hawa wengi ni roho zilizoanguka, ndege wanaongojea kuimeza mbegu iliyopandwa kando ya njia. Miongoni mwao ni blackbirds, starlings, na grackles wasio na faida. Kunguru nao huonekana kando ya barabara, wakila mizoga inayooza. Mara nyingi utawakuta wengi wakila mahindi ambayo mkulima aliyapanda kwa taabu kwa ajili yake mwenyewe. Hivyo ndivyo nafsi yenye ubinafsi hutenda dhambi inapofuatilia furaha, ikifurahia balaa la mwingine na kutumia dhambi yake kujinufaisha. Haina wimbo, kwa maana siku yake hufunikwa daima na makosa ya wengine wanaokutana nayo njiani.

Kutelekeza. Cowbird naye ni mweusi (jike ni wa kahawia/kijivu). Atakaa mahali pa juu penye mandhari pana, bila aibu akiwaita wapenzi wake kwa milio mikali. Kisha huwa na ujasiri wa kutaga yai lake kwenye kiota cha ndege mwingine na kuwalazimisha kuwalea watoto wake. Hakika huu ni mfano unaofaa wa wanawake wengi wa siku zetu. Ingawa huenda mazingira yakawa sababu yao, wanawake hawa hawajali watoto wao wenyewe, bali wameathiriwa na kutelekezwa. Hawana wimbo wa kubembeleza wa kushiriki na watoto wao, kwa maana wamewapeleka kwenye kiota cha mwingine huku akili yao ikiwa imezongwa na kazi na biashara. “Lakini Wewe ndiwe uliyenitoa tumboni; uliniwekea tumaini nilipokuwa matitini mwa mama yangu” (Zaburi 22:9). Bila shaka mama anayeimba anaweza kumjaza mtoto wake nyimbo nyingi na kuweka msingi wa maisha yenye furaha na tumaini. Ingawa tunaweza kumhurumia mwanamke aliye katika hali ngumu, wimbo mkuu wa wanawake wa kisasa una sauti zisizopatana na za huzuni tu. Hivi ni visima vilivyozibwa kwa udongo, kama vile visima ambavyo Isaka alikuta aliporudi Gerari. Wafilisti “walikuwa wamevijaza udongo” (Mwanzo 26:15). Ndivyo ilivyo katika nyumba nyingi leo zilizotelekezwa kiroho: familia zimejaza ratiba zao na shughuli za kidunia kiasi kwamba hazina muda wa kutumia saa moja kuimba pamoja. Kama ndege wangeacha kuimba, je, wangetambua hata hivyo?

Kukosa shukrani. Ukimpata mtu aliyejaa kutokuwa na shukrani, utampata mtu asiye na wimbo. Kama canary angekataa kuimba akiwa kifungoni, wengi wetu tusingesikia kamwe melodia yake ya uchangamfu. “Tulizitundika vinubi vyetu juu ya mierebi iliyokuwa katikati yake. Kwa maana waliotuchukua mateka walitutaka tuwaimbie wimbo; waliotuharibu walitutaka tufurahi, wakisema, Tuimbieni mojawapo ya nyimbo za Sayuni. Tutawezaje kuuimba wimbo wa BWANA katika nchi ya ugeni?” (Zaburi 137:2-4). Mungu alikuwa amewaagiza watu wake kupitia Yeremia wajenge nyumba, wapande bustani na kulea familia. “… Naitafutieni amani miji ambayo nimewapeleka mateka, na kuiombea kwa BWANA; kwa maana katika amani yake ninyi mtakuwa na amani” (Yeremia 29:5-7). Lakini hawakuona thamani yake. Macho yao yalipokazia mandhari ya kuhuzunisha iliyowazunguka, walipoteza wimbo wao. Israeli ilikuwa na utamaduni tajiri wa nyimbo katika historia yake. Nyimbo zao zililipuka walipovuka Bahari ya Shamu, na katika siku za Yehoshafati, na ziliweza kushinda majeshi. Usumbufu wa maisha ya duniani si kisingizio cha kunyima shukrani, kwa maana Mungu wetu anatawala, nasi ni watoto wake. Hayo ndiyo yaliyokuwa mazingira katika gereza la Filipi ambamo wafungwa wawili, Paulo na Sila, walianzisha tamasha katikati ya usiku na kutikisa korido kwa nyimbo zao za furaha.

Tunapofungua vinywa vyetu na kutumia sauti zetu kumsifu Mungu, tunaonyesha neema ya Mungu kwa matendo yetu. Tunaungana na kwaya ya waaminifu pamoja na Miriamu, Debora na Hana, na kuimba kwa upatano na Musa, Daudi, Paulo na Barnaba. Jioni, tunaimba pamoja na Bwana wetu na wanafunzi wake baada ya chakula cha jioni, na pamoja na majeshi ya malaika “wakimtukuza Mungu juu mbinguni.” Kama hilo halitoshi, labda tunapaswa kufikiria kuamka alfajiri na kuimba pamoja na makundi yasiyohesabika ya marafiki zetu wenye manyoya wanaomshukuru Mungu kwa majaliwa yake yenye upendo. “Neno la Kristo likae kwa wingi ndani yenu katika hekima yote; mkifundishana na kuonyana kwa zaburi, nyimbo za sifa na nyimbo za rohoni, huku mkiimba kwa neema mioyoni mwenu kwa Bwana … Na kila mfanyalo, lifanyeni kwa moyo, kama kwa Bwana, wala si kwa wanadamu” (Wakolosai 3:16, 23).

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

Η επείγουσα ανάγκη της τελευταίας στιγμής είναι κάτι με το οποίο πολλές νοικοκυρές ασχολούνται τακτικά. Όσο οργανωμένες κι αν είμαστε, μερικές φορές αναβάλλουμε εργασίες επειδή δεν μας αρέσουν ή περιμένουμε μέχρι να νιώσουμε την πίεση.

Η συνήθης αναβλητικότητα μπορεί να οδηγήσει σε υψηλότερα επίπεδα άγχους. Ίσως να είμαι παράξενη, αλλά μου είναι δύσκολο να παραμείνω ήρεμη και συγκροτημένη όταν αυξάνεται η πίεση. Μέχρι να ολοκληρωθούν τα πράγματα της τελευταίας στιγμής είμαι τόσο εξαντλημένη που δεν απολαμβάνω το προγραμματισμένο γεγονός.

Πονόδοντοι και ταξίδια με αυτοκίνητο

Μου είναι μυστήριο γιατί κάποιο μέλος της οικογένειας καταλήγει στην οδοντιατρική καρέκλα μία ή δύο μέρες πριν φύγουμε για ταξίδι. Ίσως δεν έχει συμβεί τόσο συχνά όσο νομίζω, αλλά η απογοήτευση ενός απρογραμμάτιστου ραντεβού στον οδοντίατρο σε ακατάλληλη στιγμή έχει χαραχτεί στο μυαλό μου. Τώρα προγραμματίζω ένα φανταστικό ραντεβού πριν από ένα ταξίδι. Αν δεν πρόκειται για οδοντιατρική έκτακτη ανάγκη, κάποιο άλλο θέμα θα γεμίσει αυτό το κενό στο πρόγραμμα.

Οι προθεσμίες είναι ένα φυσιολογικό κομμάτι της ζωής. Χωρίς αυτές δεν θα είχαμε κίνητρο και οι μέρες μας θα στερούνταν σκοπού. Οι παρεμβολές επίσης είναι φυσιολογικό κομμάτι της ζωής. Δίνουν διαρκώς μια απρόβλεπτη στροφή στις μέρες και τις εβδομάδες μας. Αν αφήσουμε πάρα πολλές εργασίες για την τελευταία στιγμή, οι παρεμβολές και οι προθεσμίες συγκρούονται και βασιλεύει το χάος.

Αλλάξτε το σενάριο της τελευταίας στιγμής

Δεν μπορούμε να εξαλείψουμε τις προθεσμίες και τις παρεμβολές, αλλά μπορούμε να περιορίσουμε τις εργασίες της τελευταίας στιγμής. Μερικές φορές χρειάζεται ειλικρινής ανασκόπηση για να καταλάβουμε τι προκάλεσε το άγχος μας. Συχνά το ρίχνουμε στις παρεμβολές και δεν συνειδητοποιούμε ότι ο κακός προγραμματισμός ή η αναβλητικότητα μπορεί να ήταν ο ένοχος.

Για παράδειγμα, αν έρχονται επισκέπτες και σκοπεύουμε να πλύνουμε τα παράθυρα και να φτιάξουμε ένα γλυκό μαζί με δώδεκα ακόμη εργασίες την ημέρα της άφιξής τους, δεν υπάρχει χώρος για απρόοπτα. Από την εμπειρία γνωρίζουμε ότι θα υπάρξουν παρεμβολές. Άρα, δεν είναι καλύτερο να «προγραμματίσουμε» ένα τσίμπημα μέλισσας και ένα χτύπημα στο δάχτυλο του ποδιού;

Γιατί να μην προγραμματίσουμε το πλύσιμο των παραθύρων και το γλυκό για άλλη μέρα; Αυτό μπορεί να σημαίνει μερικά δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα στα παράθυρα και ένα απλούστερο γλυκό, αλλά δεν είναι αυτό καλύτερο από πολύ άγχος την τελευταία στιγμή;

Κάντε μερικές εργασίες νωρίτερα

Η απόφαση νωρίς μέσα στην ημέρα για το τι να ετοιμάσουμε για δείπνο και το να πακετάρουμε την τσάντα με τα απαραίτητα για το μωρό εκ των προτέρων είναι μικρά πράγματα που μπορούν να κάνουν μεγάλη διαφορά την τελευταία στιγμή. Όταν τα παιδιά μας ήταν μικρά, άρχισα να πακετάρω τις βαλίτσες μια μέρα πριν από ένα ταξίδι αντί την ημέρα της αναχώρησης. Μπορούσα να ανταπεξέλθω καλύτερα στην τελευταία βιασύνη αν αυτή η δουλειά είχε ήδη γίνει.

Κάντε πρώτα τις πιο σημαντικές εργασίες

Αυτή η προσέγγιση δίνει την ελευθερία να παραλείψουμε εργασίες μικρότερης σημασίας όταν είμαστε πιεσμένοι από τον χρόνο.

Μερικές φορές δεν είναι όλα στη λίστα εργασιών εξίσου πολύτιμα. Το να αφήσεις μια εργασία είναι δύσκολο για έναν τελειομανή, αλλά είναι δυνατό να αναπτύξεις νέες συνήθειες.

Χωρίστε τη δουλειά σε μικρότερα κομμάτια

Μερικές φορές το μέγεθος μιας εργασίας την κάνει να φαίνεται υπερβολικά μεγάλη για να ξεκινήσει. Διασπάστε τη μεγάλη εργασία σε μικρότερα μέρη. Η ολοκλήρωση μιας μικρότερης εργασίας είναι πολύ πιο διαχειρίσιμη. Ο γενικός καθαρισμός της κουζίνας μου είναι μια εργασία που δεν απολαμβάνω. Αν το ημερολόγιό μου λέει «γενικός καθαρισμός κουζίνας», είναι εύκολο να το αγνοήσω.

Αλλά αν το ημερολόγιό μου λέει «καθαρίστε τις συσκευές, σκουπίστε τα ντουλάπια και πλύνετε τα παράθυρα», φαίνεται πιο εφικτό.

Υπάρχουν τόσα πολλά χαρούμενα γεγονότα στη ζωή· γιατί να ταλαιπωρούμαστε από αναβλητικότητα; Δώστε στον εαυτό σας την ελευθερία να ζήσει διαφορετικά. Μερικές μικρές αλλαγές μπορούν να κάνουν τη μεγαλύτερη διαφορά ανάμεσα σε μια ευλογημένη ή μια αγχωμένη τελευταία στιγμή.

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Je, unaamini miujiza? Je, unaamini mambo yasiyo ya kawaida? Vipi kuhusu uingiliaji wa Mungu? Au swali bora zaidi linaweza kuwa, je, umemwona Mungu akifanya kazi katika maisha yako? Je, wengine wanamwona Mungu akifanya kazi katika maisha yako?

Ndugu yangu alikuwa akifanya kazi kwenye chafu ya mimea mteja mmoja alipoingia na kustaajabia uzuri wa mimea yote. Kisha akasema kwa mshangao jinsi alivyoivutiwa na bidii yetu yote. Ndugu yangu akajibu, “Mmoja hupanda, mwingine humwagilia, lakini Mungu ndiye anayekuza.” Mteja akajibu, “Hapana, hapana, usimpe Mungu sifa. Ninyi mlitoka hapa na kufanya kazi hii yote. Mlipanda, mkamwagilia na kuweka mbolea kwenye mimea hii yote, na ninyi nyote mnastahili sifa, si Mungu!” Sababu iliyomfanya mtu huyo ahisi hivyo ni kwamba alikuwa mwanahumanizimu.

Humanizimu ni nini?

Kamusi hufafanua humanizimu hivi: mtazamo au mfumo wa mawazo unaoweka umuhimu mkuu kwa mambo ya kibinadamu badala ya mambo ya kimungu au yasiyo ya kawaida. Imani za wanahumanizimu husisitiza thamani na wema unaoweza kupatikana kwa wanadamu, hukazia mahitaji ya pamoja ya wanadamu, na hutafuta njia za kimantiki pekee za kutatua matatizo ya wanadamu.

Ikiwa Mungu yupo, basi itatubidi tukubali ukweli huo na kuwajibika mbele zake. Wanahumanizimu hujaribu kuthibitisha kwamba Mungu hayupo, ili waishi maisha yao kwa uhuru wapendavyo. Kwa mujibu wa humanizimu, hakuna Mungu. Ikiwa ndivyo, basi sisi wanadamu tuko juu ya Mungu. Kila kitu ni kwa ajili yetu na furaha yetu ya mwisho. Hii ndiyo fasili ya humanizimu.

Aina Mbili za Humanizimu

Kuna aina mbili za imani za humanizimu, na tutaziangalia zote. Imani ya kwanza ni nadharia kwamba hakuna Mungu. Kwa kweli, hii inaonekana kuwa njia pekee ya kimantiki ya kuwa mwanahumanizimu. Kila kitu kimeumbwa na mwanadamu na kwa ajili ya mwanadamu. Hakuna mambo mengine yanayochangia wala uingiliaji wa nguvu zisizo za kawaida. Kila kitu hutokea kwa sababu na akili ya kawaida. Kuna maelezo ya kimantiki kwa kila kitu kinachotokea. Bila shaka, baadhi ya mambo hayana maana, lakini wanahumanizimu huyapuuza na kuangalia tu mambo yanayoweza kuelezwa. Kama ilivyo kwa mimea kwenye chafu, wanatazama yote anayofanya mwanadamu na kupuuza sehemu isiyo ya kawaida ya mmea kuchipua na kupata uhai mpya. Wanasayansi kote ulimwenguni wanajitahidi kutumia mantiki ya kibinadamu kueleza kila jambo lililowahi kutokea, hata kuumbwa kwa ulimwengu. Wanasayansi, pamoja na elimu na hekima yao yote, hujaribu kutoa maelezo ya kimantiki kuhusu kwa nini majanga ya asili na migogoro ya kimataifa hutokea. Ikiwa wanaweza kueleza kila kitu, basi wanaweza kukanusha Mungu na uwepo wake. Hili huwezesha wanadamu kufanya wapendavyo bila matokeo ya milele. Hilo, kwa upande mwingine, husababisha hisia kubwa ya amani ya uongo.

Wanahumanizimu, pamoja na hoja zao zote, hudhihaki uwepo wa Mungu wenyewe. Ukienda katika vyuo vingi nchini Marekani na kuzungumza na watu kuhusu Ukristo, wanakucheka na kudhihaki ukweli kwamba Wakristo wanaamini kweli katika Mungu.

Aina ya pili ya imani ya humanizimu ni nadharia inayokubali kwamba Mungu yupo. Mtaalamu mmoja wa anthropolojia alidai kwamba humanizimu ni mradi wa usasa na mwendelezo wa teolojia ya Kikristo ya Magharibi iliyofanywa kuwa ya kidunia. Lakini ukiwauliza watu wanadhani humanizimu ina maana gani, huenda ukapata majibu tofauti, na jambo hilo linakuwa lenye kutatanisha sana. Lakini kwa nini mkanganyiko huo? Kwa sababu watu wanajaribu kuwa wanahumanizimu Wakristo. Humanizimu ya Kikristo imekosolewa mara nyingi kwa kuwa na utata na kuwa vigumu kuifafanua. Sababu iliyofanya jambo hilo liwe lenye kutatanisha sana ni kwamba watu wanataka kumwamini Mungu lakini pia kujitumaini wenyewe na kuamini kwamba ulimwengu huwazungukia.

Katika Warumi tunasoma, “Kwa maana ghadhabu ya Mungu inadhihirishwa kutoka mbinguni juu ya uasi wote wa Mungu na udhalimu wa wanadamu wanaoizuia kweli kwa udhalimu. Kwa sababu yale yanayoweza kujulikana kuhusu Mungu yamewekwa wazi ndani yao, kwa maana Mungu amewafunulia. Kwa maana mambo yake yasiyoonekana, yaani, nguvu zake za milele na Uungu wake, yanaonekana wazi tangu kuumbwa kwa ulimwengu, yakitambuliwa kupitia vitu vilivyoumbwa; kwa hiyo hawana udhuru. Kwa maana, ingawa walimjua Mungu, hawakumtukuza kama Mungu wala kumshukuru, bali wakawa bure katika mawazo yao, na mioyo yao ya upumbavu ikatiwa giza. Wakijidai kuwa wenye hekima, wakawa wapumbavu, wakabadili utukufu wa Mungu asiyeharibika na kuufananisha na sanamu ya mwanadamu anayeweza kuharibika, na ya ndege, na ya wanyama wenye miguu minne, na ya viumbe vitambaavyo. Kwa hiyo Mungu naye akawaacha wafuate uchafu, kwa tamaa za mioyo yao wenyewe, ili wayavunjie heshima miili yao wao kwa wao. Waliibadili kweli ya Mungu kuwa uongo, wakakiabudu na kukitumikia kiumbe badala ya Muumba, anayehimidiwa milele. Amina. Kwa sababu hiyo Mungu akawaacha wafuate tamaa za aibu; kwa maana hata wanawake wao walibadili matumizi ya asili na kutumia yale yaliyo kinyume na asili. Vivyo hivyo wanaume pia, wakiacha matumizi ya asili ya mwanamke, wakawaka kwa tamaa wao kwa wao; wanaume wakifanya mambo yasiyofaa na wanaume wenzao, nao wakipokea ndani yao adhabu ya upotovu wao iliyowastahili. Na kwa kuwa hawakuona vema kumtambua Mungu, Mungu akawaacha wafuate akili potovu, wafanye mambo yasiyofaa; wamejaa udhalimu wa kila namna, uasherati, uovu, tamaa mbaya, nia ya kudhuru; wamejaa wivu, uuaji, ugomvi, udanganyifu, uovu; wasengenyaji, wachongezi, wamchukiao Mungu, wenye dharau, wenye kiburi, wenye majivuno, wavumbuzi wa mambo maovu, wasiotii wazazi, wasio na ufahamu, wasio waaminifu katika maagano, wasio na upendo wa asili, wasiopatanishwa, wasio na huruma. Ingawa wanajua hukumu ya Mungu, kwamba wanaofanya mambo hayo wanastahili kifo, si kwamba wanayafanya tu, bali pia wanawakubali wanaoyafanya” (Warumi 1:18-32).

Basi, mtu anawezaje kuwa mwanahumanizimu na kumwamini Mungu? Hapa ndipo tunapokaribia zaidi nyumbani. Mwanahumanizimu wa aina hii anaamini kwamba Mungu anataka awe na furaha. Anamwamini Mungu Muumba, lakini kwa kweli haamini kwamba anapaswa kumtumikia. Hamwamini Mungu wa kweli, bali akilini mwake amejiumbia mungu wa kubuni asiye na uhai. Hilo linamwezesha kuishi kwa ajili yake mwenyewe na furaha yake mwenyewe. Mtu wa aina hii atazungumza kuhusu Mungu, kwenda kanisani, kuimba nyimbo na kusema sala. Hata hivyo, atategemea wanadamu pekee kwa mahitaji yake yote. Akiwa mgonjwa, humwita daktari. Akihitaji pesa, huenda kwa benki. Akihitaji kupumzika kutokana na uhalisi wa maisha, huenda likizoni au mapumzikoni. Huishi kwa ajili ya furaha yake mwenyewe kisha humshukuru Mungu, ingawa hakumtegemea Mungu kwa mahitaji yake. Watu hawa hujitegemea. Hujiamini wenyewe.

Huu hapa mfano: Mkristo anapanda bustani na kuitunza kila siku. Humwagilia na kuweka mbolea, hung’oa magugu na kupogoa mimea. Hatimaye, mimea yake yote huanza kuzaa matunda, matunda mazuri. Humshukuru Mungu kwa mavuno mengi. Jirani yake, mwanahumanizimu asiyeamini kwamba Mungu yupo, naye pia alipanda bustani. Yeye pia alitoka kila siku, akamwagilia, akapogoa, akang’oa magugu na kuweka mbolea. Naye pia alipata mavuno mengi. Hata hivyo, mtu huyu alijisifu kwa yote aliyokuwa amefanikisha. Wanaume hao wawili walifanya mambo yaleyale na kupata matokeo yanayofanana. Mmoja alimpa Mungu sifa, na mwingine akajipa sifa. Atasema kwamba alifanikiwa kufanya jambo lilelile bila Mungu ambalo jirani yake alifanya akiwa na Mungu. Wakristo wanajua kwamba amekosea na kwamba kwa kweli alimhitaji Mungu ili kukuza bustani yake.

Jambo linapotokea linalohitaji uingiliaji wa nguvu zisizo za kawaida, mwanahumanizimu Mkristo huomba na kuwaomba wengine waombe. Hata hivyo, haamini kwamba Mungu atajibu maombi yao, na mara moja huanza kutatua tatizo lake kwa kutumia mantiki ya kibinadamu pekee. Kisha, tatizo likitatuliwa, humshukuru Mungu kwa hilo. Aina hii ya humanizimu imeuchanganya ulimwengu wa kisasa. Imewafanya wasioamini kuidhihaki imani ya Kikristo na kuiita dini ya uongo isiyo na nguvu.

Mkristo haamini katika mantiki ya kibinadamu. Mkristo anaamini kwamba Mungu wa mbinguni ndiye sababu ya kila kitu. “Kwa maana vitu vyote viliumbwa kwa njia yake, vilivyo mbinguni na vilivyo duniani, vinavyoonekana na visivyoonekana, ikiwa ni viti vya enzi, au mamlaka, au falme, au nguvu; vitu vyote viliumbwa kwa njia yake, na kwa ajili yake” (Wakolosai 1:16). Sisi si kitu bila Yeye, na bila Yeye hatuwezi kufanya chochote. Ukristo ni kinyume cha humanizimu. Mkristo anapofanya jambo lisilo la kawaida, jambo ambalo mwanahumanizimu au asiyeamini kwamba Mungu yupo hawezi kufanya, tunakuwa na jambo litakalowashangaza wenye hekima.

Jirani anapomwona Mkristo akiwapenda adui zake, akimsamehe mtu aliyemkosea na kufanya mambo ambayo yeye hawezi kufanya, huanza kujiuliza nguvu za kufanya mambo hayo zimetoka wapi. Hilo humwongoza kwa Baba. Tusipofanya jambo lolote lisilo la kawaida, anashangaa.

Vipi Kuhusu Sisi?

Ninaogopa kwamba tunaangukia katika mtego huu wa ‘Humanizimu ya Kikristo.’ Tunazungumza kana kwamba tunaamini; tunasema tunamwamini Mungu. Tunaenda kanisani, tunaimba nyimbo na kusema sala. Hata hivyo, kwa jinsi tunavyoonekana kwa nje, tunajitegemea wenyewe. Kwa sababu tumeweka sisi wenyewe na ustawi wetu katikati ya maisha yetu, Mungu wa mbinguni hatutusikii. Maombi yetu hayajibiwi, na wakati tunaotumia kupiga magoti ni mgumu sana. Tunafuata taratibu kwa sababu ndivyo tulivyofundishwa, lakini imani yetu iko katika mantiki ya kibinadamu.

Inaweza kuwa vigumu sana kumtafuta Bwana huku ukiishi katika jamii ya kihumanizimu, jamii iliyokamilisha jitihada za kutafuta uhuru na furaha. Polepole, kanisa linaanza kujisalimisha kwa njia za ulimwengu huu.

Mhudumu mmoja kutoka China alikuwa akitembelea makanisa nchini Marekani. Kabla ya kuondoka na kurejea China, aliulizwa ni jambo gani lililomvutia zaidi kuhusu makanisa ya Marekani. Alijibu, “Ninashangazwa na yote waliyofanikiwa kufanya bila Mungu.”

Tutakuwa tumefanya vyema tukirahisisha fasili ya kisasa ya humanizimu. Mwanahumanizimu kwa fahari hukana kwamba kuna Mungu anapojisifu kwa nguvu na uwezo wake mwenyewe. Hutangaza mafanikio makubwa ya mwanadamu na kumdhihaki Mkristo mnyenyekevu.

Mkristo hujikana mwenyewe, huuchukua msalaba wake na kumfuata Bwana wake. Mkristo hajivuni yeye mwenyewe wala uwezo wa mwanadamu, bali hukiri kwa ujasiri kwamba yeye ni mavumbi tu na kwamba atarudi mavumbini upesi. Mkristo hutafuta mema kwa wengine na kumtumaini Mungu kwa mahitaji na mahangaiko yake yote ya kila siku.

Wakristo huamini kwamba wao ni watumishi tu wa bwana wao. Wanachukiwa na ulimwengu, wanadharauliwa na wengi na kukataliwa. “Ikiwa ulimwengu unawachukia, jueni kwamba ulinichukia mimi kabla ya kuwachukia ninyi. (Yohana 15:18)” Kwao, maisha haya si kutafuta furaha. Mambo ya ulimwengu huu hayawavutii hata kidogo. Furaha na amani yao hutokana tu na kumtumikia bwana wao na kumpendeza Baba yao wa Mbinguni. Kwa ulimwengu, wao ni wa ajabu. Wapumbavu. Kwa Mungu, wao ni watoto wake wapendwa.

Mungu bado anatafuta watu leo watakaoweka tumaini lao kwake. Anatazama dunia yote akitafuta mtu, mahali fulani, atakayeweka kando mantiki ya kibinadamu na akili ya kawaida na kutii sauti kutoka mbinguni. Mungu anataka watu wenye imani watakaopiga hatua na kuingia katika mambo yasiyo ya kawaida, kama Abrahamu, Musa, Daudi na maelfu ya waumini waliowafuata. Mtu atakayejikana mwenyewe na kuikataa dunia hii na kumfuata Mwokozi.

Maisha haya yatakapokwisha, wanahumanizimu, wawe wanasema wanamwamini Mungu au la, wataangamia. Nao Wakristo wataendelea kuishi milele katika utukufu.

Mwanahumanizimu? Mkristo? Mwanahumanizimu Mkristo? Wewe ni yupi?

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.
