Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Credi nei miracoli? Credi nel soprannaturale? E nell'intervento divino? O una domanda migliore potrebbe essere: hai visto Dio operare nella tua vita? Gli altri vedono Dio operare nella tua vita?

Mio fratello lavorava nella serra quando un cliente entrò e si meravigliò della bellezza di tutte le piante. Poi esclamò quanto fosse impressionato da tutto il nostro duro lavoro. Mio fratello rispose: «Alcune piante, un po' d'acqua, ma è Dio che dà l'aumento». A cui il cliente rispose: «No, no, non attribuite il merito a Dio. Siete venuti qui e avete fatto tutto questo lavoro. Avete piantato, annaffiato e concimato tutte queste piante, e voi tutti meritate il merito, non Dio!» Il motivo per cui l'uomo la pensava così era che era un umanista.

Cos'è l'umanesimo?

Il dizionario definisce l'umanesimo così: una visione o un sistema di pensiero che attribuisce importanza principale alle questioni umane piuttosto che a quelle divine o soprannaturali. Le credenze umaniste sottolineano il valore potenziale e la bontà degli esseri umani, enfatizzano i bisogni umani comuni e cercano modi puramente razionali per risolvere i problemi umani.

Se Dio esiste, allora dovremo riconoscere questo fatto e rendere conto a Lui. Gli umanisti tentano di provare che Dio non esiste, così da poter vivere liberamente la loro vita come vogliono. Secondo l'umanesimo, non c'è Dio. Se così fosse, allora noi, la razza umana, saremmo superiori a Dio. Tutto è per noi e per la nostra felicità ultima. Questa è la definizione di umanesimo.

Due tipi di umanesimo

Esistono due tipi di credenze umaniste, e ne esamineremo entrambe. La prima è la teoria che non esiste alcun Dio. In realtà, questa sembra essere l'unica via razionale per essere umanisti. Tutto è creato dall'uomo e per l'uomo. Non ci sono altri fattori o coinvolgimenti soprannaturali. Tutto accade per ragione e buon senso. C'è una spiegazione logica per tutto ciò che accade. Certo, alcune cose non hanno senso, ma gli umanisti scartano quelle e guardano solo le cose che possono essere spiegate. Come le piante nella serra, osservano tutto ciò che l'uomo fa e ignorano la parte soprannaturale di una pianta che germoglia nuova vita. Scienziati in tutto il mondo lavorano diligentemente per inserire il ragionamento umano in tutto ciò che è mai accaduto, persino nella creazione del mondo. Scienziati, con tutto il loro sapere e la loro saggezza, cercano di dare spiegazioni logiche sul perché avvengono disastri naturali e crisi globali. Se possono spiegare tutto, allora possono escludere Dio e la Sua esistenza. Questo permette alla razza umana di fare come le pare senza conseguenze eterne. Questo, a sua volta, conduce a un grande senso di falsa pace.

Gli umanisti, con tutto il loro ragionamento, deridono la stessa esistenza di Dio. Se vai nella maggior parte dei college in America e parli con le persone del cristianesimo, ridono di te e prendono in giro il fatto che i cristiani credano davvero in Dio.

Il secondo tipo di credenza umanista è una teoria che riconosce l'esistenza di Dio. Un antropologo sosteneva che l'umanesimo è un progetto della modernità e una continuazione laicizzata della teologia cristiana occidentale. Ma se chiedi alle persone cosa pensano significhi umanesimo, probabilmente otterrai risposte diverse, e diventa molto confuso. Ma perché la confusione? Perché le persone cercano di essere umanisti cristiani. L'umanesimo cristiano è stato spesso criticato per la sua vaghezza e la difficoltà a definirlo. Il motivo per cui è diventato così confuso è che la gente vuole credere in Dio ma anche credere in se stessa e che il mondo ruoti intorno a loro.

In Romani leggiamo: «L'ira di Dio si rivela dal cielo contro ogni empietà e ingiustizia degli uomini, che soffocano la verità nell'ingiustizia; poiché quel che si può conoscere di Dio è manifesto in loro, avendolo Dio manifestato loro. Infatti le sue qualità invisibili, la sua eterna potenza e divinità, si vedono chiaramente fin dalla creazione del mondo, essendo comprese per mezzo delle cose che ha fatto; perciò essi sono inescusabili. Infatti, pur avendo conosciuto Dio, non lo hanno glorificato come Dio né gli hanno reso grazie; ma sono diventati vani nei loro ragionamenti e il loro cuore stolto si è oscurato. Dichiarandosi sapienti, sono diventati stolti e hanno mutato la gloria del Dio incorruttibile in immagini simili all'uomo corruttibile, agli uccelli, ai quadrupedi e ai rettili. Perciò Dio li ha abbandonati all'impurità, secondo i desideri dei loro cuori, affinché disonorassero i propri corpi tra loro; essi hanno mutato la verità di Dio in menzogna e hanno adorato e servito la creatura invece del Creatore, che è benedetto in eterno. Amen. Per questo Dio li ha abbandonati a passioni infami: infatti le loro donne hanno mutato l'uso naturale in quello contro natura; allo stesso modo anche gli uomini, lasciando l'uso naturale della donna, si sono infiammati di desiderio gli uni per gli altri, commettendo atti indecenti, uomini con uomini, e ricevendo in se stessi la meritata ricompensa del loro traviamento. E poiché non ritennero opportuno conservare la conoscenza di Dio, Dio li ha abbandonati a una mente reproba, perché facessero ciò che non conviene; essendo pieni di ogni ingiustizia, fornicazione, malvagità, cupidigia, malignità; pieni d'invidia, omicidio, contesa, frode, malizia; calunniatori, maldicenti, odiatori di Dio, insolenti, superbi, vanagloriosi, inventori di cose malvagie, disubbidienti ai genitori, senza intendimento, sleali, senza affetto naturale, implacabili, senza misericordia; i quali, pur conoscendo il giudizio di Dio, cioè che coloro che fanno tali cose sono degni di morte, non solo le compiono, ma approvano anche chi le compie» (Romani 1:18-32).

Allora come si può essere umanisti e credere in Dio? Qui tocchiamo qualcosa di più vicino a casa. Questo tipo di umanista crede che Dio voglia che egli sia felice. Crede in un Dio Creatore ma non crede di doverGli servire nella realtà. Non crede nel vero Dio, ma nella sua mente ha creato un dio fittizio che non esiste. Questo gli permette di vivere per se stesso e per la propria felicità. Questo tipo di persona parlerà di Dio, andrà in chiesa, canterà inni e dirà preghiere. Tuttavia, cercherà ogni sua necessità solo nell'uomo. Se è malato, chiama un dottore. Se ha bisogno di denaro, va dal banchiere. Se ha bisogno di una pausa dalla realtà, prende una vacanza o un ritiro. Vive la vita per la sua felicità e poi ringrazia Dio anche se non si è rivolto a Dio per i suoi bisogni. Queste persone dipendono da se stesse. Hanno fiducia in se stesse.

Ecco un esempio: un cristiano pianta un orto e se ne prende cura ogni giorno. Annaffia, concima, estirpa le erbacce e pota. Infine, le sue piante cominciano a dare frutto, frutti belli. Ringrazia Dio per il raccolto abbondante. Il suo vicino, un umanista ateo, ha anche lui piantato un orto. Anche lui usciva ogni giorno e annaffiava, potava, estirpava e concimava. Anche lui ha ricevuto un raccolto abbondante. Quest'uomo, tuttavia, si vantava di tutto ciò che aveva realizzato. Entrambi gli uomini hanno fatto le stesse cose e hanno ottenuto risultati simili. Uno ha dato il merito a Dio, e uno ha dato il merito a se stesso. Dirà di aver ottenuto senza Dio lo stesso risultato del suo vicino con Dio. I cristiani sanno che si sbaglia e che in realtà aveva bisogno di Dio per far crescere il suo orto.

Quando accade qualcosa che richiede intervento soprannaturale, l'umanista cristiano prega e chiede ad altri di pregare. Tuttavia, non crede che Dio risponderà alle loro preghiere e si mette subito al lavoro per risolvere il suo problema, usando solo il ragionamento umano. Poi, se il problema si risolve, ringrazia Dio per questo. Questo tipo di umanesimo ha confuso il mondo moderno. Ha portato gli increduli a deridere la fede cristiana e a chiamarla una religione falsa senza potere.

Il cristiano non crede nel ragionamento umano. Il cristiano crede che il Dio dei cieli sia la ragione di ogni cosa. «Perché in lui sono state create tutte le cose che sono nei cieli e sulla terra, visibili e invisibili, siano essi troni o dominazioni o principati o potestà; tutte le cose sono state create per mezzo di lui e per lui» (Colossesi 1:16). Noi non siamo nulla senza di Lui, e senza di Lui non possiamo fare nulla. Il cristianesimo è l'opposto dell'umanesimo. Quando il cristiano compie qualcosa di soprannaturale, qualcosa che l'umanista o l'ateo non possono fare, allora abbiamo qualcosa che confonderà i sapienti.

Quando il vicino vede il cristiano amare i suoi nemici, perdonare chi gli ha fatto torto e fare cose che lui non può fare, allora comincia a domandarsi da dove venga il potere di fare queste cose. Questo lo conduce al Padre. Quando non c'è nulla di soprannaturale in ciò che facciamo, rimane confuso.

E noi?

Temo che stiamo cadendo in questa trappola dell'«umanesimo cristiano». Parliamo bene; diciamo di credere in Dio. Andiamo in chiesa, cantiamo inni e preghiamo. Tuttavia, dall'apparenza esteriore, confidiamo in noi stessi. Poiché abbiamo centrato le nostre vite su noi stessi e sul nostro benessere, il Dio dei cieli non ci ascolta. Le nostre preghiere non vengono esaudite e il tempo sulle nostre ginocchia è una lotta, nella migliore delle ipotesi. Facciamo le cose per abitudine perché così ci è stato insegnato, ma la nostra fede risiede nel ragionamento umano.

Può essere estremamente difficile cercare il Signore vivendo in una società umanistica. Una società che ha perfezionato la ricerca della libertà e della felicità. Lentamente, la chiesa sta cedendo ai modi di questo mondo.

Un ministro dalla Cina stava visitando le chiese in America. Prima di ritornare in Cina, gli fu chiesto che cosa lo avesse impressionato maggiormente delle chiese americane. Rispose: «Sono stupito di ciò che hanno compiuto senza Dio».

Faremmo bene a semplificare la moderna definizione di umanesimo. L'umanista nega con orgoglio che esista un Dio quando si vanta della propria forza e abilità. Proclama i grandi risultati dell'uomo e deride il cristiano umile.

Il cristiano rinnega se stesso, prende la sua croce e segue il suo Maestro. Il cristiano non pensa nulla di se stesso o della capacità dell'uomo, ammettendo con fiducia che è solo polvere e che a quella polvere tornerà presto. Il cristiano cerca il bene negli altri e confida in Dio per tutti i suoi bisogni e le sue preoccupazioni quotidiane.

I cristiani credono di essere semplicemente servi del loro padrone. Sono odiati dal mondo e disprezzati dalla maggior parte, rifiutati. «Se il mondo vi odia, sappiate che ha odiato me prima di voi» (Giovanni 15:18). Per loro, questa vita non è la ricerca della felicità. Le cose di questo mondo non li interessano nemmeno. La loro gioia e pace vengono esclusivamente dal servire il loro padrone, dal compiacere il loro Padre celeste. Per il mondo, sono strani. Sciocchi. Per Dio, sono i suoi cari figli.

Dio sta ancora cercando persone oggi che pongano la loro fiducia in Lui. Sta guardando tutta la terra sperando di trovare qualcuno, da qualche parte, che metta da parte il ragionamento umano e il buon senso e obbedisca alla voce dal cielo. Dio vuole uomini con fede che facciano un passo nel soprannaturale, come Abramo, Mosè, Davide e le migliaia di credenti che seguirono. Qualcuno che rinneghi se stesso e questo mondo e segua il Salvatore.

Quando questa vita sarà finita, gli umanisti, che dicano o meno di credere in Dio, periranno. E i cristiani vivranno per sempre nella gloria.

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Tror du på mirakler? Tror du på det övernaturliga? Vad sägs om gudomligt ingripande? Eller en bättre fråga kanske är: har du sett Gud verka i ditt liv? Ser andra Gud verka i ditt liv?

Min bror arbetade i växthuset när en kund kom in och förundrades över skönheten hos alla växterna. Han utropade hur imponerad han var över allt vårt hårda arbete. Min bror svarade: ”En del planterar, en del vattnar, men Gud får det att växa.” Kunden svarade då: ”Nej, nej, ge inte äran åt Gud. Ni gick ut här och gjorde allt detta arbete. Ni planterade, vattnade och gödslade alla dessa plantor, och ni förtjänar äran, inte Gud!” Anledningen till att mannen kände så var att han var humanist.

Vad är humanism?

Ordboken definierar humanism så här: en syn eller ett tankesystem som fäster främsta vikt vid mänskliga snarare än gudomliga eller övernaturliga frågor. Humanistiska uppfattningar betonar människors potentiella värde och godhet, framhäver gemensamma mänskliga behov och söker endast rationella sätt att lösa mänskliga problem.

Om Gud finns måste vi erkänna detta faktum och svara inför Honom. Humanister försöker bevisa att Gud inte finns, så att de fritt kan leva sina liv som de behagar. Enligt humanismen finns ingen Gud. Om så är fallet är vi, människosläktet, överlägsna Gud. Allt är för oss och vår yttersta lycka. Detta är definitionen av humanism.

Två typer av humanism

Det finns två typer av humanistiska uppfattningar, och vi ska se på båda. Den första uppfattningen är teorin att det inte finns någon Gud. I verkligheten verkar detta vara det enda rationella sättet att vara humanist på. Allt är skapat av människan och för människan. Det finns inga andra faktorer eller övernaturligt ingripande. Allt händer genom förnuft och sunt förnuft. Det finns en logisk förklaring till allt som händer. Visst, vissa saker är obegripliga, men humanister bortser från dem och ser bara till det som kan förklaras. Som växterna i växthuset ser de allt som människan gör och ignorerar den övernaturliga delen av en växts uppvaknande till nytt liv. Forskare runt om i världen arbetar ihärdigt för att föra in mänskligt tänkande i allt som någonsin hänt, till och med världens skapelse. Forskare, med all sin kunskap och visdom, försöker ge logiska förklaringar till varför naturkatastrofer och globala kriser inträffar. Om de kan förklara allt kan de utesluta Gud och Hans existens. Detta tillåter människosläktet att göra som det behagar utan eviga konsekvenser. Detta leder i sin tur till en stor känsla av falsk frid.

Humanisterna, med allt sitt resonemang, förlöjligar själva Guds existens. Om du går till de flesta högskolor i Amerika och pratar med folk om kristendomen skrattar de åt dig och hånar det faktum att kristna faktiskt tror på Gud.

Den andra typen av humanistisk uppfattning är en teori om humanism som erkänner Guds existens. En antropolog hävdade att humanism är ett modernitetsprojekt och en sekulariserad fortsättning på västerländsk kristen teologi. Men om du frågar folk vad de tycker att humanism betyder kommer du sannolikt att få olika svar, och det blir mycket förvirrande. Men varför förvirringen? För att människor försöker vara kristna humanister. Kristen humanism har ofta kritiserats för sin vaghet och svårighet att definieras. Anledningen till att det blivit så förvirrande är att människor vill tro på Gud men också tro på sig själva och att världen kretsar kring dem.

I Romarbrevet läser vi: ”Ty Guds vrede uppenbaras från himlen över all gudlöshet och orättfärdighet hos människor som håller sanningen fången i orättfärdighet. Det som kan kännas om Gud är uppenbart bland dem, för Gud har uppenbarat det för dem. Ända sedan världens skapelse har hans osynliga egenskaper, hans eviga makt och gudomlighet, kunnat uppfattas genom hans verk och är tydligt synliga. Därför är de utan ursäkt. De kände Gud men ärade honom inte som Gud och tackade honom inte heller. I stället blev deras tankar tomma och deras oförståndiga hjärtan förmörkades. De påstod sig vara visa men blev dårar, och bytte ut den oförgänglige Gudens härlighet mot bilder som liknade förgängliga människor, fåglar, fyrfotadjur och kräldjur. Därför utlämnade Gud dem åt orenhet, åt deras hjärtans begär, så att de vanärade sina kroppar med varandra. De bytte ut Guds sanning mot lögnen och dyrkade och tjänade det skapade i stället för Skaparen, som är välsignad i evighet. Amen. Därför utlämnade Gud dem åt skamliga begär. Deras kvinnor bytte ut det naturliga umgänget mot det som är onaturligt. På samma sätt övergav männen det naturliga umgänget med kvinnan och upptändes av begär till varandra. Män gjorde skamliga saker med män och fick själva ta emot den lön för sin villfarelse som de förtjänade. Eftersom de inte ansåg det värt att behålla kunskapen om Gud, utlämnade Gud dem åt ett förkastligt sinnelag, så att de gjorde sådant som inte borde göras. De blev uppfyllda av all slags orättfärdighet, ondska, girighet och elakhet, fulla av avund, mordlust, stridslystnad, svek och illvilja. De skvallrar, baktalar, hatar Gud, är fräcka, högmodiga och skrytsamma. De hittar på onda saker, är olydiga mot sina föräldrar, oförståndiga, trolösa, utan naturlig kärlek, obevekliga och utan barmhärtighet. De känner till Guds rättvisa dom: att de som handlar så förtjänar döden. Ändå gör de inte bara sådant själva, utan de berömmer också andra som gör det.” (Romarbrevet 1:18-32)

Så hur kan man vara humanist och tro på Gud? Här kommer vi lite närmare vår egen verklighet. Denna typ av humanist tror att Gud vill att han ska vara lycklig. Han tror på en skapande Gud men tror inte att han i verkligheten måste tjäna Honom. I verkligheten tror han inte på den sanna Guden utan i sitt sinne har han skapat en fiktiv gud som inte existerar. Detta tillåter honom att leva för sig själv och sin egen lycka. Denna typ av person pratar om Gud, går till kyrkan, sjunger sånger och ber böner. Han vänder sig dock endast till människan för alla sina behov. Är han sjuk ringer han en läkare. Behöver han pengar går han till bankiren. Om behovet är en paus från verkligheten tar han en semester eller reträtt. Han lever för sin egen lycka och tackar sedan Gud fastän han inte vände sig till Gud för sina behov. Dessa människor är beroende av sig själva. De har förtroende för sig själva.

Här är ett exempel: En kristen planterar en trädgård och tar hand om den varje dag. Han vattnar och gödslar, rensar ogräs och beskär. Slutligen börjar hans växter bära frukt, fin frukt. Han tackar Gud för den rikliga skörden. Hans granne, en ateistisk humanist, planterade också en trädgård. Han gick också ut varje dag och vattnade, beskärde, rensade ogräs och gödslade. Han fick också en riklig skörd. Denne man skryter dock om allt han åstadkommit. Båda männen gjorde samma saker och fick liknande resultat. Den ene gav Gud äran, den andre berömde sig själv. Han kommer att säga att han uppnådde samma sak utan Gud som hans granne gjorde med Gud. Kristna vet att han har fel och att han faktiskt behövde Gud för att få sin trädgård att växa.

När något händer som kräver övernaturligt ingripande ber den kristna humanisten och ber andra att be. Han tror dock inte att Gud kommer att svara på deras böner och sätter genast igång för att lösa sitt problem med endast mänskligt resonemang. Sedan, om problemet blir löst, tackar han Gud för det. Denna typ av humanism har förvirrat den moderna världen. Den har fått otroende att håna den kristna tron och kalla den en falsk religion utan kraft.

Den kristne tror inte på mänskligt resonemang. Den kristne tror att himlens Gud är orsaken till allt. ”Ty genom honom skapades allt i himlen och på jorden, det synliga och det osynliga, tronfurstar och herrar, härskare och makter. Allt är skapat genom honom och till honom.” (Kolosserbrevet 1:16) Vi är ingenting utan Honom, och utan Honom kan vi ingenting göra. Kristendomen är motsatsen till humanism. När den kristne gör något övernaturligt, något som humanisten eller ateisten inte kan göra, då har vi något som förvirrar de vise.

När grannen ser den kristne älska sina fiender, förlåta någon som gjort fel mot honom och göra saker som han inte kan göra, börjar han undra var kraften att göra dessa saker kom ifrån. Detta leder honom då till Fadern. När det inte finns något övernaturligt vi gör blir han förvirrad.

Vad sägs om oss?

Jag fruktar att vi faller i denna fälla av ”kristen humanism”. Vi talar väl; vi säger att vi tror på Gud. Vi går till kyrkan, sjunger sånger och ber böner. Men utåt sett litar vi på oss själva. Eftersom vi har centrerat våra liv kring oss själva och vårt välbefinnande hör himlens Gud oss inte. Våra böner besvaras inte, och tiden på knä är i bästa fall en kamp. Vi går igenom ritualerna eftersom det är så vi blivit undervisade, men vår tro vilar i mänskligt resonemang.

Det kan vara oerhört svårt att söka Herren medan man lever i ett humanistiskt samhälle. Ett samhälle som fulländat jakten på frihet och lycka. Sakta men säkert viker kyrkan för denna världens sätt.

En predikant från Kina besökte kyrkorna i Amerika. Innan han återvände till Kina blev han frågad vad som imponerade mest på honom med kyrkorna i Amerika. Han svarade: ”Jag är förundrad över vad de alla har åstadkommit utan Gud.”

Vi skulle göra väl i att förenkla den moderna definitionen av humanism. Humanisten förnekar stolt att det finns en Gud när han skryter om sin egen styrka och förmåga. Han proklamerar människans stora bedrifter och förlöjligar den ödmjuka kristne.

Den kristne förnekar sig själv, tar upp sitt kors och följer sin Mästare. Den kristne tänker intet om sig själv eller människans förmåga, och erkänner tryggt att han blott är stoft och snart ska återgå till det stoftet. Den kristne ser det goda i andra och litar på Gud för alla sina dagliga behov och bekymmer.

Kristna anser sig blott vara tjänare åt sin Herre. De blir hatade av världen och föraktade av de flesta, avvisade. ”Om världen hatar er ska ni veta att den har hatat mig innan den hatade er.” (Johannes 15:18) För dem är detta liv inte jakten på lycka. Världens ting intresserar dem inte ens. Deras glädje och frid kommer enbart från att tjäna sin Herre, från att behaga sin himmelske Fader. För världen är de främmande. Dårar. För Gud är de Hans kära barn.

Gud söker fortfarande människor idag som vill sätta sitt förtroende till Honom. Han söker över hela jorden efter någon, någonstans, som vill lägga åt sidan mänskligt resonemang och sunt förnuft och lyda rösten från himlen. Gud vill ha människor med tro som vågar träda in i det övernaturliga, som Abraham, Mose, David och de tusentals troende som följde. Någon som vill förneka sig själv och denna värld och följa Frälsaren.

När detta livet är över ska humanisterna, vare sig de säger att de tror på Gud eller inte, gå under. Och de kristna ska gå vidare för att leva för evigt i härlighet.

Humanist? Kristen? Kristen humanist? Vilken är du?

Arise be glad! For dawn is here!
Rejoice and sing! The night is past,
The Dayspring shineth from on high,
The grace of God to man is nigh!
Rejoice and praise the King of Kings!
Give thanks and laud, for more is here!

Arise and glorify the Lord!
Extol and praise His worthy name!
He shineth from the heav’ns in love,
And showers blessings from above,
His mercy reaches down to men-
Adore and praise our mighty Lord!

Give thanks and sing to Christ our King
And worship Him with reverent praise;
Bow down in awful, holy fear-
The Holiness of God is here;
In wondrous beauty bend the knee;
Adore th’ almighty King of Kings!

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“डॉ. वॉल्ड्रन, एल्सी को मदद चाहिए!” एल्सी का पति दृढ़ था, लगभग क्रोधित, और मेरी ओर घूर रहा था। दूसरी ओर, एल्सी फर्श की ओर देख रही थी, मानो वह वहाँ मौजूद ही न हो। मैं उन दोनों से पहले कभी नहीं मिला था और थोड़ा-सा यह समझने की कोशिश कर रहा था कि उसकी मदद के लिए मुझसे क्या अपेक्षित था।

“क्या हो रहा है?” मैंने उसका चार्ट पलटते हुए पूछा। यह कागज़ी चार्टों का ज़माना था, और मैं उसके चार्ट के प्रयोगशाला वाले हिस्से पर पहुँचा। वहाँ मुझे कुछ भी बहुत असामान्य नहीं दिखा—उसके लिवर एंज़ाइम थोड़े बढ़े हुए थे, लेकिन बाकी सब ठीक लग रहा था।

“उसका शराब पीना!” उसके पति ने मुझे बताया। “वह हर रात और ज़्यादा पीती जा रही है। व्हिस्की लेने के अलावा वह कहीं नहीं जाती। वह हर रात तब तक पीती है जब तक बेहोश न हो जाए, और सुबह उठने के लिए उसे हर दिन कुछ न कुछ पीना पड़ता है।”

“क्या यह सच है?” मैंने एल्सी से पूछा। मुझे ऐसा लग रहा था मानो मैं जूरी के मुकदमे की अध्यक्षता कर रहा कोई न्यायाधीश हूँ।

“हाँ,” उसने कहा। उसका चेहरा भावहीन था, और मैं नहीं बता सकता था कि वह वहाँ आना चाहती थी या नहीं।

“क्या तुम मदद चाहती हो?” मैंने उससे पूछा। यह एक ऐसा सवाल था जिसमें बहुत कुछ निहित था। शराब की लत से जूझ रहे बहुत-से लोग उसकी शिकंजे जैसी पकड़ से मुक्त होने के लिए तैयार नहीं होते। शायद एल्सी अलग हो।

“मुझे लगता है,” उसने उदासीनता से कहा। एक बार फिर, मैं नहीं बता सका कि वह वहाँ आना चाहती थी या नहीं।

“जिस रफ़्तार से तुम पी रही हो, अगर तुमने शराब पूरी तरह नहीं छोड़ी, तो एक साल के भीतर—ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा शायद दो साल में—तुम अपनी जान ले बैठोगी,” मैंने उससे कहा। “अगर तुम चाहो, तो मैं तुम्हारे लिए अस्पताल में भर्ती करके इलाज करने वाला कोई कार्यक्रम ढूँढ़ने की कोशिश करूँगा, ताकि तुम्हें नशे से मुक्त किया जा सके और शराब छुड़ाई जा सके।”

“वह तैयार है,” उसके पति ने दृढ़ता से कहा।

जब कोई बहुत ज़्यादा शराब पीता हो, तो यह बेहद ज़रूरी है कि वह चिकित्सकीय सहायता के बिना अचानक शराब पीना बंद न करे। शराब का अचानक सेवन बंद करने से शरीर में विदड्रॉल हो सकता है, जिससे डिलीरियम ट्रेमेन्स नाम की स्थिति और यहाँ तक कि दौरे भी पड़ सकते हैं।

मैं जाँच-कक्ष से बाहर निकला और फ़ोन करने लगा। किसी भी तरह के नशीले पदार्थों के इस्तेमाल से उबरने के लिए किसी के वास्ते जगह ढूँढ़ना कभी आसान नहीं होता, और डेढ़ घंटे से भी ज़्यादा समय बाद मुझे एक ऐसी सुविधा मिली जो एल्सी को भर्ती करने और उसे व्हिस्की छुड़ाने में मदद करने के लिए तैयार थी।

जाँच-कक्ष में वापस लौटते हुए मैंने राहत की साँस ली। मुझे डर था कि उसके लिए जाने की कोई जगह नहीं मिलेगी।

मैंने उन्हें योजना बताई, और उसके पति ने ज़ोर से सिर हिलाकर हामी भरी, जबकि एल्सी चुपचाप फर्श को देखती रही। “जाने से पहले क्या हम साथ में प्रार्थना कर सकते हैं?” मैंने उनसे पूछा। जब उन्होंने सहमति में सिर हिलाया, तो मैंने उनके साथ प्रार्थना की और उन दोनों के जीवन में स्वतंत्रता और यीशु की उपस्थिति के लिए विनती की।

वे मेरे दफ़्तर से स्पष्ट निर्देशों और जाने की जगह के पते के साथ चले गए। बाकी सुबह मैं प्रसन्नता से भरा रहा, यह जानते हुए कि मैंने अतिरिक्त प्रयास किया था और इस अधेड़ उम्र के दंपति के जीवन में सचमुच बदलाव लाया था।

दोपहर लगभग 2 बजे मुझे पुनर्वास केंद्र से फ़ोन आया। वहाँ किसी ने एल्सी या उसके पति की परछाईं तक नहीं देखी थी। यह आश्चर्य की बात थी, क्योंकि दिन धूप से भरा था और केंद्र भी बहुत दूर नहीं था। मन में बुरा-सा एहसास लिए मैंने उस दंपति का फ़ोन नंबर मिलाया।

“वह नहीं जाएगी!” उसके पति ने मुझे बताया। “वह कहती है कि उसने मुझे पहले ही बता दिया था। वह शराब कम करने की कोशिश करेगी, लेकिन किसी पुनर्वास केंद्र या ऐसी किसी जगह जाने को तैयार नहीं है। मुझे लगता है, बस उन्हें बता दो कि अगर उसका मन बदला तो हम उन्हें बता देंगे।”

मेरी नर्स ने पुनर्वास केंद्र को बुरी खबर बता दी, और मैं स्तब्ध होकर अपनी कुर्सी पर बैठ गया। मैं और क्या कर सकता था? क्या एल्सी के लिए कोई समाधान था—क्या कुछ अलग कहा जा सकता था, जिससे उसके जीवन में बदलाव आता?

लगभग एक साल बाद मुझे दुखद खबर मिली कि एल्सी की घर पर मृत्यु हो गई थी। मुझे यक़ीन था कि अगर वह पुनर्वास के लिए चली गई होती और उसने अपना नियंत्रण यीशु को सौंप दिया होता, तो हालात अलग होते। इनमें से कुछ भी नहीं हुआ था, और मुझे महसूस हुआ कि मेरे दिल में निंदकता घर कर रही है।

निंदकता

हम निंदकता के युग में जी रहे हैं। प्राचीन यूनान में निंदक दार्शनिकों का एक विचित्र समूह था, जो चिड़चिड़े रहने और लोगों से कटु (वे इसे सच कहते) बातें कहने में माहिर था। वे अक्सर फटे-पुराने कपड़े पहनते और ऐसा व्यवहार करते कि अधिकांश शिष्ट एथेनियाई उनसे दूर रहना चाहते थे।

आज निंदकता का अर्थ है लोगों और परिस्थितियों के बारे में सबसे बुरा मानने की प्रवृत्ति। निंदक लोग मानते हैं कि सभी लोग केवल स्वार्थ से प्रेरित होते हैं और बुरी घटनाओं के ही हावी होने की संभावना रहती है।

कई युवा डॉक्टर आदर्शवादी और बहुत आशावान होते हैं। वे मानते हैं कि यदि वे पूरी कोशिश करें, तो अपने मरीज़ों के जीवन पर वास्तविक और सकारात्मक प्रभाव डाल सकते हैं। दुर्भाग्य से, समय बीतने पर, जब वे अपनी पूरी कोशिश करते हैं और उनके मरीज़ नहीं बदलते, तो वे हार मान सकते हैं। ये डॉक्टर अब भी प्रयास करते हैं, लेकिन उन्हें अब सचमुच यह आशा नहीं रहती कि उनके प्रयासों से कोई बड़ा बदलाव आएगा।

ऐसा लगता है कि राजनीति में शामिल होने वाले लोग अक्सर नेक इरादों से आते हैं। वे इसे समाज को बेहतर बनाने का रास्ता मानते हैं। दुर्भाग्य से, समय बीतने पर और सत्ता में बैठे लोगों के चेहरे बदलने के बावजूद नीतियाँ वास्तव में नहीं बदलतीं, तो वे निंदक हो जाते हैं।

कभी-कभी यह निंदकता सभी राजनेताओं के विरुद्ध होती है। कभी-कभी यह केवल उन दलों के सदस्यों के प्रति क्रोध होता है जो उनके दल की नीतियों का विरोध करते हैं। आशा की जगह निंदकता ले लेती है।

बाइबल में निंदकता

यदि बाइबल में कोई ऐसी पुस्तक है जो किसी निंदक व्यक्ति द्वारा लिखी हुई लगती है, तो वह सभोपदेशक की पुस्तक है। उपदेशक, जिसे हम सुलैमान मानते हैं, उन सभी चीज़ों की सूची देता है जिनमें उसने आनंद पाने की कोशिश की।

अध्याय 2:17-23 में सुलैमान काम को व्यर्थ बताता है। वह यह कहते हुए अपनी बात समाप्त करता है, “मनुष्य को उसके सारे परिश्रम और मन के क्लेश से, जिसके लिए वह सूर्य के नीचे परिश्रम करता है, क्या मिलता है? उसके सारे दिन दुख से भरे हैं, और उसका काम शोक का कारण है; हाँ, रात में भी उसके मन को चैन नहीं मिलता। यह भी व्यर्थ है।” (सभोपदेशक 2:22,23)

उसने संसार को अत्याचारियों के प्रभुत्व में देखा, और लोगों के पास इसके बारे में करने को बहुत कम था। सुलैमान ने यहाँ तक कहा कि राजनीतिक सत्ता अर्थहीन है: “उस बूढ़े और मूर्ख राजा से, जो अब किसी की सलाह नहीं मानता, एक निर्धन और बुद्धिमान बालक बेहतर है। क्योंकि वह बंदीगृह से निकलकर राजा बनता है, जबकि अपने राज्य में जन्मा हुआ व्यक्ति निर्धन हो जाता है।” (सभोपदेशक 4:13)

सभोपदेशक 6:6 में वह लंबी उम्र को तुच्छ मानता हुआ लगता है। “हाँ, चाहे वह दो बार हज़ार वर्ष तक जीवित रहे, फिर भी उसने कोई भलाई नहीं देखी; क्या सभी को एक ही स्थान पर नहीं जाना है?”

बेशक, वह अपनी छोटी-सी पुस्तक का समापन इस निर्देश के साथ करता है कि हम अपनी जवानी के दिनों में अपने सृष्टिकर्ता को स्मरण रखें। जिन लोगों में अभी थोड़ी ऊर्जा बाकी है, उनके लिए परमेश्वर पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना आशीष का कारण है—ऐसा नहीं कि वे सुलैमान की तरह बूढ़े और निराश हो जाने पर ही ऐसा करें।

बाद में, ऐसा लगने लगा मानो परमेश्वर ने अपने लोगों से आशा छोड़ दी हो। उसने फिर भी उनके पास भविष्यद्वक्ता भेजे, लेकिन वह निःसंदेह जानता था कि लोग कोई उत्तर नहीं देंगे। “इसलिए तू ये सारी बातें उनसे कहना; परन्तु वे तेरी न सुनेंगे। तू उन्हें पुकारेगा भी, पर वे तुझे उत्तर न देंगे।” (यिर्मयाह 7:27)

नए नियम में भी पौलुस ने तीमुथियुस से कहा कि ऐसा समय आने वाला है जब लोग शुद्ध शिक्षा को सहन नहीं करेंगे। “क्योंकि ऐसा समय आएगा जब वे शुद्ध शिक्षा को सहन नहीं करेंगे; बल्कि अपनी अभिलाषाओं के अनुसार अपने लिए बहुत-से शिक्षक इकट्ठे करेंगे, क्योंकि उनके कानों में खुजली होती है।” (2 तीमुथियुस 4:3)

इन अंशों में से चुनकर पढ़ने पर हम भविष्य के बारे में और ख़ास तौर पर इंसानों की बदलने की इच्छा के बारे में बहुत निराशाजनक दृष्टिकोण अपना सकते हैं। ऐसा लगता है कि अपने आस-पास के लोगों में अपना समय और प्रयास लगाने का कोई ख़ास मतलब नहीं है। वे दुःखों से भरे हैं और उनके बदलने की संभावना उतनी ही है जितनी किसी चिपमंक के अवकल कलन में निपुण होने की।

निंदकता का विपरीत

निंदकता का विपरीत आशा है। यह विश्वास है कि भविष्य बेहतर हो सकता है।

यह दिलचस्प है कि प्रेरित पौलुस ने रोमियों के नाम पत्री में क्लेशों के बारे में लिखा: “और केवल यही नहीं, बल्कि हम क्लेशों में भी घमण्ड करते हैं, यह जानकर कि क्लेश से धीरज उत्पन्न होता है, और धीरज से खरा निकलना, और खरे निकलने से आशा उत्पन्न होती है; और आशा से लज्जा नहीं होती, क्योंकि पवित्र आत्मा जो हमें दिया गया है, उसके द्वारा परमेश्वर का प्रेम हमारे हृदयों में उंडेला गया है।” (रोमियों 5:3-5)

हो सकता है कि हम उस मुकाम पर न पहुँचे हों जहाँ हम अपने अनुभव किए हुए क्लेशों में घमण्ड करें, लेकिन निश्चय ही उनसे वे अन्य बातें उत्पन्न होनी चाहिए जिनका पौलुस ज़िक्र करता है। क्योंकि परीक्षाओं का सामना करते हुए हम धीरज और अनुभव में बढ़ते हैं, और इससे भी बढ़कर, हमें एहसास होता है कि हमारे पास आने वाले कल के लिए आशा है, क्योंकि हम एक महान परमेश्वर की सेवा करते हैं।

लूका 15 में उधाऊ पुत्र की कहानी का विरोधाभास हमें आशा के बारे में बहुत कुछ सिखाता है। पिता और बड़े भाई के रवैये में ज़मीन-आसमान का अंतर था।

पिता ने कभी आशा नहीं छोड़ी—वह जानता था कि उसके बेटे ने उसे निराश किया था और उस सही मार्ग से बहुत दूर चला गया था जिसे वह जानता था, फिर भी पिता चाहता था कि उधाऊ पुत्र अपनी सुध-बुध में आए और घर लौटे।

दूसरी ओर, बड़े भाई को अपने छोटे भाई से कोई आशा तो थी ही नहीं, वह उससे नाराज़ भी था। उधाऊ पुत्र ने अपना धन बरबाद किया था, पाप में जीवन बिताया था, और अब केवल इसलिए घर लौटा था क्योंकि उसके पास पैसे ख़त्म हो गए थे।

निश्चय ही, छोटे बेटे पर भरोसा करने का कोई कारण नहीं था। फिर भी, हमारा स्वर्गीय पिता हमारे लिए ठीक यही करता है।

सही जगहों पर आशा खोजें

समस्या का एक हिस्सा यह है कि हम गलत जगहों पर आशा खोजते हैं। कई साल पहले, राष्ट्रपति पद के एक उम्मीदवार ने “आशा और बदलाव” के नारे के साथ चुनाव लड़ा था, लेकिन चुने जाने के बावजूद, मेरा अनुमान है कि अधिकतर लोगों को यह महसूस नहीं हुआ कि उनके जीवन में कोई उल्लेखनीय सुधार हुआ है।

इस संसार की मूल्यवान मानी जाने वाली चीज़ों—राजनीतिक सत्ता और धन—के पीछे भागने से खालीपन मिलना तय है। यह शैतान का तरीक़ा है—वह हमेशा वादे बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर करता है और देता कम है।

यीशु को प्रलोभित करते समय उसने यही किया था: “यदि तू गिरकर मुझे प्रणाम करे, तो मैं ये सब कुछ तुझे दे दूँगा।” (मत्ती 4:8) शैतान ने जो कुछ भी देने की पेशकश की, वह उस महिमा की तुलना में कुछ भी नहीं था जो अंततः क्रूस की राह से चलकर यीशु को मिली।

इसी तरह, शैतान मसीहियों को उन मूल्यवान चीज़ों की खोज से भटकाना चाहता है जो आशा लाएँगी। शैतान मसीहियों से कहता है कि राजनीति न केवल संसार को बेहतर बनाएगी, बल्कि यह संसार को बदलने का आसान रास्ता भी है।

बाइबल स्पष्ट कहती है कि परमेश्वर के साथ अपने संबंध को बढ़ावा देने और फिर अपने भाई-बहनों की मदद करके उनके जीवन में भी वही संबंध बनाने से हम आशा पाते हैं। हम आशा इसलिए नहीं कर सकते कि लोग इतने अद्भुत हैं—हमें यह समझने के लिए ज़्यादा समय तक जीने की ज़रूरत नहीं कि वे ऐसे नहीं हैं। हम इसलिए आशा करते हैं क्योंकि हम एक महान और विश्वासयोग्य परमेश्वर की सेवा करते हैं, जो हमारी सबसे कठिन परीक्षाओं में भी हमारे साथ चलता है।

याद रखें कि हमारी आशा अनर्जित है

क्षमा के बारे में यीशु की शिक्षाएँ स्पष्ट करती हैं कि अपने जीवन में दूसरों को क्षमा करने का एक प्रमुख कारण यह है कि हमें स्वयं महान और अनर्जित क्षमा मिली है। आशा के बारे में भी यही सच है।

हममें से हर एक आशाहीन था और उसके पास आशा पाने की उम्मीद करने का कोई कारण नहीं था, फिर भी हमारे अंधकार के बीच हमें प्रकाश की एक किरण दी गई। शायद हमारे लिए अपने आस-पास के लोगों के लिए अच्छी बातों की आशा करना इतना कठिन होने का एक कारण यह है कि हम यह याद नहीं रखते कि अनुग्रह पाने से पहले हम कितने आशाहीन थे।

यदि यीशु हमारी आशाहीन अवस्था में आशा ला सकता था, तो निश्चय ही वह हमारे आस-पास के दूसरे लोगों के हृदयों और जीवनों में अद्भुत कार्य कर सकता है। हमें केवल उन्हीं लोगों से आशा छोड़नी चाहिए जिनसे हमारे उद्धारकर्ता ने भी आशा छोड़ दी है।

छोटे प्रयास सचमुच बदलाव लाते हैं

मुझे एक ऐसे युवा के साथ हुई बातचीत याद है जो चिकित्सा के क्षेत्र में जाने की योजना बना रहा था और विदेश जाकर वहाँ के लोगों की सेवा करना चाहता था। हमारी बातचीत के दौरान एक उम्रदराज़ व्यक्ति भी शामिल हुआ और उसने कहा कि उसे विकासशील देशों में बदलाव की बहुत कम आशा दिखाई देती है।

उन देशों के लोग बस बेहतर होने में दिलचस्पी नहीं रखते थे और कीड़े तथा परजीवी जैसी चीज़ों से बचने के लिए ज़रूरी न्यूनतम कदम भी नहीं उठाते थे। ऐसे माहौल में डॉक्टर और नर्सें कोई बदलाव नहीं ला सकते थे।

जब उस उम्रदराज़ व्यक्ति ने अपनी बात कही, तो मैं उस युवा का मन टूटता हुआ महसूस कर सकता था। उसके पास अनुभव था, और उसने आशा छोड़ दी थी। दुख की बात यह थी कि वह ऐसे व्यक्ति की आशा भी छीन रहा था जो अब भी सेवा करना चाहता था।

जब मैं प्रशिक्षण ले रहा था, तो एक सर्जन ने मुझसे कहा कि पारिवारिक डॉक्टर वास्तव में कुछ नहीं करते। वे बस अपने मरीज़ों को अगली मुलाक़ात तक जीवित रखते हैं, जबकि सर्जन सचमुच लोगों को “ठीक” करते हैं—समस्या पैदा करने वाले अंग को निकालकर।

आख़िरकार, छोटे प्रयास सचमुच बदलाव लाते हैं। मैं मस्तिष्क की सर्जरी नहीं करता, लेकिन फिर भी किसी और के जीवन में बदलाव ला सकता हूँ—शायद बस थोड़ा समय देकर, सुनकर और प्रार्थना करके। यह बात हम सब पर लागू होती है।

इससे भी बढ़कर, हमें एहसास होता है कि यह प्रयास करना हमारे अपने जीवन को बेहतर बनाता है। यीशु ने भेड़ों से कहा कि जब वे “मेरे इन भाइयों में से सबसे छोटे” की सेवा कर रहे थे, तब वे उसकी सेवा कर रहे थे।

भले ही किसी का जीवन बेहतर न हो, हमारा उद्धारकर्ता हमारी इच्छाओं को जानता है और हमारे प्रयासों को महसूस करता है, और एक दिन उन्हें प्रतिफल देगा।

याद रखने योग्य कुछ बातें

जब हम असफलताओं का सामना करते हैं, तो हम आम तौर पर दो में से किसी एक दिशा में जाते हैं। हममें से जो आशावादी हैं, वे मानते हैं कि यह घटना अपवाद थी और भविष्य अब भी उज्ज्वल है। दूसरी ओर, निराशावादी मानते हैं कि असफलताएँ स्थायी, व्यक्तिगत और सर्वव्यापी होती हैं।

निराशावादी मानते हैं कि उनकी असफलताएँ उनके स्वभाव में मौजूद चरित्र-दोषों का नतीजा हैं, कि ये बातें उनके पूरे जीवन को प्रभावित करती हैं और इनके बदलने की संभावना कम है। उस धर्मी व्यक्ति से अलग, जो गिरकर फिर उठता है, ये लोग गिरते हैं और जहाँ गिरे होते हैं वहीं पड़े रहते हैं—शुरुआत से ही पराजित।

दूसरे लोगों के साथ व्यवहार करते समय हमें उन्हें वही अनुग्रह देना चाहिए जो हमें स्वयं को देना चाहिए। वे भी बढ़ रहे हैं, और अगर आज उनसे चूक हुई है, तो वे कल बेहतर करेंगे। शायद उनसे फिर चूक हो, लेकिन कम-से-कम वे “पहले से बेहतर ढंग से असफल” होंगे।

निष्कर्ष

हमारे संसार में निंदकता व्यापक है। बहुत-से लोगों ने बेहतर भविष्य की आशा छोड़ दी है, और उन लोगों के लिए यह बात समझ में आती है जिन्होंने अपनी आशा इस संसार की संस्थाओं पर लगाई थी। सरकार, सेनाओं या नौकरशाही में कोई वास्तविक आशा नहीं है।

गीत कहता है, “यीशु में आशा न हो तो यह संसार कितना अँधकारमय होगा!” क्योंकि यीशु ही है जो हमारे अंधकार में प्रकाश लाता है और हमें आगे बढ़ते रहने देता है, तब भी जब दूसरे हमें निराश करते हैं।

परमेश्वर ही है जो हमारा उद्धार करता है। उसी ने भविष्यद्वक्ताओं को भेजा, हालाँकि उनके संदेशों को अनसुना किया गया और भविष्यद्वक्ताओं को सताया गया। वही हमारे लिए आशा करता रहता है, तब भी जब हमने अतीत में उसे बहुत बार निराश किया है।

वही कारण है कि हम आगे बढ़ते रहते हैं। वही कारण है कि हमारे पास आशा है—न केवल अपने लिए, बल्कि अपने भाइयों के लिए भी।
