Jamin mwenye umri wa miaka minane hakuwa mwerevu sana. Au angalau hivyo ndivyo kaka yake alivyomwambia. Karibu kila siku, kaka yake Kenny alipata njia za kumkumbusha Jamin mapungufu yake na kucheka makosa yake.

“Jamin, hutakuwa mwerevu kamwe,” Kenny alisema. Moyoni mwake, Jamin alihisi amekubali kwamba maisha yake yangekuwa ya kuchanganyikiwa na kufanya makosa. Je, angeendelea kuwa mtu asiye na ustadi daima? Je, angeendelea kusema mambo vibaya daima? Hivyo ndivyo Kenny alivyosema.

Jamin aliamini mahubiri ya Kenny kwa imani isiyo na shaka. Kenny alikuwa mkubwa kuliko yeye kwa miaka mitatu, kwa hiyo lazima alikuwa sahihi. Basi, sawa, Jamin angekuwa mtu asiye na akili nyingi. Kenny angekuwa mwerevu. Maisha hayakuwa ya haki. Baba na Mama hawakupenda maneno ya majivuno ya Kenny na walimwadhibu kila walipomkuta akitoa mojawapo ya hotuba zake. Lakini Kenny alikuwa na namna ya kusema bila wao kusikia. Kwa hiyo aliendelea kumdhihaki Jamin.

Bibi Otto alitazama majaribu haya akiwa kwenye kiti chake cha kubembea barazani. Alikuwa mwanamke mzee mtulivu.

“Jamin, unajua Kenny yuko wapi?” Mama aliuliza huku akitabasamu. “Karibu ni wakati wa chakula cha jioni.”

“Ameenda kukagua mitego yake ya koyoti. Nitaenda kumtafuta.”

Hewa ilikuwa na ubaridi alipokuwa akivuka kwa hatua nzito eneo la nyasi za uani, na jua lilikuwa likichoka alipovuka mpaka wa msitu. Vivuli vya muda mfupi vilikimbia juu ya vilima. Ubaridi ulizidi alipoingia ndani zaidi kwa hatua nzito. Alivuta hewa yenye harufu nzito na kufuata njia ya Kenny. Hatimaye, njia hiyo ingefika kwenye uwanda wa nyasi, lakini Jamin alitumaini angempata Kenny kabla hajalazimika kwenda mbali kiasi hicho. Mitego mbalimbali ilikuwa tayari imekaguliwa, kwa hiyo Jamin alijua Kenny alikuwa amepitia huko. Jamin aliendelea kutembea kwa hatua nzito, akiwa na azimio thabiti. Nywele zake za rangi ya dhahabu zilipokea miale hafifu iliyotoka kwenye jua na kupenya katikati ya miti. Na punde miale hiyo nayo ikafifia, ikiacha harufu nzito ya msitu. Viwavi wanaosuka utando wakati wa vuli walikuwa wamefanya kazi yao, na mapazia yao ya utando yalining’inia kama vifuniko kwenye matawi yaliyokuwa juu yake.

Hatimaye, miti ilipopungua na kutawanyika, na uwanda wa nyasi ukaonekana, Jamin alijua hapa ndipo njia ya mitego ya kaka yake ilipoishia. Ikiwa Kenny hakuwa hapa, asingejua mahali pengine pa kumtafuta.

Lakini Kenny alikuwa hapo. Jamin alipoingia kwenye uwanda kwa hatua nzito, aliweza kuona mtu aliyejikunyata kwa kufadhaika upande wake wa kulia. Sauti ya huyo aliyejikunyata ilikuwa ya kufahamika. Uso wake ulionyesha maumivu. Huyo aliyejikunyata alikuwa Kenny. “Uko salama? Kumetokea nini?” Jamin alihisi jambo lisilo la kawaida alipomwona Kenny amejikunyata chini kwenye udongo. Kenny alikuwa mwerevu. “Ulikanyaga mtego?”

“Ndiyo, Jamin. Mi..mimi sikuwa nikiangalia nilikokuwa nikienda. Nisaidie. Tafadhali.”

Jamin aliinama na kuona kifundo cha mguu kimeshikwa kwa nguvu na taya za mtego wa chuma. Giza lilitanda juu ya ardhi iliyomzunguka Kenny. Kwa haraka, Jamin alitumia mikono yake yenye nguvu kufungua taya hizo. Kenny aliyumba alipojinasua. “Unaweza kutembea?”

“Ndiyo. Nafikiri naweza. Ukinishikilia, naweza kwenda nikichechemea.”

“Baba na Mama watakuwa na wasiwasi. Tumekosa chakula cha jioni.”

Kwa kweli, ndugu hao walipokuwa wakirudi kupitia msituni kwa kuchechemea, walimsikia baba yao akiita kwa sauti ndefu. Jamin aliitikia, na baada ya muda mfupi baba alikuwa pembeni yao; alikiona kifundo cha mguu na kumwinua Kenny kama kondoo aliyejeruhiwa. Kikundi hicho kidogo kisicho cha kawaida kiliharakisha kurudi nyumbani, na mlango wa wavu ukafungwa kwa kishindo Baba alipokuwa akivuka baraza kwa haraka. Jamin alienda kwenye kibanda cha kuogea na kusugua mikono yake mpaka ikawa safi. Akaelekea kwenye mlango wa mbele.

“Jamin.” Alikuwa Bibi. Mwanga wa barazani ulimwonyesha akiwa kwenye kiti chake cha zamani cha kubembea. Blanketi zito lilikuwa limetanda mabegani mwake.

“Naam, Bibi?”

“Unafikiri wewe si mwerevu sana?”

“Hivyo ndivyo Kenny anavyosema.” Jamin alijitikisa kwa kutokuwa na raha.

“Ulikuwa na nguvu za kutosha kufungua mtego, lakini Kenny hakuwa nazo. Ulikuwa na ujasiri wa kutosha kumtafuta gizani. Wavulana wengi wadogo wasingekuwa nao.” Jamin alinyamaza. Bibi Otto aliendelea kubembea kidogo, kisha akatabasamu. “Mungu alikuumba jinsi ulivyo kwa sababu fulani, Jamin. Alimuumba Kenny jinsi alivyo kwa sababu fulani. Ana mpango kwa ajili yako, na nafasi ambayo wewe peke yako unaweza kuijaza, unajua.”

Jamin aligeuka na kuingia jikoni kulikokuwa na joto. Alikuwa akitabasamu.

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

هل تؤمن بالمعجزات؟ هل تؤمن بما يفوق الطبيعة؟ ماذا عن التدخل الإلهي؟ أو لعل السؤال الأفضل هو: هل رأيت الله يعمل في حياتك؟ وهل يرى الآخرون الله يعمل في حياتك؟

كان أخي يعمل في الدفيئة حين دخل أحد الزبائن وتأمل بإعجاب جمال النباتات كلها. ثم هتف معبّرًا عن إعجابه بكل ما بذلناه من عمل شاق. فأجابه أخي: «يزرع أحدهم، ويسقي آخر، لكن الله هو الذي ينمّي». فرد الزبون قائلًا: «لا، لا، لا تنسب الفضل إلى الله. أنتم من جاء إلى هنا وبذل كل هذا الجهد. زرعتم كل هذه النباتات وسقيتموها وسمّدتموها، وأنتم تستحقون الفضل كله، لا الله!» والسبب في شعور الرجل هذا هو أنه إنسانيّ.

ما الإنسانية؟

يعرّف القاموس الإنسانية بأنها نظرة أو منظومة فكرية تولي أهمية قصوى للإنسان بدلًا من الأمور الإلهية أو الخارقة للطبيعة. وتشدد المعتقدات الإنسانية على القيمة والخير الكامنين في البشر، وتؤكد الاحتياجات الإنسانية المشتركة، وتسعى إلى إيجاد حلول لمشكلات البشر بالطرق العقلانية وحدها.

إذا كان الله موجودًا، فعلينا أن نقرّ بهذه الحقيقة وأن نجيب أمامه. ويحاول الإنسانيون إثبات أن الله غير موجود، لكي يعيشوا حياتهم بحرية كما يشاؤون. ووفقًا للإنسانية، لا إله. وإذا كان الأمر كذلك، فنحن، الجنس البشري، أسمى من الله. كل شيء من أجلنا ومن أجل سعادتنا القصوى. هذا هو تعريف الإنسانية.

نوعان من الإنسانية

هناك نوعان من المعتقدات الإنسانية، وسنتناول كليهما. المعتقد الأول هو النظرية القائلة بعدم وجود الله. وفي الواقع، يبدو أن هذه هي الطريقة العقلانية الوحيدة لتكون إنسانيًا. فالإنسان هو الذي يخلق كل شيء ولأجل الإنسان. ولا وجود لعوامل أخرى أو لتدخل خارق للطبيعة. كل شيء يحدث بالعقل والمنطق السليم. ولكل ما يحدث تفسير منطقي. وبالطبع، هناك أمور لا تبدو منطقية، لكن الإنسانيين يتجاهلونها ولا ينظرون إلا إلى الأمور التي يمكن تفسيرها. وكما هو الحال مع النباتات في الدفيئة، ينظرون إلى كل ما يفعله الإنسان ويتجاهلون الجانب الخارق للطبيعة في خروج النبتة إلى حياة جديدة. ويعمل العلماء في أنحاء العالم بجدّ لإخضاع كل ما حدث قط، حتى خلق العالم، للتفسير بالعقل البشري. ويحاول العلماء، بكل ما لديهم من علم وحكمة، تقديم تفسيرات منطقية لأسباب وقوع الكوارث الطبيعية والأزمات العالمية. فإذا استطاعوا تفسير كل شيء، أمكنهم استبعاد الله ووجوده. وهذا يتيح للجنس البشري أن يفعل ما يشاء دون عواقب أبدية. ويؤدي ذلك بدوره إلى شعور عظيم بالسلام الزائف.

يسخر الإنسانيون، بكل ما لديهم من استدلال، من وجود الله نفسه. وإذا ذهبت إلى معظم الكليات في أمريكا وتحدثت إلى الناس عن المسيحية، ضحكوا عليك واستهزؤوا بحقيقة أن المسيحيين يؤمنون بالله فعلًا.

أما النوع الثاني من المعتقدات الإنسانية فهو نظرية إنسانية تقرّ بوجود الله. وقد جادل أحد علماء الأنثروبولوجيا بأن الإنسانية مشروع حداثي واستمرار علماني للاهوت المسيحي الغربي. لكن إذا سألت الناس عمّا يظنون أن الإنسانية تعنيه، فغالبًا ما تحصل على إجابات مختلفة، ويغدو الأمر مربكًا جدًا. ولكن ما سبب هذا الالتباس؟ لأن الناس يحاولون أن يكونوا إنسانيين مسيحيين. وكثيرًا ما وُجّه النقد إلى الإنسانية المسيحية بسبب غموضها وصعوبة تعريفها. والسبب في هذا الالتباس هو أن الناس يريدون الإيمان بالله، لكنهم يريدون أيضًا الإيمان بأنفسهم وبأن العالم يدور حولهم.

نقرأ في رسالة رومية: «لأن غضب الله مُعلَن من السماء على جميع فجور الناس وإثمهم، الذين يحجزون الحق بالإثم؛ إذ معرفة الله ظاهرة فيهم، لأن الله أظهرها لهم. لأن أموره غير المنظورة تُرى منذ خلق العالم، مُدرَكة بالمصنوعات، قدرته السرمدية ولاهوته، حتى إنهم بلا عذر. لأنهم لما عرفوا الله لم يمجدوه أو يشكروه كإله، بل حمقوا في أفكارهم وأظلم قلبهم الغبي. وبينما هم يزعمون أنهم حكماء صاروا جهلاء، وأبدلوا مجد الله الذي لا يفنى بصورة شبه الإنسان الذي يفنى، والطيور والدواب والزحافات. لذلك أسلمهم الله أيضًا في شهوات قلوبهم إلى النجاسة، لإهانة أجسادهم بين ذواتهم. الذين استبدلوا حق الله بالكذب، واتقوا وعبدوا المخلوق دون الخالق، الذي هو مبارك إلى الأبد. آمين. لذلك أسلمهم الله أيضًا إلى أهواء الهوان، لأن نساءهم استبدلن الاستعمال الطبيعي بالذي على خلاف الطبيعة. وكذلك الرجال أيضًا، تاركين استعمال الأنثى الطبيعي، اشتعلوا بشهوتهم بعضهم لبعض، فاعلين الفحشاء ذكورًا بذكور، ونائلين في أنفسهم جزاء ضلالهم المحق. وكما لم يستحسنوا أن يُبقوا الله في معرفتهم، أسلمهم الله إلى ذهن مرفوض، ليفعلوا ما لا يليق؛ مملوئين من كل إثم وزنى وشر وطمع وخبث، مشحونين حسدًا وقتلًا وخصامًا ومكرًا وسوءًا، نمامين ومفترين ومبغضين لله وشاتمين ومتكبرين ومدّعين ومبتدعين شرورًا وعاصين للوالدين، بلا فهم ولا عهد ولا حنو ولا رضا ولا رحمة. الذين إذ عرفوا حكم الله أن الذين يفعلون مثل هذه يستوجبون الموت، لا يفعلونها فقط، بل يسرّون أيضًا بالذين يفعلونها» (رومية 1:18-32).

فكيف يمكن للمرء أن يكون إنسانيًا ويؤمن بالله؟ هنا يقترب الأمر منا أكثر. يؤمن هذا النوع من الإنسانيين بأن الله يريد له أن يكون سعيدًا. وهو يؤمن بإله خالق، لكنه لا يؤمن بأنه ينبغي له أن يخدمه في الواقع. فهو لا يؤمن بالإله الحقيقي، بل خلق في ذهنه إلهًا وهميًا لا وجود له. وهذا يتيح له أن يعيش لنفسه ولسعادته الخاصة. سيتحدث هذا النوع من الأشخاص عن الله، ويذهب إلى الكنيسة، وينشد الترانيم، ويردد الصلوات. لكنه لا ينظر إلا إلى البشر لتلبية جميع احتياجاته. فإذا مرض، اتصل بطبيب. وإذا احتاج إلى المال، قصد المصرفي. وإذا احتاج إلى الابتعاد عن الواقع، أخذ إجازة أو ذهب في خلوة. يعيش حياته من أجل سعادته الخاصة، ثم يشكر الله مع أنه لم يلجأ إلى الله لتلبية احتياجاته. هؤلاء الناس يعتمدون على أنفسهم، ويثقون بأنفسهم.

إليك مثالًا: يزرع مسيحي حديقة ويعتني بها كل يوم. يسقيها ويسمّدها ويزيل الأعشاب الضارة ويقلّم نباتاتها. وأخيرًا تبدأ نباتاته كلها بإنتاج ثمار طيبة. فيشكر الله على الحصاد الوفير. وقد زرع جاره، وهو إنساني ملحد، حديقة أيضًا. وكان هو كذلك يخرج كل يوم ليسقي ويقلّم ويزيل الأعشاب الضارة ويسمّد. وحصل هو أيضًا على حصاد وفير. لكنه تفاخر بكل ما أنجزه. فعل الرجلان الأمور نفسها وحصدا نتائج متشابهة. نسب أحدهما الفضل إلى الله، ونسبه الآخر إلى نفسه. وسيقول إنه أنجز من دون الله ما أنجزه جاره مع الله. ويعلم المسيحيون أنه مخطئ، وأنه كان محتاجًا إلى الله فعلًا لكي ينمّي حديقته.

عندما يحدث أمر يتطلب تدخلًا خارقًا للطبيعة، يصلي الإنساني المسيحي ويطلب من الآخرين أن يصلوا. لكنه لا يؤمن بأن الله سيستجيب لصلواتهم، ويبادر فورًا إلى العمل على حل مشكلته مستخدمًا العقل البشري وحده. ثم إذا حُلّت المشكلة، يشكر الله عليها. لقد أربك هذا النوع من الإنسانية العالم الحديث. وتسبب في سخرية غير المؤمنين من الإيمان المسيحي ووصفه بأنه دين زائف لا قوة له.

المسيحي لا يؤمن بالاستدلال البشري. بل يؤمن بأن إله السماء هو علة كل شيء. «فإنه فيه خُلق الكل، ما في السماوات وما على الأرض، ما يُرى وما لا يُرى، سواء كان عروشًا أم سيادات أم رياسات أم سلطات. الكل به وله قد خُلق» (كولوسي 1:16). نحن لا شيء بدونه، وبدونه لا نستطيع أن نفعل شيئًا. المسيحية هي نقيض الإنسانية. وعندما يفعل المسيحي أمرًا خارقًا للطبيعة، أمرًا لا يستطيع الإنساني أو الملحد فعله، يكون لدينا أمر يحير الحكماء.

عندما يرى الجار المسيحي يحب أعداءه، ويغفر لمن أساء إليه، ويفعل أمورًا لا يستطيع الجار فعلها، يبدأ بالتساؤل عن مصدر القدرة على فعل هذه الأمور. وهذا يقوده إلى الآب. وعندما لا نفعل شيئًا خارقًا للطبيعة، فإنه يحتار.

وماذا عنا؟

أخشى أننا نقع في فخ «الإنسانية المسيحية». نتكلم بما ينبغي أن نقوله؛ ونقول إننا نؤمن بالله. نذهب إلى الكنيسة، وننشد الترانيم، ونردد الصلوات. ومع ذلك، توحي مظاهرنا الخارجية بأننا نتكل على أنفسنا. ولأننا جعلنا حياتنا تدور حول أنفسنا ورفاهنا، لا يسمعنا إله السماء. لا تُستجاب صلواتنا، ويغدو قضاء الوقت على ركبنا جهادًا في أحسن الأحوال. نؤدي الحركات المعتادة لأن هذا ما عُلّمناه، لكن إيماننا يقوم على الاستدلال البشري.

قد يكون طلب الرب بالغ الصعوبة ونحن نعيش في مجتمع إنساني، مجتمع أتقن السعي إلى الحرية والسعادة. وببطء، ترضخ الكنيسة لأساليب هذا العالم.

كان أحد الخدام من الصين يزور الكنائس في أمريكا. وقبل عودته إلى الصين، سُئل عمّا أثار إعجابه أكثر من غيره في الكنائس الأمريكية. فأجاب: «يدهشني كل ما أنجزوه من دون الله».

يحسن بنا أن نبسّط تعريف الإنسانية المعاصر. فالإنساني ينكر بفخر وجود الله حين يتباهى بقوته وقدراته. ويعلن إنجازات الإنسان العظيمة ويسخر من المسيحي المتواضع.

ينكر المسيحي ذاته، ويحمل صليبه، ويتبع سيده. ولا يرى المسيحي في نفسه أو في قدرة الإنسان شيئًا يُعتدّ به، بل يقرّ بثقة بأنه ليس إلا ترابًا، وأنه سيعود سريعًا إلى ذلك التراب. وينظر المسيحي إلى الخير في الآخرين، ويتكل على الله في جميع احتياجاته وهمومه اليومية.

يؤمن المسيحيون أنهم ليسوا إلا خدامًا لسيدهم. يكرههم العالم، ويزدريهم معظم الناس ويرفضونهم. «إن كان العالم يبغضكم، فاعلموا أنه قد أبغضني قبلكم» (يوحنا 15:18). بالنسبة إليهم، هذه الحياة ليست سعيًا وراء السعادة. ولا تهمهم أمور هذا العالم حتى. يأتي فرحهم وسلامهم حصريًا من خدمة سيدهم وإرضاء أبيهم السماوي. وهم غريبون في نظر العالم. حمقى. أما عند الله فهم أولاده الأحباء.

لا يزال الله يبحث اليوم عمّن يضعون ثقتهم فيه. فهو يتطلع في كل الأرض باحثًا عن شخص، في مكان ما، يطرح جانبًا الاستدلال البشري والمنطق السليم ويطيع الصوت الآتي من السماء. يريد الله رجالًا ذوي إيمان يخطون إلى عالم ما يفوق الطبيعة، مثل إبراهيم وموسى وداود وآلاف المؤمنين الذين تبعوهم. يريد شخصًا ينكر ذاته وهذا العالم ويتبع المخلّص.

عندما تنتهي هذه الحياة، سيهلك الإنسانيون، سواء قالوا إنهم يؤمنون بالله أم لا. أما المسيحيون فسيمضون ليعيشوا إلى الأبد في المجد.

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Meu irmão estava trabalhando na estufa quando um cliente entrou e admirou a beleza de todas as plantas. Em seguida, exclamou o quanto ficou impressionado com todo o nosso trabalho. Meu irmão respondeu: “Um planta, outro rega, mas Deus dá o crescimento.” Ao que o cliente respondeu: “Não, não, não dê o crédito a Deus. Vocês vieram aqui e fizeram todo esse trabalho. Vocês plantaram, regaram e adubaram todas essas plantas, e vocês merecem o crédito, não Deus!” A razão pela qual o homem se sentia assim é porque ele era um humanista.

O que é Humanismo?

O dicionário define humanismo assim: uma visão ou sistema de pensamento que atribui importância principal às questões humanas em vez das divinas ou sobrenaturais. As crenças humanistas enfatizam o valor e a bondade potenciais dos seres humanos, salientam as necessidades humanas comuns e buscam exclusivamente maneiras racionais de resolver os problemas humanos.

Se Deus realmente existe, então teremos de reconhecer esse fato e prestar contas a Ele. Os humanistas tentam provar que Deus não existe, para que possam viver livremente como lhes aprouver. Segundo o humanismo, não há Deus. Se assim for, então nós, a raça humana, somos superiores a Deus. Tudo existe para nós e para a nossa felicidade suprema. Esta é a definição de humanismo.

Dois Tipos de Humanismo

Existem dois tipos de crenças humanistas, e vamos examinar ambos. A primeira crença é a teoria de que não há Deus. Na realidade, esta parece ser a única forma racional de ser um humanista. Tudo é criado pelo homem e para o homem. Não há outros fatores nem envolvimento sobrenatural. Tudo acontece por razão e bom senso. Há uma explicação lógica para tudo o que ocorre. Claro, algumas coisas não fazem sentido, mas os humanistas deixam essas de lado e olham apenas para as coisas que podem ser explicadas. Como as plantas na estufa, eles observam tudo o que o homem faz e ignoram a parte sobrenatural de uma planta brotar com nova vida. Cientistas em todo o mundo trabalham diligentemente para aplicar o raciocínio humano a tudo o que já aconteceu, inclusive à criação do mundo. Cientistas, com todo seu aprendizado e sabedoria, tentam dar explicações lógicas para por que desastres naturais e crises globais acontecem. Se puderem explicar tudo, então podem excluir Deus e Sua existência. Isso permite que a raça humana faça o que quiser sem consequências eternas. Isso, por sua vez, leva a uma grande sensação de paz falsa.

Os humanistas, com todo o seu raciocínio, zombam da própria existência de Deus. Se você for à maioria das faculdades na América e conversar com as pessoas sobre o cristianismo, elas riem de você e zombam do fato de os cristãos realmente crerem em Deus.

O segundo tipo de crença humanista é uma teoria que reconhece a existência de Deus. Um antropólogo argumentou que o humanismo é um projeto da modernidade e uma continuação secularizada da teologia cristã ocidental. Mas se você perguntar às pessoas o que acham que o humanismo significa, provavelmente obterá respostas diferentes, e isso se torna muito confuso. Mas por que a confusão? Porque as pessoas estão tentando ser humanistas cristãos. O humanismo cristão tem sido frequentemente criticado por sua vaguidade e dificuldade de definição. A razão pela qual se tornou tão confuso é que as pessoas querem crer em Deus, mas também acreditam em si mesmas e que o mundo gira ao seu redor.

Em Romanos lemos: “Porque a ira de Deus se revela do céu contra toda impiedade e injustiça dos homens que suprimem a verdade; Porque o que de Deus se pode conhecer neles se manifesta, porque Deus lho manifestou. Pois as coisas invisíveis dele, desde a criação do mundo, tanto o seu eterno poder como a sua divindade, se entendem pelas coisas que estão criadas, de modo que eles são inexcusáveis; Porque, tendo conhecido a Deus, não o glorificaram como Deus, nem lhe deram graças; antes se tornaram vãos nos seus pensamentos, e o coração insensato deles se obscureceu. Dando-se por sábios, tornaram-se loucos, e mudaram a glória do Deus incorruptível em semelhança da imagem do homem corruptível, e de aves, e de quadrúpedes e de répteis. Por isso Deus os entregou nas concupiscências de seus corações, à impureza, para desonrarem os seus corpos entre si; que mudaram a verdade de Deus em mentira, e honraram e serviram mais a criatura do que o Criador, o qual é bendito eternamente. Amém. Por isso Deus os entregou a paixões infames; porque até as suas mulheres mudaram o uso natural, no contrário à natureza. E semelhantemente também os homens, deixando o uso natural da mulher, se inflamaram em suas concupiscências uns para com os outros, cometendo homens com homens torpeza, e recebendo em si mesmos a recompensa que convinha ao seu erro. E, como não aprovaram ter conhecimento de Deus, Deus os entregou a um sentimento reprovado, para fazerem coisas que não convêm; cheios de toda injustiça, fornicação, malícia, avareza, maldade; cheios de inveja, homicídio, contenda, engano, malignidade; murmuradores, detratores, odiosos de Deus, injuriosos, soberbos, presunçosos, inventores de males, desobedientes aos pais, sem entendimento, sem aliança, sem afeição natural, implacáveis, sem misericórdia; os quais, conhecendo a justiça de Deus, que são dignos de morte os que tais coisas fazem, não só as fazem, mas também se complacem com os que as fazem” (Romanos 1:18-32).

Então, como alguém pode ser humanista e crer em Deus? Aqui é onde chegamos mais perto de casa. Esse tipo de humanista crê que Deus quer que ele seja feliz. Ele acredita em um Deus Criador, mas não crê que tenha de servi-Lo na realidade. Ele não crê no verdadeiro Deus, mas, em sua mente, criou um deus fictício que não existe. Isso lhe permite viver para si mesmo e para a própria felicidade. Esse tipo de pessoa falará sobre Deus, irá à igreja, cantará hinos e fará orações. Contudo, ele olhará apenas para o homem para todas as suas necessidades. Se estiver doente, chama um médico. Se precisar de dinheiro, vai ao banqueiro. Se precisar de uma pausa da realidade, tira férias ou vai a um retiro. Vive a vida para a própria felicidade e então agradece a Deus, embora não tenha buscado a Deus para suas necessidades. Essas pessoas dependem de si mesmas. Têm confiança em si mesmas.

Aqui está um exemplo: um cristão planta um jardim e cuida dele todos os dias. Ele rega e aduba, arranca ervas daninhas e poda. Finalmente, suas plantas começam a frutificar, frutos bons. Ele agradece a Deus pela colheita abundante. Seu vizinho, um humanista ateu, também plantou um jardim. Ele também saía todos os dias para regar, podar, arrancar ervas e adubar. Também colheu abundantemente. Esse homem, entretanto, gabou-se de tudo o que havia realizado. Ambos os homens fizeram as mesmas coisas e tiveram resultados semelhantes. Um deu o crédito a Deus, e outro creditou a si mesmo. Ele dirá que realizou o mesmo sem Deus que seu vizinho fez com Deus. Os cristãos sabem que ele está errado e que, na verdade, ele precisou de Deus para fazer seu jardim crescer.

Quando algo acontece que exige intervenção sobrenatural, o humanista cristão ora e pede que outros orem. Porém, ele não crê que Deus responderá às suas orações e, instantaneamente, põe-se a trabalhar para resolver seu problema, usando somente o raciocínio humano. Então, se o problema é resolvido, ele agradece a Deus por isso. Esse tipo de humanismo confundiu o mundo moderno. Fez os incrédulos zombarem da fé cristã e a chamarem de uma religião falsa e sem poder.

O cristão não acredita no raciocínio humano. O cristão crê que o Deus dos céus é a razão de tudo. “Porque nele foram criadas todas as coisas, que nos céus e na terra, visíveis e invisíveis, sejam tronos, ou dominações, ou principados, ou potestades; tudo foi criado por ele e para ele” (Colossenses 1:16). Não somos nada sem Ele, e sem Ele nada podemos fazer. O cristianismo é o oposto do humanismo. Quando o cristão faz algo sobrenatural, algo que o humanista ou o ateu não pode fazer, então temos algo que confundirá os sábios.

Quando o vizinho vê o cristão amar seus inimigos, perdoar alguém que o ofendeu e fazer coisas que ele não consegue fazer, então começa a perguntar de onde veio o poder para fazer essas coisas. Isso então o conduz ao Pai. Quando não há nada sobrenatural no que estamos fazendo, ele fica confuso.

E Quanto a Nós?

Receio que estamos caindo nessa armadilha do “Humanismo Cristão”. Falamos o que convém; dizemos que cremos em Deus. Vamos à igreja, cantamos hinos e fazemos orações. No entanto, pela aparência exterior, confiamos em nós mesmos. Porque centramos nossas vidas em nós mesmos e em nosso bem-estar, o Deus dos céus não nos ouve. Nossas orações não são respondidas, e o tempo de joelhos é, na melhor das hipóteses, uma luta. Fazemos os gestos porque assim fomos ensinados, mas nossa fé repousa no raciocínio humano.

Pode ser extremamente difícil buscar o Senhor enquanto se vive em uma sociedade humanista. Uma sociedade que aperfeiçoou a busca da liberdade e da felicidade. Aos poucos, a igreja está cedendo aos modos deste mundo.

Um ministro da China estava visitando as igrejas na América. Antes de partir de volta para a China, foi perguntado o que mais o impressionara nas igrejas americanas. Ele respondeu: “Estou impressionado com o que tudo eles realizaram sem Deus.”

Faríamos bem em simplificar a definição moderna de humanismo. O humanista nega orgulhosamente que haja um Deus quando se gaba de sua própria força e habilidades. Proclama os grandes feitos do homem e zomba do cristão humilde.

O cristão nega a si mesmo, toma sua cruz e segue seu Mestre. O cristão não pensa em si mesmo nem nas capacidades do homem, admitindo confiantemente que é apenas pó e que em pó logo retornará. O cristão busca o bem nos outros e confia em Deus para todas as suas necessidades e cuidados diários.

Os cristãos creem que são meramente servos de seu Senhor. São odiados pelo mundo e desprezados pela maioria, rejeitados. “Se o mundo vos odeia, sabei que primeiro me odiou a mim. Se a vós odeia, também me odiou antes de odiar a vós.” (João 15:18) Para eles, esta vida não é a busca da felicidade. As coisas deste mundo nem sequer os interessam. Sua alegria e paz vêm unicamente de servir ao seu Senhor, de agradar ao seu Pai Celestial. Para o mundo, são estranhos. Tolos. Para Deus, são Seus queridos filhos.

Deus ainda está procurando hoje pessoas que ponham sua confiança Nele. Ele busca por toda a terra alguém, em algum lugar, que deixe de lado o raciocínio humano e o bom senso e obedeça à voz do céu. Deus quer homens com fé que deem um passo no sobrenatural, como Abraão, Moisés, Davi e os milhares de crentes que os seguiram. Alguém que negue a si mesmo e a este mundo e siga o Salvador.

Quando esta vida terminar, os humanistas, quer digam que creem em Deus ou não, perecerão. E os cristãos seguirão para viver eternamente na glória.

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Vår Faders värld är en värld som inte fördärvats av mänskliga uppfinningar och ingrepp. Även om synden och tekniken har förvrängt och berövat mänskligheten många vackra ting, finns ännu några kvar som civilisationen inte har skadat. Små barn i den friska oskulden under sin obefläckade morgon står främst som ett stycke himmel på jorden och kallar alla som ser dem att vända blicken mot himlen. Ett annat är himlens fåglar, så som de beskrivs i Första Moseboken. Paulus vädjade till församlingen i Korinth: ”Lär inte själva naturen er?” Vi uppmanas att betrakta liljorna, korparna och markens gräs. Var och en av dessa bär i sin tillvaro en betydelsefull aspekt av den evige Guden och ger oss en bild av sin Skapare. Kanske kan hela naturen ge oss ögonblicksbilder av den himmelska världen, om vi hade tid och ögon att betrakta den.

Fåglarna har en unik plats i Guds skapelse, för deras värld finns i himlen. Människan kan stiga upp på ett flygplans vingar och undkomma jorden där nere i några timmar, men himlen kommer aldrig att vara en plats där hon normalt har herravälde. Fåglarna är en bild av ett himmelskt släkte, för där är de hemma. De är en naturlig bild av Guds heliga och änglar, och därför gör vi klokt i att ge dem tillbörlig uppmärksamhet. Även om det finns dussintals lärdomar att dra av dessa bärare av nåd och skönhet, märks en av de mest framträdande och enastående dygderna i sången de stämmer upp. Många djur som lever på jorden är praktiskt taget stumma. De som ändå ger ljud ifrån sig gör det ofta för att hota eller uttrycka klagan. ”Skriar vildåsnan när den har gräs? Eller råmar oxen över sitt foder?” (Job 6:5). När de är glada och nöjda har de inget budskap att förmedla. Hunden skäller på en inkräktare för att driva bort honom, medan katten jamar för att få uppmärksamhet. De ger ljud ifrån sig när de är hotade eller missnöjda, rädda eller har ont. På liknande sätt delar den jordiska människan sin natur med markens däggdjur.

Fåglarna är annorlunda. De använder sina glada röster så mycket att de är själva sinnebilden för lycka. Uttrycket ”glad som en lärka” är så vanligt att det används av människor som aldrig ens har begett sig ut på ängen för att se eller höra en lärka. Även om somliga upplyser oss om att dessa sånger bara är parningsläten och har föga med deras känslor att göra, kan vi inte komma ifrån den inre övertygelsen att dessa fåglar, vare sig de parar sig eller inte, finner glädje i att ge ett jublande uttryck för glädje, och vi gör klokt i att låta dem undervisa oss. ”Är någon glad? Låt honom sjunga psalmer” (Jakobsbrevet 5:13). Fåglarna gör detta oupphörligt, och det tycks omöjligt att dra någon annan slutsats än att de är glada när de gör det. Gå nära en svalas bo, så upptäcker du att de också har sätt att uttrycka ogillande. Skrikstrandpiparen tvekar inte heller att uttrycka häftigt missnöje mot dem som tränger in på dess område, men dessa läten ska inte förväxlas med sånger. De sjungande fåglarna är en vackert målad bild av Guds heliga och änglar.

Hur lite kunskap om himlen har inte anförtrotts vårt förstånd. De himmelska scener som beskrivs och läggs fram för oss i Uppenbarelseboken kan knappast föra våra begränsade sinnen in i dess oändliga rike. En aspekt som vi kan förstå är att det är en plats fylld av sång. Det är inte så underligt, för det är det slutliga målet för Guds förnöjsamma och glädjefyllda heliga, och där ska de sjunga en ny sång. Nästan varje scen vid tronen i Uppenbarelseboken präglas av någon form av lovprisning. ”Och han har lagt en ny sång i min mun, en lovsång till vår Gud” (Psaltaren 40:3). Vid 22 tillfällen upprepar Skriften uttrycket: Jag ska sjunga.

Det ligger i fåglarnas natur att sjunga. Det är deras första tanke när de vaknar och morgonen förgyller himlen, och sången strömmar ur deras inre som en källa. Alla deras sånger är inte likadana. Somliga är konstfulla till sin längd, rytm och tonhöjd, medan andra är enkla. Somliga bara kvittrar med glatt hjärta. Vandringstrasten inleder kören tidigt på våren, men dess sång överträffas snart i skönhet av sångsparven och sedan av den rosenbröstade kardinalen. Gärdsmygens sång överträffar dem alla i uthållighet och livfullhet. Kanariefågeln sjunger i en bur, medan näktergalen sjunger i mörkret. Vandringstrastarna sjunger i regnet. Fältsparvarna fyller dagens heta timmar med sång när andra fåglar är tysta. Hur olika deras sång än må vara, brister de alla ut i sprudlande glädje. Det är här de ska undervisa oss.

”Tala till varandra med psalmer och hymner och andliga sånger, sjung och spela i era hjärtan för Herren” (Efesierbrevet 5:19). Kristi ankomst präglades av änglaskaran som förkunnade fred och välvilja mot människorna. Alla som vill bära hans namn måste förmedla samma budskap. I Johannes 4 möter vi scenen vid Jakobs brunn, där Kristus ber kvinnan om något att dricka. Hennes svar tycks bära en anstrykning av bitterhet. ”Judarna har inget samröre med samarierna.” Även om hon betraktade sig själv som en andlig människa och villigt följde honom in i ett religiöst samtal, hade hon ingen sång. Liksom i brunnen de talar över låg hennes vatten djupt under ytan, och hur mödosamt var det inte att få upp det. Kristus erbjuder ett annat alternativ. ”Men det vatten som jag ska ge honom ska i honom bli en vattenkälla som springer fram till evigt liv” (Johannes 4:14).

Kristi brunn är en artesisk brunn. Man behöver varken kruka eller arbete för att hämta upp vattnet, för det strömmar fram rikligt av sig självt. Även om Kristus troligen talar om Anden, som i Johannes 7:38, kan detta förvisso lika väl tillämpas på ett hjärta fyllt av glädje. Vad kunde mer passande strömma ur en källa inspirerad av Kristus än sångens hänförelse? ”Se, mina tjänare ska sjunga av hjärtats glädje” (Jesaja 65:14). Allt detta borde nu verka tydligt nog att förstå och lätt nog att göra, men ack, vi finner att vi har en ständig och ihärdig motståndare som försöker hindra vår sång. Vi är inte ovetande om hans knep...

Synd. Alla fåglar sjunger inte. Somliga har ett yttre som är svart som synden. Dessa tycks bara skräna och skrika och är inget föredöme för Guds heliga att efterlikna. Det pladdrande oljud vi hör från många förbipasserande fordon liknar sannerligen dessa orena fåglars sånger. ”Det stora Babylon har fallit, har fallit, och har blivit en boning för demoner och ett tillhåll för varje oren ande och en bur för varje oren och avskyvärd fågel” (Uppenbarelseboken 18:2). Dessa talrika varelser är de fallna andarna, fåglarna som väntar på att sluka säden som såtts vid vägen. Till sådana hör de värdelösa trupialerna, stararna och båtstjärtarna. Kråkorna visar sig också vid vägkanten, där de äter ruttnande kadaver. Ofta finner man dem i stort antal när de äter av majsen som bonden mödosamt planterat åt sig själv. Så syndar den själviska själen i sin jakt på lycka, när han glatt livnär sig på en annans olycka och utnyttjar dennes synd. Han har ingen sång, för hans dag förmörkas ständigt av missgärningarna hos andra som korsar hans väg.

Försummelse. Kostaren är också svart (honan är brun/grå). Hon sitter på en hög utsiktsplats och kallar skamlöst på sina älskare med sina gälla skrik. Sedan har hon fräckheten att lägga sitt ägg i en annan fågels bo och tvinga dem att föda upp hennes avkomma. Detta är sannerligen en passande sinnebild för ett stort antal kvinnor i vår tid. Även om omständigheterna får rättfärdiga dem, bryr sig dessa kvinnor inte om sina egna, utan är produkter av försummelse. De har ingen vaggvisa att dela med sina små, för de har fört dem till någon annans bo medan deras tankar är upptagna av arbete och affärer. ”Men du är den som tog mig ur moderlivet; du fick mig att hoppas när jag låg vid min mors bröst” (Psaltaren 22:9). Utan tvivel kan den sjungande modern plantera rikligt med sånger i sitt spädbarn och lägga grunden för ett lyckligt och hoppfullt liv. Även om vi kan visa barmhärtighet mot en kvinna i svåra omständigheter, bär den förhärskande sången hos moderna kvinnor ackord som bara är disharmoniska och vemodiga. Dessa är tilltäppta brunnar likt de brunnar som Isak fann när han återvände till Gerar. Filistéerna ”hade fyllt dem med jord” (Första Moseboken 26:15). Så står det till i många familjers andligt försummade hem i dag, där man fyller sina scheman med så många jordiska åtaganden att man inte har tid att tillbringa en timme tillsammans i sång. Om fåglarna slutade sjunga, skulle de ens märka det?

Otacksamhet. Finn en själ som är dränkt i otacksamhet, så finner du en själ utan sång. Om kanariefågeln vägrade sjunga i fångenskap, skulle få av oss någonsin ha hört dess sprudlande melodi. ”Vi hängde våra harpor på pilträden där. Ty där krävde de som hade fört oss bort i fångenskap att vi skulle sjunga, och de som hade ödelagt oss krävde glädje och sade: Sjung en av Sions sånger för oss. Hur ska vi kunna sjunga HERRENS sång i ett främmande land?” (Psaltaren 137:2-4). Guds folk hade genom Jeremia fått anvisningar att bygga hus, plantera trädgårdar och bilda familjer. ”… Och sök fred för den stad dit jag har låtit föra er i fångenskap, och be till HERREN för den, ty i dess fred ska ni ha fred” (Jeremia 29:5-7). Men de kunde inte se något värde i det. Med blicken fäst på den dystra omgivningen förlorade de sin sång. Israel hade i sin historia en rik sångtradition. Deras sång bröt fram vid övergången av Röda havet under Josafats dagar och hade varit känd för att besegra härar. Jordiskt obehag är ingen ursäkt för att hålla inne med tacksamheten, för vår Gud regerar och vi är hans barn. Sådana var förhållandena i fängelset i Filippi, där två burfåglar, Paulus och Silas, inledde konserten vid midnatt och fick korridorerna att skaka med sin glada sång.

När vi öppnar våra munnar och låter våra röster ljuda i lovprisning, ger vi uttryck åt Guds nåd. Vi ansluter oss till de trognas kör vid sidan av Mirjam, Debora och Hanna och förenar oss i harmoni med Mose, David, Paulus och Barnabas. På kvällen sjunger vi med vår Herre och hans lärjungar efter måltiden och med legioner av änglar som ”ger ära åt Gud i höjden”. Om det inte räcker, borde vi kanske överväga att stiga upp i den tidiga gryningen och sjunga med de oräkneliga skarorna av våra befjädrade vänner som är tacksamma för Guds kärleksfulla försyn. ”Låt Kristi ord bo rikligt hos er i all vishet; undervisa och förmana varandra med psalmer och hymner och andliga sånger, och sjung med nåd i era hjärtan för Herren … Och vad ni än gör, gör det av hjärtat, som för Herren och inte för människor” (Kolosserbrevet 3:16, 23).

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

শেষ মুহূর্তের তাড়াহুড়ো এমন এক বিষয়, যার মুখোমুখি অনেক গৃহকর্ত্রী নিয়মিত হন। আমরা যতই সুসংগঠিত থাকি না কেন, কখনও কখনও কাজগুলো অপছন্দ করি বলে পিছিয়ে দিই, অথবা চাপের মুখে পড়া পর্যন্ত অপেক্ষা করি।

অভ্যাসগতভাবে কাজ ফেলে রাখলে মানসিক চাপ বেড়ে যেতে পারে। হয়তো আমি একটু অদ্ভুত, কিন্তু চাপ বাড়তে থাকলে শান্ত ও সংযত থাকা আমার জন্য কঠিন। শেষ মুহূর্তের কাজগুলো শেষ হতে হতে আমি এতটাই ক্লান্ত হয়ে পড়ি যে পরিকল্পিত অনুষ্ঠানটি উপভোগ করতে পারি না।

দাঁতের ব্যথা ও সড়কপথে ভ্রমণ

ভ্রমণে রওনা হওয়ার এক-দুদিন আগে পরিবারের কেউ কেন শেষ পর্যন্ত দাঁতের ডাক্তারের চেয়ারে গিয়ে বসে, তা আমার কাছে রহস্য। হয়তো আমার ধারণার মতো এটা অত ঘন ঘন ঘটেনি, কিন্তু অনুপযুক্ত সময়ে পরিকল্পনাবহির্ভূতভাবে দাঁতের ডাক্তারের কাছে যাওয়ার হতাশার কথা আমার মনে গেঁথে আছে। এখন ভ্রমণের আগে আমি মনে মনে একটি অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট ঠিক করে রাখি। দাঁতের জরুরি সমস্যা না হলে, অন্য কোনো সমস্যা যে ওই সময়টা নিয়ে নেবে, তা নিশ্চিত।

সময়সীমা জীবনের একটি স্বাভাবিক অংশ। সেগুলো না থাকলে আমরা অনুপ্রাণিত হতাম না, আর আমাদের দিনগুলোতে কোনো উদ্দেশ্য থাকত না। বাধাবিঘ্নও জীবনের স্বাভাবিক অংশ। সেগুলো আমাদের দিন ও সপ্তাহের মধ্যে ক্রমাগত অনিশ্চিত মোড় এনে দেয়। আমরা যদি অনেক কাজ শেষ মুহূর্ত পর্যন্ত ফেলে রাখি, বাধাবিঘ্ন ও সময়সীমা একসঙ্গে এসে পড়ে, আর বিশৃঙ্খলা রাজত্ব করে।

শেষ মুহূর্তের পরিস্থিতি বদলান

সময়সীমা ও বাধাবিঘ্ন দূর করা যায় না, তবে শেষ মুহূর্তের কাজ কমিয়ে আনা যায়। কখনও কখনও আমাদের মানসিক চাপের কারণ খুঁজে বের করতে সৎভাবে পেছন ফিরে তাকাতে হয়। প্রায়ই আমরা এর জন্য বাধাবিঘ্নকে দায়ী করি এবং বুঝতে পারি না যে খারাপ পরিকল্পনা বা কাজ ফেলে রাখাই হয়তো এর কারণ।

উদাহরণস্বরূপ, অতিথিরা আসছেন, আর তাঁদের আসার দিনেই আমরা যদি জানালা ধোয়া ও একটি মিষ্টান্ন তৈরি করাসহ আরও ডজনখানেক কাজ করার পরিকল্পনা করি, তাহলে কোনো বিঘ্নের জন্যই অবকাশ থাকবে না। অভিজ্ঞতা থেকে আমরা জানি, বাধাবিঘ্ন আসবেই। তাহলে মৌমাছির কামড় বা পায়ের আঙুলে আঘাত লাগার কথাও কি “পরিকল্পনায়” রাখা ভালো নয়?

জানালা ধোয়া ও মিষ্টান্ন তৈরির কাজ অন্য দিনের জন্য রাখা যায় না কেন? তাতে হয়তো জানালায় কিছু আঙুলের ছাপ থেকে যাবে এবং মিষ্টান্নটিও হবে সাধারণ, কিন্তু শেষ মুহূর্তে প্রচণ্ড চাপের চেয়ে কি তা ভালো নয়?

কিছু কাজ আগে থেকেই করে রাখুন

দিনের শুরুতেই রাতের খাবারে কী রান্না করবেন ঠিক করে নেওয়া এবং ডায়াপারের ব্যাগ আগে থেকে গুছিয়ে রাখা—এমন ছোটখাটো কাজ শেষ মুহূর্তে বড় পার্থক্য গড়ে দিতে পারে। আমাদের সন্তানরা ছোট থাকার সময়, রওনা হওয়ার দিন স্যুটকেস গোছানোর বদলে আমি ভ্রমণের এক দিন আগে গোছাতে শুরু করেছিলাম। কাজটি আগেই সেরে রাখলে শেষ মুহূর্তের তাড়াহুড়ো সামলানো আমার পক্ষে সহজ হতো।

সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ কাজগুলো আগে করুন

সময়ের টান পড়লে এই পদ্ধতিতে কম গুরুত্বপূর্ণ কাজগুলো বাদ দেওয়ার সুযোগ থাকে।

কখনও কখনও কাজের তালিকার সবকিছু সমান গুরুত্বপূর্ণ নয়। যিনি সবকিছু নিখুঁতভাবে করতে চান, তাঁর পক্ষে কোনো কাজ বাদ দেওয়া কঠিন, তবে নতুন অভ্যাস গড়ে তোলা সম্ভব।

কাজগুলো ছোট ছোট ভাগে ভাগ করুন

কখনও কখনও কোনো কাজের বিশালতা সেটি শুরু করাকেই অসম্ভব বলে মনে করায়। বড় কাজটিকে ছোট ছোট ভাগে ভাগ করুন। ছোট একটি কাজ শেষ করা অনেক বেশি সামলানো যায়। আমার রান্নাঘর ভালোভাবে পরিষ্কার করা এমন একটি কাজ, যা করতে আমি পছন্দ করি না। আমার পরিকল্পনাপত্রে যদি লেখা থাকে, “রান্নাঘর ভালোভাবে পরিষ্কার করো,” তাহলে সেটি উপেক্ষা করা সহজ।

কিন্তু পরিকল্পনাপত্রে যদি লেখা থাকে, “যন্ত্রপাতি পরিষ্কার করো, আলমারির ভেতরটা মুছে পরিষ্কার করো, আর জানালা ধোও,” তাহলে কাজটি করা সম্ভব বলে মনে হয়।

জীবনে এত আনন্দের ঘটনা ঘটে; কাজ ফেলে রাখার কারণে কেন হয়রান হতে হবে? নিজেকে অন্যভাবে জীবনযাপন করার স্বাধীনতা দিন। কয়েকটি ছোট পরিবর্তনই আশীর্বাদময় ও চাপপূর্ণ শেষ মুহূর্তের মধ্যে বড় পার্থক্য গড়ে দিতে পারে।
