Eine christuszentrierte Kennenlernzeit ist eine Reihe von Predigten über eine gottgefällige Kennenlernzeit von Paul Hershberger. Er hielt diese Predigten in den letzten zehn Jahren mehrmals an verschiedenen Orten. Vor Kurzem haben wir sie abschreiben und für eine bessere Lesbarkeit kürzen lassen. Nachdem alle sechs Artikel in The Heartbeat of the Remnant erschienen sind, werden wir sie als Broschüre veröffentlichen. Dies ist der erste von sechs Artikeln.

Einleitung

Meine Frau und ich durften eine Kennenlernzeit erleben, auf die wir ohne Reue oder Schuldgefühle zurückblicken. Wir waren mit Eltern gesegnet, die uns auf dem richtigen Weg führten und uns Möglichkeiten eröffneten, die sie selbst nicht gehabt hatten.

Wenn ihr das nicht bezeugen könnt oder diese Erinnerung nicht habt, quält euch bitte nicht mit Schuldgefühlen. Aber ich bete für euch, dass in eurem Herzen ein brennendes Anliegen und eine Vision entstehen, euren Kindern dies zu ermöglichen. Das kann euer Lohn sein.

Eine christuszentrierte Kennenlernzeit ist ein Zeitraum zwischen dem Leben als Unverheirateter und dem Eheleben. Die Entscheidungen, die ihr in dieser Zeit trefft, werden sich auf den Rest eures Lebens auswirken. Mit Gottes Segen auf eurem Leben könnt ihr am Ende ohne Reue oder Schuldgefühle zurückblicken.

Fünf Ziele dieser Reihe über eine christuszentrierte Kennenlernzeit.

Ziel Nr. 1. Die Herzen der Väter ihren Kindern zuzuwenden.

Ziel Nr. 2. Die Herzen der Kinder ihren Vätern zuzuwenden.

Ziel Nr. 3. Dass Eltern das Anliegen bekommen, jedes ihrer Kinder in den vollkommenen Willen Gottes für sein Leben zu führen.

Ziel Nr. 4. Dass junge Menschen das Anliegen bekommen, nach Gott zu suchen, im Wandel mit Gott Erfüllung und Lebenssinn zu finden, und dass ihr nach Reife in eurem Verhalten und eurem Charakter strebt.

Ziel Nr. 5. Dass junge Männer und junge Frauen sich aufmachen, gottesfürchtige Väter und gottesfürchtige Mütter zu werden, mit der Vision, eine weitere gottesfürchtige Generation heranzuziehen, damit das Evangelium Jesu Christi weitergetragen werden kann.

Gottes Plan für Mann und Frau

Prediger 12:1 sagt: „Gedenke deines Schöpfers in den Tagen deiner Jugend, ehe die bösen Tage kommen und die Jahre nahen, von denen du sagen wirst: Ich habe keine Freude an ihnen.“ Mein Wunsch ist, dass jeder von euch in den Tagen seiner Jugend seines Schöpfers gedenkt. Richtet euer Herz, eure Aufmerksamkeit und euer Leben darauf aus, nach eurem Schöpfer, dem allmächtigen Gott im Himmel, zu suchen.

Was meint er mit „solange die bösen Tage noch nicht kommen“ und „die Jahre noch nicht nahen“? Es bedeutet, den Herrn zu suchen, solange ihr jung seid. Setzt die Kraft eurer Jugend ein und sucht nach Gott. Ihr jungen Menschen seid jung und voller Ideen, Visionen, Pläne und Träume. Ich bezweifle, dass irgendjemand von euch einfach gern in einem bequemen Sessel sitzt, die Füße hochlegt und nur davon träumt, wie schrecklich und furchtbar das Leben werden wird. Das tun wir doch nicht, oder? Aber wenn wir nicht mit Gott wandeln und Gottes Plan folgen, werden schwere Dinge über uns kommen. Wenn Schweres im Leben kommt, haben wir keinen Ort, an den wir uns wenden können. Wir träumen davon, dass das Leben gut verlaufen wird. Die Entscheidungen und Handlungen unserer Jugend wirken sich auf den Rest unseres Lebens aus. Die gute Nachricht ist, dass sie sich zum Guten auswirken können. Die schlechte Nachricht ist, dass sie sich zum Schlechten auswirken können. Es hängt davon ab, welche Entscheidungen wir treffen und was wir wählen. Aber ihr jungen Menschen seid jung und habt die Möglichkeit, euch zu entscheiden.

Gehen wir zum Anfang des ersten Buches Mose.

„Und Gott, der HERR, sprach: Es ist nicht gut, dass der Mensch allein ist; ich will ihm eine Hilfe machen, die ihm entspricht. Und Gott, der HERR, bildete aus dem Erdboden alle Tiere des Feldes und alle Vögel des Himmels und brachte sie zu Adam, um zu sehen, wie er sie nennen würde; und wie Adam jedes lebendige Wesen nannte, so war sein Name. Und Adam gab allem Vieh und den Vögeln des Himmels und allen Tieren des Feldes Namen; aber für Adam fand sich keine Hilfe, die ihm entsprach. Und Gott, der HERR, ließ einen tiefen Schlaf auf Adam fallen, und er schlief; und er nahm eine seiner Rippen und verschloss die Stelle mit Fleisch. Und Gott, der HERR, machte aus der Rippe, die er dem Menschen genommen hatte, eine Frau und brachte sie zu dem Menschen. Und Adam sprach: Dies ist nun Bein von meinem Bein und Fleisch von meinem Fleisch; sie soll Frau genannt werden, denn sie wurde aus dem Mann genommen. Darum wird ein Mann seinen Vater und seine Mutter verlassen und seiner Frau anhangen; und sie werden ein Fleisch sein“ (1. Mose 2:18-24).

„Und Gott sprach: Lasst uns den Menschen in unserem Bild machen, uns ähnlich; und sie sollen herrschen über die Fische des Meeres und über die Vögel des Himmels und über das Vieh und über die ganze Erde und über alles Kriechende, das auf der Erde kriecht. So schuf Gott den Menschen in seinem eigenen Bild, im Bild Gottes schuf er ihn; als Mann und Frau schuf er sie. Und Gott segnete sie, und Gott sprach zu ihnen: Seid fruchtbar und vermehrt euch und füllt die Erde und macht sie euch untertan; und herrscht über die Fische des Meeres und über die Vögel des Himmels und über jedes lebendige Wesen, das sich auf der Erde bewegt“ (1. Mose 1:26-28).

„Und Gott, der Herr, sprach: Es ist nicht gut, dass der Mensch allein ist; ich will ihm eine Hilfe machen, die ihm entspricht“ (1. Mose 2:18). „Ich werde ihm eine Hilfe machen, die zu ihm passt.“ Gott sagte, dass er das tun würde.

„So schuf Gott den Menschen in seinem eigenen Bild, im Bild Gottes schuf er ihn; als Mann und Frau schuf er sie“ (1. Mose 1:27). Gott hat uns gemacht. Gott hat uns als Mann und Frau geschaffen. Es braucht sehr viel blinden Glauben, um zu glauben, dass wir uns durch Evolution vollkommen als Mann und Frau entwickelt haben. Die Erschaffung von Mann und Frau ist Gottes Plan. Sie ist einer der lebendigen Beweise für die Schöpfung. Gott hat uns gemacht. Gott hat uns geschaffen. Es ist Gottes Plan. Gott ist der Urheber. Und Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

Ich möchte zehn verschiedene Aspekte dieses Segens betrachten, der aus Gottes Plan kommt.

1) Gott bringt Eva zu Adam.

„Und Gott, der Herr, machte aus der Rippe, die er dem Menschen genommen hatte, eine Frau und brachte sie zu dem Menschen. Und Adam sprach: Dies ist nun Bein von meinem Bein und Fleisch von meinem Fleisch; sie soll Frau genannt werden, denn sie wurde aus dem Mann genommen“ (1. Mose 2:22-23).

Gott ließ Adam in einen tiefen Schlaf fallen. Dann schuf Gott Eva und brachte sie zu Adam. Adam erwachte und erkannte: „Diese ist für mich!“ Er hatte alle Tiere vorbeiziehen sehen, als er ihnen Namen gab. Nun bringt Gott ihm jemanden, der für ihn bestimmt ist. Er erkannte auch: „Sie wurde aus meiner Seite genommen.“ Sie ist seinem Herzen nahe. „Dies ist Bein von meinem Bein und Fleisch von meinem Fleisch.“ Es ist kein Hund, keine Giraffe, kein Affe und kein Menschenaffe. Diese, die Gott zu ihm brachte, ist ihm gleich. Gottes Plan birgt einen Segen.

Adam und Eva hatten zuvor noch nie einen Partner gehabt. Adam und Eva hatten zuvor noch nie den Gefühlen ihres Herzens freien Lauf gelassen. In den Herzen von Adam und Eva geschah etwas. Adam war ein Mann, der nur einer Frau zugetan war, und Eva eine Frau, die nur einem Mann zugetan war. Sie hatten die leidenschaftlichen Regungen ihres Herzens keinem anderen geschenkt. Diesen Plan hat Gott auch für uns. Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

2) Verlassen und Anhangen in lebenslanger Einheit.

„Darum wird ein Mann seinen Vater und seine Mutter verlassen und seiner Frau anhangen; und sie werden ein Fleisch sein“ (1. Mose 2:24).

Dieser Vers sagt: „Darum wird ein Mann seinen Vater und seine Mutter verlassen“, aber Adam und Eva hatten weder Vater noch Mutter. Gott sagt damit, dass es ohne das Verlassen kein Anhangen geben kann. Auch in Markus 10:7 lesen wir: „Aus diesem Grund wird ein Mann seinen Vater und seine Mutter verlassen und seiner Frau anhangen.“ Das ist Gottes Plan, und Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

Verlassen bedeutet, hinter sich zu lassen, aufzugeben. „Aus diesem Grund wird ein Mann seinen Vater und seine Mutter verlassen“ bedeutet, die Eltern hinter sich zu lassen. Denken wir an einen jungen Mann, der ein wirklich gutes Elternhaus hat. Er ist gesegnet und hat alles, was er braucht. Doch sobald Gott seine Eva in sein Leben bringt, regt sich etwas in ihm, und er sagt: „Ich gehe!“ Aber das ist Gottes Plan. Und Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

Er verlässt nicht nur seinen Vater und seine Mutter; er hängt auch seiner Frau an. Anhangen bedeutet „festkleben, haften“. Wir kennen verleimte Holzplatten sehr gut. Allerlei stabile Möbel werden aus miteinander verleimten Platten hergestellt. Und wenn sie richtig verleimt sind, werden sie an den Verbindungsstellen nicht auseinandergehen. Wenn man sie auseinanderreißt, muss man das Holz selbst zerreißen. Mit Gottes Leim ist es genauso, wenn er zwei Menschen miteinander verbindet. Man kann sie nur auseinanderreißen, indem man splittert und zerreißt, und das segnet Gott nicht. Aber verlassen und anhangen, zusammenbleiben und fest miteinander verbunden sein – das ist Gottes Plan, und es bringt Segen.

3) Sie werden ein Fleisch sein.

„Darum wird ein Mann seinen Vater und seine Mutter verlassen und seiner Frau anhangen; und sie werden ein Fleisch sein“ (1. Mose 2:24). Zwei unverheiratete Menschen, die ein Ehepaar werden, werden vor Gott eine Einheit und vor Gott eine Familie. Sie werden ein Fleisch, sodass Gott sie gemeinsam als eins sieht.

„Und die beiden werden ein Fleisch sein; so sind sie nun nicht mehr zwei, sondern ein Fleisch. Was nun Gott zusammengefügt hat, soll der Mensch nicht trennen“ (Markus 10:8-9). Gottes Plan für Mann und Frau ist, dass er Eva zu Adam bringt. Dann sollen das Verlassen und das Anhangen geschehen. Er bewirkt, dass sie ein Fleisch werden. Das Auseinanderreißen bringt überhaupt keinen Segen, sondern Qual, Schmerz, Mühsal und Verletzungen. In der Trennung liegt kein Segen. Aber Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

4) Kein ungleiches Joch.

„Zieht nicht in einem ungleichen Joch mit Ungläubigen; denn welche Gemeinschaft hat Gerechtigkeit mit Ungerechtigkeit?“ (2. Korinther 6:14-15). „Die Frau ist durch das Gesetz gebunden, solange ihr Mann lebt; wenn aber ihr Mann gestorben ist, ist sie frei, zu heiraten, wen sie will; nur im Herrn“ (1. Korinther 7:39).

Gottes Plan ist, dass die Ehe ein gleiches Joch ist. Gott wird einem Adam keine Eva für eine Ehe bringen, die ein ungleiches Joch ist. Denken wir an das Verlassen und Anhangen, an das feste Verbinden und daran, dass zwei eins werden. In der Ehe sind diese beiden nun vor Gott eins. Stellt euch vor, in einer solchen schlechten Ehebeziehung zu leben – eine solche Familie, die versucht, gemeinsam zu funktionieren. Da wird kein Segen sein.

Aber ein gleiches Joch bringt Segen! Gott möchte, dass wir zu einem Fleisch, einem Herzen und einem Sinn verbunden sind. Er möchte uns mit Herz, Sinn und Fleisch verbunden sehen – dass unser ganzes Wesen eins ist. Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

5) Gott hat vorgesehen, dass wir Kinder haben.

„Und Gott segnete sie, und Gott sprach zu ihnen: Seid fruchtbar und vermehrt euch und füllt die Erde und macht sie euch untertan; und herrscht über die Fische des Meeres und über die Vögel des Himmels und über jedes lebendige Wesen, das sich auf der Erde bewegt“ (1. Mose 1:28). Denkt an die Freude und das Wunder, jedes Mal wenn ein weiteres Kind in eine christliche Familie hineingeboren wird. Gott hat es so vorgesehen. Und wenn Gott Adam seine Eva gebracht hat und sie verlassen und anhangen, werden sie ein Fleisch, ein Herz, ein Sinn. Wenn sie in einem gleichen Joch verbunden sind und Gott sie mit Kindern segnet, wird ihr Zuhause zu einem freudigen Zufluchtsort, an dem Gott wohnen kann. „Und Gott segnete Noah und seine Söhne und sprach zu ihnen: Seid fruchtbar und vermehrt euch und füllt die Erde“ (1. Mose 9:1). „Und ihr, seid fruchtbar und vermehrt euch; bringt reichlich Nachkommen auf der Erde hervor und vermehrt euch auf ihr“ (1. Mose 9:7). Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

6) Die Ordnung der Hauptschaft.

„Ich möchte aber, dass ihr wisst, dass das Haupt jedes Mannes Christus ist; und das Haupt der Frau ist der Mann; und das Haupt Christi ist Gott“ (1. Korinther 11:3). Es ist Gott, dann Christus, der Mann und die Frau. Gott hat eine Ordnung der Hauptschaft eingesetzt, und diese Ordnung der Hauptschaft ist ein Segen. Sie ist Gottes Plan, und sie ist ein Segen.

„Kinder, gehorcht euren Eltern im Herrn; denn das ist recht. Ehre deinen Vater und deine Mutter; das ist das erste Gebot mit einer Verheißung: damit es dir gut geht und du lange auf der Erde lebst“ (Epheser 6:1-3). Kinder, euren Eltern im Herrn zu gehorchen ist ein Teil der Ordnung der Hauptschaft. Das ist nicht schwer zu verstehen, oder? Ein Zuhause, das Gottes Plan folgt, ist einfach ein gesegneter Ort. Ihr jungen Menschen, lernt, euch der Autorität unterzuordnen. Macht das zu einer hohen Priorität. Je früher ihr lernt, euch der Autorität unterzuordnen, desto besser werdet ihr auf die Verantwortungen im Leben vorbereitet sein.

Ich erinnere mich, wie ich auf das Eheleben blickte und mir wünschte, Kinder zu unterweisen und eine gottesfürchtige Familie aufzubauen. Ich hörte die Reihe „Godly Home“ und dachte, ich sei bereit, loszulegen. Aber dann kam der Tag, an dem ich an der Reihe war und die Verantwortung trug, und plötzlich wollte mein Herz verzagen. Verantwortung fühlt sich anders an, als davon zu träumen. DU musst etwas tun! DU bist verantwortlich. DU musst dafür sorgen, dass es geschieht. Und übrigens nicht nur irgendwie; du musst es auf eine Christus gemäße Weise tun. Du musst es so tun, dass die Salbung des Geistes Gottes auf deine Familie herabkommen kann. Je besser wir lernen, uns der Autorität unterzuordnen, desto besser werden wir auf diese Verantwortungen vorbereitet sein. Je mehr wir erkennen, dass wir Gott brauchen, desto besser steht es um uns. Machen wir es zu einer hohen Priorität, als Kinder und als junge Menschen zu lernen, uns der Autorität unterzuordnen. „Mein Sohn, vergiss meine Weisung nicht; sondern dein Herz bewahre meine Gebote. Denn viele Tage, ein langes Leben und Frieden werden sie dir hinzufügen“ (Sprüche 3:1-2).

Gott wird seinen Segen hinzufügen, wenn wir in dieser Ordnung der Hauptschaft bleiben. Je mehr ihr lernt, euch der Autorität unterzuordnen, desto mehr werdet ihr gesegnet sein, wenn ihr euer eigenes Zuhause gründet. Gottes Plan birgt Segen.

7) Eine gottgefällige Ehe.

Epheser 5:21,22,24 sagt: „Ordnet euch einander unter in der Furcht Gottes. Ihr Frauen, ordnet euch euren eigenen Männern unter wie dem Herrn. . . Wie nun die Gemeinde Christus untergeordnet ist, so sollen auch die Frauen ihren eigenen Männern in allem untergeordnet sein.“

Betrachtet zuerst Vers 21: „Ordnet euch einander unter.“ In einem gottgefälligen Zuhause muss ein Zusammenwachsen stattfinden. Dieses Zusammenwachsen soll in der Furcht Gottes geschehen. Wenn wir uns einander in der Furcht Gottes unterordnen, werden wir Gott gehorchen, weil wir seinen Segen wollen.

Epheser 5:22,24: „Ihr Frauen, ordnet euch euren eigenen Männern unter wie dem Herrn. . . Wie nun die Gemeinde Christus untergeordnet ist, so sollen auch die Frauen ihren eigenen Männern in allem untergeordnet sein.“ Ihr jungen Frauen, darauf könnt ihr zählen: Sich dem Vater unterzuordnen ist gleichbedeutend mit der Unterordnung unter einen Ehemann. Ihr könnt üben, solange ihr unverheiratet seid. Das wird euch helfen, euren Charakter zu bilden. Eine rebellische und widerspenstige Frau zu sein wird nicht den Segen Gottes bringen.

Weiter heißt es in Epheser 5:25,28,29: „Ihr Männer, liebt eure Frauen, wie auch Christus die Gemeinde geliebt und sich selbst für sie hingegeben hat . . . So sollen die Männer ihre Frauen lieben wie ihren eigenen Leib. Wer seine Frau liebt, liebt sich selbst. Denn niemand hat je sein eigenes Fleisch gehasst, sondern er nährt und pflegt es, wie auch der Herr die Gemeinde.“ Ihr jungen Männer, hier steht, dass Ehemänner ihre Frauen lieben sollen. Wen hat Gott wohl in euer Leben gestellt, um euch darauf vorzubereiten, eure Frau zu lieben? Eure Mutter! Wollt ihr lernen, eure Frau zu lieben? Lernt, mit eurer Mutter auszukommen, sie zu lieben und euch um sie zu kümmern. Wollt ihr üben, eure zukünftige Frau zu lieben? Dann fangt damit an, eure Mutter zu lieben.

Vers 33: „Doch soll jeder Einzelne von euch seine Frau so lieben wie sich selbst; die Frau aber soll darauf achten, ihren Mann zu ehren.“ Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

8) Gemeinsam Erben der Gnade des Lebens sein.

1. Petrus 3:7: „Ebenso ihr Männer, lebt mit ihnen verständnisvoll zusammen und erweist der Frau Ehre als dem schwächeren Gefäß und als gemeinsamen Erben der Gnade des Lebens, damit eure Gebete nicht behindert werden.“ Als Ehemänner erweisen wir der Frau Ehre. Sie ist das schwächere Gefäß und diejenige, die die Kinder geboren hat! Sie hat in ihrem Leben viele einschneidende Veränderungen durchgemacht. Sie ist diejenige, die erschöpft wird und schneller müde wird.

Und er sagt: „Ihr Männer, lebt mit ihnen verständnisvoll zusammen.“

Ihr jungen Männer, lernt, eure Mutter und eure Schwestern zu verstehen. Das wird euch helfen, wenn ihr verheiratet seid. Sagt nicht einfach: „Ach, so sind Frauen eben.“ Nein, ihr wollt den Segen Gottes. Lernt, sie zu kennen und zu verstehen.

„Gemeinsame Erben der Gnade des Lebens sein.“ Gott möchte, dass wir gemeinsam Erben der Gnade des Lebens sind. Wenn wir nicht gemeinsam Erben der Gnade des Lebens sind, können wir dann getrennt Erben der Gnade des Lebens sein? Ich glaube nicht. Er sagt, wir sollen gemeinsam Erben sein, damit unsere Gebete nicht behindert werden. Könnten wir also sagen, dass unsere Gebete behindert werden, wenn wir getrennt Erben sind? Ja, unsere Gebete werden behindert werden. Erweisen wir der Frau Ehre als dem schwächeren Gefäß. Jedes noch so kleine Stück, das ihr auf diesem Gebiet vorankommt, wird euch später nur zum Segen sein. Es lohnt sich. Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

9) Ein gesegnetes und geborgenes Zuhause.

Das ergibt sich zum Teil aus 1. Petrus 3:7, aber auch aus Psalm 144:12: „Dass unsere Söhne in ihrer Jugend wie herangewachsene Pflanzen seien; dass unsere Töchter wie Ecksteine seien, nach dem Vorbild eines Palastes behauen.“ Die Gnade Gottes ruht auf einem geborgenen Zuhause, in dem Einheit herrscht. Wo der Vater die Mutter versteht, wo der Vater sich um die Mutter kümmert. Der Vater dient und ist da, um zu helfen und zu führen. Er ist da, um mit einem mitfühlenden Herzen Orientierung zu geben. Gottes Plan für Mann und Frau – Gottes Plan bringt Segen.

10) Wie Christus und die Gemeinde.

„Wie nun die Gemeinde Christus untergeordnet ist, so sollen auch die Frauen ihren eigenen Männern in allem untergeordnet sein. Ihr Männer, liebt eure Frauen, wie auch Christus die Gemeinde geliebt und sich selbst für sie hingegeben hat, damit er sie heilige und reinige durch das Wasserbad im Wort, damit er sie sich selbst als eine herrliche Gemeinde darstelle, die keinen Flecken oder Runzel oder etwas dergleichen hat, sondern heilig und ohne Makel ist. So sollen die Männer ihre Frauen lieben wie ihren eigenen Leib. Wer seine Frau liebt, liebt sich selbst. Denn niemand hat je sein eigenes Fleisch gehasst, sondern er nährt und pflegt es, wie auch der Herr die Gemeinde“ (Epheser 5:24-29).

„Ihr Männer, liebt eure Frauen, wie auch Christus die Gemeinde geliebt und sich selbst für sie hingegeben hat.“ Gott sucht Männer, die bereit sind, ihr Leben hinzugeben. Unverheiratete junge Männer, die bereit sind, dem Ruf zu folgen und ihr Leben hinzugeben. Das ist eine hohe Berufung Gottes. Es ist Gottes Plan.

Ihr jungen Männer, seid ihr bereit, euer Leben, eure eigenen Pläne und die Dinge, die ihr gern unabhängig tut, hinzugeben? Seid ihr bereit, geduldig, sanft und verständnisvoll zu sein? Seid ihr bereit, auf Schlaf zu verzichten und weiterzumachen, auch wenn ihr müde seid? Seid ihr bereit, in belastenden Situationen ruhig zu bleiben und nicht aufbrausend zu reagieren? Seid ihr bereit, eine Frau und Kinder, ewige Seelen, durch dieses Leben zu führen und zu leiten?

Meine Bitte ist aber, dass ihr euch freiwillig meldet und sagt: „Ich bin bereit, mich dem Wort Gottes, dem Willen Gottes und dem Plan Gottes zu widmen, und ich werde mein Leben hingeben. Ich bin bereit, es auf den Altar zu legen.“ Jesus gab sein Leben für uns, und er vergleicht die Ehe mit der Beziehung zwischen der Gemeinde und ihm.

Es werden auch Mütter gebraucht, die sich unterordnen und der Autorität fügen. Mütter, die nicht der Frauenbefreiungsbewegung unserer Zeit folgen, sondern vielmehr zufrieden sind, sich um Haushalt und Zuhause zu kümmern.

Ihr jungen Frauen, seid ihr bereit, euch zu melden? Wollt ihr euer Herz hingeben, um geführt und geleitet zu werden? Seid ihr bereit, zu folgen und euch freudig der Autorität unterzuordnen, unter der ihr steht? Seid ihr bereit, zu dienen und euch für eure Familie aufzuopfern? Seid ihr bereit, zu dienen und euch für EURE Familie aufzuopfern? Wenn ihr eines Tages heiratet, wird es EURE Familie sein, der ihr dient und für die ihr euch aufopfert. Seid ihr bereit, Schmerzen und Beschwerden zu ertragen? Seid ihr bereit, eine ihm entsprechende Hilfe zu sein und euch für seine Last und seine Vision hinzugeben?

Wenn wir Gottes Plan und seinen Segen betrachten: Ihr jungen Menschen wollt doch Gottes Segen! Aber das bedeutet, dass ihr entsprechende Entscheidungen treffen müsst. Macht euch auf und trefft Entscheidungen, die zur Reife führen. Reife entsteht im Prozess des Suchens nach Gott. Fasst in eurem Herzen den festen Entschluss, euch Gottes Segen und seinen Grundsätzen zu öffnen. Ich ermutige euch, mit Gott zu wandeln, eine Beziehung zu Jesus Christus zu haben und dies in Demut zu tun.

Strebt nach einem Christus gemäßen Charakter, und tut es bewusst. Es fällt uns so leicht, das Leben einfach so zu leben, wie es sich gerade ergibt. Aber wenn wir bewusst Entscheidungen treffen, werden sie uns voranbringen! Diese Entscheidungen sind wichtig. Handelt nach Gottes Plan.

Gott hat einen Plan für Mann und Frau, und er hat einen Plan für euch.

Circumstantial overload might be the most difficult. We can choose not to go to a Norwex party if we need to give our schedule some space. But if a child breaks a leg in the middle of wedding preparations, we have no choice other than to make the best of the situation.

Circumstantial overload may happen slowly, as in the following story, or it may happen quickly as in the case of an accident in which a family member is injured.

Becky is in her thirties with seven children under seventeen. A few years ago, one of their chicken houses burned down. At the time, they were thankful that the chickens had left the day before and that no one was close by when the propane tank exploded.

“My husband faced the disaster like a man,” says Becky. “His calm spirit helped me relax. I felt certain that we could make the financial adjustments and life would go on as before. But I was wrong. Very wrong.”

“In time the mess was cleaned up, and Rick looked into rebuilding. The quotes were higher than expected, so he opted to do some of the work himself. He also took on a part-time job to provide more income. Our boys were old enough to help, yet they couldn’t do much without Rick’s direction.”

“I first felt the adjustment in my wallet, but I consoled myself that this was only temporary. Then the spark in Rick’s eyes was replaced with a dull stare. He became distant from us. I knew something wasn’t right, but I couldn’t put my finger on it.”

“Then he was elected to finish the last four months of secretarial duties for a brother who spent some time in Bulgaria. That night he came home and wept. ‘Doesn’t anyone understand what I’m going through? Every time I turn around, there is something to do. The boys want to go fishing, you need a new clothesline, and the chicken house needs to be finished in six months! I am not mentally capable of handling one more duty.’”

“That was the straw that broke the camel’s back,” Becky said. “I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”

“It was clear to me that my perfectionist husband was overloaded. More and more Rick leaned on me. I cut back on my commitments and tried to keep my time free so that I was available to help lessen his load.”

“I felt like a lifeguard trying to keep a man from drowning while taking in a bit too much water myself. Many of the home-life responsibilities fell on my shoulders. Then I was asked to fill the position of food committee for Mrs. ‘Going-to-Bulgaria.’”

Unfortunately, circumstantial stress is often unnoticed. Worse yet, the victim can be misunderstood or misjudged. Becky said, “My darkest day came when I was accused of being selfish with my time because I declined the food committee request.”

Prolonged overload can be emotionally and mentally damaging

Intense, long-lasting pressures or troubles shouldered alone can cause severe stress. Minor stress is normal, but prolonged stress can cause depression, anxiety, heart disease, and high blood pressure. How you handle prolonged stress is important.

Sometimes this type of overload is not public knowledge. Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates. At the same time, other saints are suffering deeply on the sidelines with little recognition or financial aid. It could be strained relationships or little bills that add up to a big sum. Betrayal and rejection cause stress beyond measure. There are no quick fixes to circumstantial stress, but little sparks of light can help you navigate the darkness.

Talk about your situation with someone you trust

Sometimes just talking about problems can help you to put issues in perspective. Hearing yourself verbalize a stressful situation somehow clears brain fog and gives a clearer path forward.

Find routine

When stress prevails, racing thoughts, forgetfulness, and inability to focus comes uninvited. Having a routine can bring some rhythm to your mental well-being. The smallest normalcy brings a moment of pleasure, and it is soothing to the soul.

Intentionally seek a breather

Lingering stress can cause agitation, moodiness, and the desire to take control. Sometimes it is hard to think beyond mental fog, but it is so important to find refreshment for your mental wellbeing. Stress hormones can speed up your heart rate and tighten your blood vessels. That temporarily raises your blood pressure. The opposite happens when you relax. Being relaxed helps you have a calmer, clearer mind which improves your concentration and decision-making.

Believe that God cares

Say it. Read the Psalms over and over. Listen to good music. Take short walks and pray aloud. Keep your eyes on Jesus. Believe “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

If you are facing circumstantial overload, be patient and realistic. God will make a way for you. Many times, He opens doors just when we are running out of options. He will supply the needed grace for that hour. And the next hour. And the next. At times, surprising opportunities come, and prayers are answered in unexpected ways. However He chooses to work on your behalf, hold to His unchanging hand.

Regardless of the type of overload you might be encountering, turn to your Heavenly Father.

Ask Him for direction and wisdom. And say with the Psalmist, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).

Omstandigheidsoorlading is dalk die moeilikste. Ons kan kies om nie na ’n Norwex-partytjie te gaan as ons ons skedule ’n bietjie asemruimte moet gee nie. Maar as ’n kind sy been breek te midde van trouvoorbereidings, het ons geen ander keuse as om die beste van die situasie te maak nie.

Omstandigheidsoorlading kan stadig gebeur, soos in die volgende verhaal, of dit kan vinnig gebeur, soos in die geval van ’n ongeluk waarin ’n familielid beseer word.

Becky is in haar dertigs en het sewe kinders onder die ouderdom van sewentien. ’n Paar jaar gelede het een van hulle hoenderhuise afgebrand. Destyds was hulle dankbaar dat die hoenders die dag tevore weg is en dat niemand naby was toe die propaantenk ontplof het nie.

“My man het die ramp soos ’n man aangepak,” sê Becky. “Sy kalm geaardheid het my gehelp om te ontspan. Ek was seker dat ons die finansiële aanpassings kon maak en dat die lewe soos voorheen sou voortgaan. Maar ek was verkeerd. Baie verkeerd.”

“Mettertyd is die gemors opgeruim, en Rick het ondersoek ingestel na herbou. Die prysramings was hoër as verwag, daarom het hy besluit om van die werk self te doen. Hy het ook ’n deeltydse werk aanvaar om meer inkomste te verdien. Ons seuns was oud genoeg om te help, maar sonder Rick se leiding kon hulle nie veel doen nie.”

“Ek het die aanpassing eers in my beursie gevoel, maar ek het myself getroos met die gedagte dat dit net tydelik was. Toe is die vonkel in Rick se oë vervang deur ’n dowwe staar. Hy het van ons begin onttrek. Ek het geweet iets is nie reg nie, maar ek kon nie my vinger daarop lê nie.”

“Toe is hy gekies om die laaste vier maande se sekretariële pligte waar te neem vir ’n broer wat ’n ruk in Bulgarye sou deurbring. Daardie aand het hy huis toe gekom en gehuil. ‘Verstaan niemand waardeur ek gaan nie? Elke keer as ek omdraai, is daar iets om te doen. Die seuns wil gaan visvang, jy het ’n nuwe wasgoedlyn nodig, en die hoenderhuis moet binne ses maande klaar wees! Ek is verstandelik nie in staat om nog ’n plig te hanteer nie.’”

“Dit was die strooi wat die kameel se rug gebreek het,” sê Becky. “Ek het bekommerd geraak toe ek hom in die middel van die nag hoor gaap en besef dat hy nie slaap nie.”

“Dit was vir my duidelik dat my perfeksionistiese man oorlaai was. Rick het al hoe meer op my gesteun. Ek het my verpligtinge verminder en probeer om my tyd oop te hou sodat ek beskikbaar was om sy las te help verlig.”

“Ek het gevoel soos ’n lewensredder wat probeer keer dat ’n man verdrink, terwyl ek self ’n bietjie te veel water insluk. Baie van die verantwoordelikhede by die huis het op my skouers geval. Toe is ek gevra om die pos in die voedselkomitee vir mev. ‘Gaan-na-Bulgarye’ te vul.”

Ongelukkig bly omstandigheidsverwante stres dikwels onopgemerk. Nog erger, die slagoffer kan misverstaan of verkeerd beoordeel word. Becky sê: “My donkerste dag het aangebreek toe ek daarvan beskuldig is dat ek selfsugtig met my tyd is omdat ek die versoek om op die voedselkomitee te dien, van die hand gewys het.”

Langdurige oorlading kan emosioneel en verstandelik skadelik wees

Intense, langdurige druk of probleme wat ’n mens alleen dra, kan ernstige stres veroorsaak. ’n Bietjie stres is normaal, maar langdurige stres kan depressie, angs, hartsiektes en hoë bloeddruk veroorsaak. Hoe jy langdurige stres hanteer, is belangrik.

Soms is hierdie soort oorlading nie algemeen bekend nie. Traumatiese gebeure in ons gewone kringe kry dikwels gebed, finansiële hulp en weeklikse begrotingsopdaterings. Terselfdertyd ly ander gelowiges diep aan die kantlyn, met min erkenning of finansiële hulp. Dit kan gespanne verhoudings wees of klein rekeninge wat saam ’n groot bedrag uitmaak. Verraad en verwerping veroorsaak stres wat nie gemeet kan word nie. Daar is geen kitsoplossings vir omstandigheidsverwante stres nie, maar klein vonkies lig kan jou help om deur die duisternis te kom.

Praat oor jou situasie met iemand wat jy vertrou

Soms kan dit help om net oor probleme te praat, sodat jy sake in perspektief kan plaas. Om jouself ’n stresvolle situasie hardop te hoor verwoord, help op die een of ander manier om die breinmis te verdryf en gee ’n duideliker pad vorentoe.

Vind ’n roetine

Wanneer stres oorheers, kom jaende gedagtes, vergeetagtigheid en die onvermoë om te fokus ongenooid. ’n Roetine kan ’n bietjie ritme aan jou geestelike welstand gee. Selfs die kleinste stukkie normaliteit bring ’n oomblik van plesier en is balsem vir die siel.

Soek doelbewus ’n blaaskans

Aanhoudende stres kan prikkelbaarheid, buierigheid en die begeerte om beheer te neem veroorsaak. Soms is dit moeilik om verder as die breinmis te dink, maar dit is baie belangrik om verkwikking vir jou geestelike welstand te vind. Streshormone kan jou hartklop versnel en jou bloedvate vernou. Dit verhoog jou bloeddruk tydelik. Die teenoorgestelde gebeur wanneer jy ontspan. Ontspanning help jou om ’n rustiger, helderder gemoed te hê, wat jou konsentrasie en besluitneming verbeter.

Glo dat God omgee

Sê dit. Lees die Psalms oor en oor. Luister na goeie musiek. Gaan stap kort entjies en bid hardop. Hou jou oë op Jesus. Glo: “Die geween mag ’n nag duur, maar die vreugde kom in die môre” (Psalm 30:5).

As jy omstandigheidsoorlading ervaar, wees geduldig en realisties. God sal vir jou ’n uitweg maak. Dikwels maak Hy deure oop net wanneer ons besig is om sonder opsies te raak. Hy sal die nodige genade vir daardie uur voorsien. En vir die volgende uur. En die volgende. Soms duik verrassende geleenthede op en word gebede op onverwagte maniere verhoor. Hoe Hy ook al kies om vir jou te werk, hou vas aan Sy onveranderlike hand.

Ongeag die soort oorlading waarmee jy te kampe het, wend jou tot jou Hemelse Vader.

Vra Hom om leiding en wysheid. En sê saam met die Psalmis: “Op U, HERE, vertrou ek; laat my nooit beskaamd staan nie” (Psalm 71:1).

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

Tidspresset i siste liten er noe mange hjemmeværende ofte må forholde seg til. Uansett hvor organiserte vi er, utsetter vi noen ganger oppgaver fordi vi misliker dem eller venter til vi står under press.

Vanemessig utsettelse kan føre til høyere stressnivåer. Kanskje jeg er merkelig, men det er vanskelig for meg å holde meg rolig når presset øker. Når oppgavene som skulle gjøres i siste liten, endelig er fullført, er jeg for utslitt til å nyte det planlagte arrangementet.

Tannverk og bilturer

Det er et mysterium for meg hvorfor et familiemedlem havner i tannlegestolen en dag eller to før vi drar på tur. Kanskje det ikke har skjedd så ofte som jeg tror, men frustrasjonen over et uventet besøk hos tannlegen på et ugunstig tidspunkt sitter fast i minnet. Nå setter jeg av tid til en tenkt tannlegetime før en reise. Hvis det ikke er en tannlegekrise, vil et annet problem sannsynligvis fylle det tidsrommet.

Frister er en normal del av livet. Uten dem ville vi mangle motivasjon, og dagene våre ville mangle mening. Avbrudd er også en normal del av livet. De gir stadig dagene og ukene våre uforutsigbare vendinger. Hvis vi lar for mange oppgaver vente til siste liten, kolliderer avbrudd og frister, og kaos råder.

Endre situasjonen i siste liten

Frister og avbrudd kan ikke fjernes, men vi kan begrense oppgavene vi gjør i siste liten. Noen ganger må vi se ærlig tilbake for å finne ut hva som forårsaket stresset vårt. Ofte skylder vi på avbrudd og innser ikke at dårlig planlegging eller utsettelse kan ha vært årsaken.

For eksempel, hvis gjester kommer og vi planlegger å vaske vinduer og lage dessert, i tillegg til et dusin andre oppgaver, på ankomstdagen, er det ikke rom for forstyrrelser. Av erfaring vet vi at avbrudd vil komme. Så er det ikke bedre å «planlegge» for et vepsestikk og en forslått tå?

Hvorfor ikke planlegge vindusvask og dessert til en annen dag? Det kan bety noen fingeravtrykk på vinduene og en enklere dessert, men er ikke det bedre enn mye stress i siste liten?

Gjør noen oppgaver på forhånd

Å bestemme tidlig på dagen hva du skal lage til middag og pakke stellevesken på forhånd er små ting som kan gjøre stor forskjell når det nærmer seg. Da barna våre var små, begynte jeg å pakke koffertene en dag før en reise i stedet for på avreisedagen. Jeg taklet hastverket i siste liten bedre hvis den oppgaven var unnagjort.

Gjør de viktigste oppgavene først

Denne tilnærmingen gir frihet til å hoppe over mindre viktige gjøremål når tiden blir knapp.

Noen ganger er ikke alt på oppgavelisten like viktig. Det er vanskelig for en perfeksjonist å droppe en oppgave, men det er mulig å utvikle nye vaner.

Del arbeidet opp i mindre biter

Noen ganger gjør omfanget av en oppgave at den virker for stor til å gå i gang med. Del den store oppgaven opp i mindre deler. Det er mye mer overkommelig å fullføre en mindre oppgave. Grundig rengjøring av kjøkkenet er en oppgave jeg ikke liker. Hvis planleggeren min sier «rengjør kjøkkenet grundig», er det lett å overse.

Men hvis planleggeren min sier «rengjør hvitevarene, tørk av innsiden av skapene og vask vinduene», virker det mer gjennomførbart.

Det er så mange gledelige hendelser i livet; hvorfor la utsettelse være til bry? Gi deg selv friheten til å leve livet annerledes. Noen få små endringer kan utgjøre den største forskjellen mellom en velsignet og en stressende siste liten.

A Christ-centered Courtship is a series of messages on godly courtship preached by Paul Hershberger. He preached these messages several times at different locations over the last ten years. Recently, we had them transcribed and abridged for reading clarity. After printing all six articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, we will publish them in a booklet. This is the first article of six.

Introduction

My wife and I had the privilege of having a courtship without regrets or guilt. We were blessed with parents who guided us in the right way and gave us opportunities that they didn’t have.

If you don’t have that testimony or memory, please don’t go on a guilt trip. But my prayer for you is that you get a burning burden and vision in your heart to have it for your children. That can be your reward.

A Christ-centered courtship is a period of time between a single life and a married life. The decisions you make in this period will affect you for the rest of your lives. With God’s blessing on your life, you can end up with no regrets or guilt.

Five goals for this Christ-Centered Courtship series.

Goal #1. To turn the hearts of the fathers to their children.

Goal #2. To turn the hearts of the children to their fathers.

Goal #3. That parents would get a burden to lead each one of their children into the perfect will of God for their lives.

Goal #4. That young people would get a burden to seek after God, find fulfillment and purpose in walking with God, and you would seek maturity in your manners and in your character.

Goal #5. That young men and young women would rise up to be godly fathers and godly mothers with a vision to raise up another godly generation, and the Gospel of Jesus Christ can go on.

God’s Plan for Male and Female

Ecclesiastes 12:1 says, “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.” My desire is that each one of you, remember your Creator in the days of your youth. Turn your heart, your focus, and your life to pursue after your Creator, Almighty God, in heaven.

What does he mean, “while the evil days come not” and “the years draw nigh”? It means to seek the Lord when you’re young. Take the energy of your youth and seek after God. Young people, you’re young and full of ideas, visions, plans, and dreams. I doubt there are any of you who just enjoy sitting down in an easy chair, putting your feet up, and just dreaming about how terrible and horrible life is going to be. We don’t do that, do we? But if we don’t walk with God and follow God’s plan, hard things will come upon us. When hard things come in life, we have no place to turn to. We dream that life will turn out well. The decisions and actions in our youth affect us for the rest of our lives. The good news is they can affect us in a good way. The bad news is they can affect us in a bad way. It depends on what decisions and choices we make. But young people, you’re young, and you have the opportunity to choose.

Let’s go to the beginning of Genesis.

“And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:18-24).

“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:26-28).

“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (Genesis 2:18). “I’ll make him an help that is meet for him.” God said He would do that.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Genesis 1:27). God made. God created us male and female. It takes a lot of blind faith to believe that we evolved perfectly as male and female. The creation of male and female is God’s plan. It is one of the living proofs of Creation. God made. God created. It’s God’s plan. God is the Author. And God’s plan brings blessing.

I’d like to look at ten different aspects of this blessing of God’s plan.

1) God brings Eve to Adam.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man” (Genesis 2:22-23).

God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep. Then God created Eve and brought her to Adam. Adam awoke and realized, “This one is for me!” He had seen all the animals go by when he named them. Now God brings him someone that is for him. He also realized, “She was taken out of my side.” She’s close to his heart. “This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.” It’s not a dog; it’s not a giraffe, or a monkey, or an ape. This one that God brought to him is like him. God’s plan has a blessing.

Adam and Eve had never had a companion before. Adam and Eve had never let the emotions of their heart go before. Something happened in Adam and Eve’s hearts. Adam was a “one-woman man,” and Eve was a “one-man woman.” They never gave their heart passions to anybody else. God has that plan for us, too. God’s plan brings blessings.

2) Leaving and cleaving in unity for life.

“Therefore Bshall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

This verse says, “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother,” but Adam and Eve did not have a father and mother. What God is saying it doesn’t work for there to be cleaving unless there’s leaving. Also, in Mark 10:7, we read, “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife.” This is God’s plan, and God’s plan brings blessing.

Leaving means to leave behind, to abandon. “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother” is to leave parents leave behind. Let’s consider a young man who has a really good home life. He’s blessed and has everything he needs. Yet once God brings his Eve into his life, something rises up inside him, and he says, “I’m leaving!” But this is God’s plan. And God’s plan brings blessing.

It’s not just leaving his father and mother; he also cleaves to his wife. Cleave means “to glue to, to adhere.” We are very familiar with glued wood panels. All kinds of solid furniture are made out of panels glued together. And if they’re glued together right, they will not come apart at the joints. If you tear them apart, you’re going to have to tear the wood apart. God’s glue is the same way, where it glues two people together. The only way to tear them apart is by splintering and ripping and God does not bless that. But leaving and cleaving, staying together and being glued together, that’s God’s plan and it brings blessing.

3) They shall be one flesh.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). Two single people who become one married couple, become one unit before God, and become one family before God. They become one flesh, where God sees them as together as one.

“And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder” (Mark 10:8-9). God’s plan for male and female is that He brings Eve to Adam. Then the leaving and cleaving to take place. He causes them to become one flesh. Pulling apart is no blessing at all but bringsagony,pain,travail, and hurt. There is no blessing in separation. But God’s plan brings blessing.

4) Not an unequal yoke.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness” (2 Corinthians 6:14-15). “The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 7:39).

God’s plan is that marriage is an equal yoke. God will not bring an Eve to an Adam in a marriage that is an unequal yoke.Let’s think about leaving and cleaving, getting glued together, and two becoming one. In marriage, those two are now one before God. Imagine being in a bad marriage relationship like this—a family like this trying to function together. There will be no blessing.

But an equal yoke brings blessing! God desires that we be joined together in one flesh, one heart, and one mind. He wants to see us joined in heart, mind, and fleashthe whole being, being one. God’s plan brings blessing.

5) God planned for us to have children.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:28). Think of the joy and miracle every time another child is born into a Christian home. God planned it this way. And if God brought Adam his Eve, and they leave and cleave, they become one flesh, one heart, one mind. If they are equally yoked and God blesses them with children, it becomes a joyful haven where God can dwell. “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” (Genesis 9:1). “And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein” (Genesis 9:7). God’s plan brings blessing.

6) Headship order.

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1 Corinthians 11:3). It is God, and then Christ, the man, and the woman. God established a headship order, and this headship order is a blessing. It’s God’s plan, and it’s a blessing.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honor thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth” (Ephesians 6:1-3). . Children, obey your parents in the Lord is a part of the headship order. This not difficult to understand, is it? A home following the plan of God is just a blessed situation. Young people learn to be under authority. Make that your high priority. The sooner you learn to be under authority, the better you will be prepared for the responsibilities in life.

I remember looking at married life and having aspirations about teaching children and raising a godly family. I listened to the “Godly Home” series and thought I was ready to go. But then the day came when it was my turn and my responsibility, and all of a sudden, my heart wanted to wither. Responsibility doesn’t feel the same as dreaming about it does. YOU need to do something! YOU are responsible. YOU need to make it happen. And, by the way, not just make it happen; you need to make it happen in a Christlike way. You need to make it happen in a way that the anointing of the Spirit of God can come down on your family. The better we learn how to be under authority, the better we’ll be prepared for those responsibilities. The more we realize we need God, the better off we are. Let’s make a high priority out of learning to be under authority as children and as young people. “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee” (Proverbs 3:1-2).

God will add his blessing if we stay in this headship order. The more you learn how to be under authority, the more you will be blessed when you establish your home. God’s plan has blessings.

7) A godly marriage.

Ephesians 5:21,22,24 says, “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.”

First of all look at verse 21, “submitting yourselves one to another.” There’s a blending together that needs to happen in a godly home. This blending together should happen in the fear of God. If we’re submitting one to another in the fear of God, we’re going to obey God because we want His blessings.

Ephesians 5: 22, 24 “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Young ladies, you can count on it: submission to Dad equals submission to a husband. You can practice while you are single. This will help build character in your life. Being a rebellious and froward woman is not going to bring the blessing of God.

It goes on and says, in Ephesians 5:25,28,29. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it . . . So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” Young men, this says that husbands should love their wives. So who do you think God put in your life to prepare you to love your wife? Your mother! Do you want to learn how to love your wife? Learn how to get along with your mom, love your mom, and care about her. Do you want to practice to love your future wife? Go ahead and love your mom.

Verse 33, “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” God’s plan brings blessings.

8) Being heirs together of the grace of life.

1 Peter 3:7 “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.” As husbands, we give honor to the wife. She is the weaker vessel and the one that born the children! She’s gone through a lot of traumatic changes in her life. She’s the one that gets worn out and tires sooner.

And he says, “Husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge.”

Young men, learn to understand your mom and your sisters. It will help you after you get married. Don’t conclude that—ah, that’s just women. No, you want the blessing of God. Learn to know and understand them.

“Being heirs together of the grace of life.” God wants us to be heirs together of the grace of life. If we’re not heirs together of the grace of life, can we be heirs separated of the grace of life? I don’t think so. He says we should be heirs together so that our prayers are not hindered. So if we’re heirs separated, could we say our prayers will be hindered? Yes, our prayers will be hindered. Let’s give honor unto the wife as unto the weaker vessel. Every ounce you can gain in this area will only bless you later. It’s worth it. God’s plan brings blessing.

9) A blessed and secure home.

This comes partly out of 1 Peter 3:7, but also from Psalm 144:12 “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.” The grace of God is on a secure home where there is unity. Where Dad is understanding Mom, where Dad cares about Mom. Dad is ministering and is there to help and guide. He’s there to give direction with a heart of compassion. God’s plan for male and female—God’s plan brings blessings.

10) As Christ and the church.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church” (Ephesians 5:24-29).

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave Himself for it.” God is looking for men who are willing to give their lives. Single young men, who are willing to answer the call and give their life. This is a high calling of God. It’s the plan of God.

Young men, are you willing to lay down your life, your agenda, and those independent things you like to do? Are you willing to be patient, gentle, and understanding? Are you willing to lose sleep and keep going even when you’re tired? Are you willing to stay calm and not react in stressful circumstances? Are you willing to lead and guide a wife and children, eternal souls, through this life?

But my plea is that you would volunteer and say, “I’m willing to apply myself to the Word of God, the will of God, the plan of God, and I’ll give my life. I’m willing to lay it on the altar.” Jesus gave His life for us, and He’s comparing the marriage with the church and Him.

There’s also a need for mothers who are submissive and yielded to authority. Mothers who do not follow the women’s lib of our day but are rather content to be keepers at home.

Young ladies, are you willing to enlist? Will you give your heart to be guided and led? Are you willing to follow and to cheerfully submit to your authority? Are you willing to serve and be spent for your family? Are you willing to serve and be spent for YOUR family? If you get married someday, it will be YOUR family that you’ll be serving and being spent for. Are you willing to bear pain and discomfort? Are you willing to be a helpmeet, giving yourself for his burden and vision?

But as we look at God’s plan and blessings, you want God’s blessing, young people! But that means you need to make choices accordingly. Rise up and make decisions that will lead to maturity. Maturity comes with the process of seeking after God. Make a commitment in your heart to open yourself to God’s blessings and principles. I encourage you to walk with God, to have a relationship with Jesus Christ, and to do so in humility.

Seek after Christlike character, and do it on purpose. It is so easy for us to just live life however it happens. But if we make decisions on purpose, it will take us somewhere! Those decisions matter. Do things according to God’s plan.

God has a plan for male and female and he has a plan for you.

Um Cortejo Centrado em Cristo é uma série de mensagens sobre o cortejo piedoso, pregadas por Paul Hershberger. Ele pregou essas mensagens várias vezes em diferentes locais ao longo dos últimos dez anos. Recentemente, nós as transcrevemos e resumimos para facilitar a leitura. Depois de publicar todos os seis artigos em O Pulsar do Remanescente, nós os publicaremos em um livreto. Este é o primeiro de seis artigos.

Introdução

Minha esposa e eu tivemos o privilégio de passar por um cortejo sem arrependimentos nem culpa. Fomos abençoados com pais que nos guiaram pelo caminho certo e nos deram oportunidades que eles mesmos não tiveram.

Se você não tem esse testemunho ou essa lembrança, por favor, não se culpe. Mas minha oração por você é que receba no coração um ardente senso de responsabilidade e uma visão: que você possa proporcionar isso aos seus filhos. Essa pode ser a sua recompensa.

Um cortejo centrado em Cristo é um período entre a vida de solteiro e a vida de casado. As decisões que você tomar nesse período vão afetá-lo pelo resto da vida. Com a bênção de Deus sobre sua vida, você pode chegar ao fim sem arrependimentos nem culpa.

Cinco objetivos desta série sobre o cortejo centrado em Cristo.

Objetivo nº 1. Voltar o coração dos pais para seus filhos.

Objetivo nº 2. Voltar o coração dos filhos para seus pais.

Objetivo nº 3. Que os pais recebam o encargo de conduzir cada um de seus filhos à perfeita vontade de Deus para a vida deles.

Objetivo nº 4. Que os jovens recebam o encargo de buscar a Deus, encontrar realização e propósito em andar com Deus e buscar maturidade em seus modos e em seu caráter.

Objetivo nº 5. Que os jovens homens e as jovens mulheres se levantem para ser pais e mães piedosos, com a visão de criar outra geração piedosa, para que o Evangelho de Jesus Cristo continue sendo anunciado.

O plano de Deus para o homem e a mulher

Eclesiastes 12:1 diz: “Lembra-te do teu Criador nos dias da tua mocidade, antes que venham os dias maus, e cheguem os anos dos quais dirás: Não tenho neles prazer.” Meu desejo é que cada um de vocês se lembre do seu Criador nos dias da juventude. Voltem o coração, o foco e a vida para buscar o seu Criador, o Deus Todo-Poderoso, no céu.

O que ele quer dizer com “antes que venham os dias maus” e “cheguem os anos”? Significa buscar o Senhor quando se é jovem. Usem a energia da juventude e busquem a Deus. Jovens, vocês são jovens e estão cheios de ideias, visões, planos e sonhos. Duvido que algum de vocês goste simplesmente de sentar numa poltrona, pôr os pés para cima e ficar sonhando com o quanto a vida será terrível e horrível. Nós não fazemos isso, fazemos? Mas, se não andarmos com Deus e não seguirmos o plano de Deus, coisas difíceis nos sobrevirão. Quando coisas difíceis acontecem na vida, não temos para onde nos voltar. Sonhamos que a vida dará certo. As decisões e ações tomadas na juventude nos afetam pelo resto da vida. A boa notícia é que podem nos afetar de maneira positiva. A má notícia é que podem nos afetar de maneira negativa. Tudo depende das decisões e escolhas que fazemos. Mas, jovens, vocês são jovens e têm a oportunidade de escolher.

Vamos ao princípio, em Gênesis.

“E disse o SENHOR Deus: Não é bom que o homem esteja só; far-lhe-ei uma ajudadora idônea para ele. E formou o SENHOR Deus da terra todo animal do campo, e toda ave dos céus, e os trouxe a Adão, para ver como este lhes havia de chamar; e tudo o que Adão chamou a toda criatura vivente, isso foi o seu nome. E Adão deu nomes a todo o gado, e às aves dos céus, e a todo animal do campo; mas para Adão não se achava ajudadora idônea para ele. Então o SENHOR Deus fez cair um sono pesado sobre Adão, e este adormeceu; e tomou uma de suas costelas, e fechou a carne em seu lugar. E da costela que o SENHOR Deus tomou do homem, formou uma mulher e a trouxe ao homem. E disse Adão: Esta é agora osso dos meus ossos e carne da minha carne; será chamada mulher, porquanto do homem foi tomada. Portanto deixará o homem seu pai e sua mãe, e se unirá à sua mulher; e serão ambos uma só carne” (Gênesis 2:18-24).

“E disse Deus: Façamos o homem à nossa imagem, conforme a nossa semelhança; e domine sobre os peixes do mar, e sobre as aves dos céus, e sobre o gado, e sobre toda a terra, e sobre todo réptil que se move sobre a terra. E criou Deus o homem à sua imagem; à imagem de Deus o criou; homem e mulher os criou. E Deus os abençoou; e Deus lhes disse: Sede fecundos, multiplicai-vos, enchei a terra e sujeitai-a; e dominai sobre os peixes do mar, e sobre as aves dos céus, e sobre todo ser vivente que se move sobre a terra” (Gênesis 1:26-28).

“E disse o Senhor Deus: Não é bom que o homem esteja só; far-lhe-ei uma ajudadora idônea para ele” (Gênesis 2:18). “Farei para ele uma ajudadora que lhe seja adequada.” Deus disse que faria isso.

“E criou Deus o homem à sua imagem; à imagem de Deus o criou; homem e mulher os criou” (Gênesis 1:27). Deus fez. Deus nos criou homem e mulher. É preciso muita fé cega para acreditar que evoluímos perfeitamente como homem e mulher. A criação do homem e da mulher é o plano de Deus. É uma das provas vivas da Criação. Deus fez. Deus criou. É o plano de Deus. Deus é o Autor. E o plano de Deus traz bênção.

Gostaria de examinar dez aspectos dessa bênção do plano de Deus.

1) Deus traz Eva a Adão.

“E da costela que o Senhor Deus tomou do homem, formou uma mulher e a trouxe ao homem. E disse Adão: Esta é agora osso dos meus ossos e carne da minha carne; será chamada mulher, porquanto do homem foi tomada” (Gênesis 2:22-23).

Deus fez Adão cair num sono profundo. Então Deus criou Eva e a trouxe a Adão. Adão despertou e percebeu: “Esta é para mim!” Ele tinha visto todos os animais passarem enquanto lhes dava nomes. Agora Deus lhe traz alguém que é para ele. Ele também percebeu: “Ela foi tirada do meu lado.” Ela está perto do seu coração. “Esta é osso dos meus ossos e carne da minha carne.” Não é um cachorro; não é uma girafa, nem um macaco, nem um símio. Aquela que Deus lhe trouxe é como ele. O plano de Deus traz bênção.

Adão e Eva nunca haviam tido um companheiro antes. Adão e Eva nunca haviam entregado a paixão de seus corações a outra pessoa. Algo aconteceu nos corações de Adão e Eva. Adão era “homem de uma só mulher”, e Eva era “mulher de um só homem”. Eles nunca entregaram a paixão de seus corações a mais ninguém. Deus também tem esse plano para nós. O plano de Deus traz bênçãos.

2) Deixar e unir-se em unidade para toda a vida.

“Portanto deixará o homem seu pai e sua mãe, e se unirá à sua mulher; e serão ambos uma só carne” (Gênesis 2:24).

Este versículo diz: “Portanto deixará o homem seu pai e sua mãe”, mas Adão e Eva não tinham pai nem mãe. O que Deus está dizendo é que não pode haver união sem que haja separação. Além disso, em Marcos 10:7, lemos: “Por esta causa deixará o homem seu pai e sua mãe, e se unirá à sua mulher.” Este é o plano de Deus, e o plano de Deus traz bênção.

Deixar significa abandonar, deixar para trás. “Por esta causa deixará o homem seu pai e sua mãe” significa deixar os pais para trás. Consideremos um jovem que tem uma vida familiar muito boa. Ele é abençoado e tem tudo de que precisa. No entanto, quando Deus traz a sua Eva para a vida dele, algo desperta dentro dele, e ele diz: “Vou partir!” Mas este é o plano de Deus. E o plano de Deus traz bênção.

Não se trata apenas de deixar o pai e a mãe; ele também se une à esposa. Unir-se significa “colar-se, aderir”. Conhecemos bem os painéis de madeira colados. Todo tipo de móvel resistente é feito de painéis colados. Se forem colados corretamente, não se separarão nas juntas. Se você os separar, terá de partir a madeira. A cola de Deus é assim: ela une duas pessoas. A única maneira de separá-las é despedaçando e rasgando, e Deus não abençoa isso. Mas deixar e unir-se, permanecer juntos e estar unidos, esse é o plano de Deus e traz bênção.

3) Serão uma só carne.

“Portanto deixará o homem seu pai e sua mãe, e se unirá à sua mulher; e serão ambos uma só carne” (Gênesis 2:24). Duas pessoas solteiras que se tornam um casal casado tornam-se uma unidade diante de Deus e uma família diante de Deus. Tornam-se uma só carne, e Deus os vê unidos como um só.

“E serão os dois uma só carne; assim já não são dois, mas uma só carne. Portanto, o que Deus ajuntou não o separe o homem” (Marcos 10:8-9). O plano de Deus para o homem e a mulher é que Ele traga Eva a Adão. Então ocorre a separação dos pais e a união do casal. Ele faz com que se tornem uma só carne. Separar-se não traz bênção alguma, mas traz agonia, dor, sofrimento e mágoa. Não há bênção na separação. Mas o plano de Deus traz bênção.

4) Não estar em jugo desigual.

“Não vos prendais a um jugo desigual com os infiéis; porque que comunhão tem a justiça com a injustiça?” (2 Coríntios 6:14-15). “A mulher está ligada pela lei enquanto o marido vive; mas, se o marido morrer, fica livre para casar com quem quiser, contanto que seja no Senhor” (1 Coríntios 7:39).

O plano de Deus é que o casamento seja um jugo igual. Deus não trará uma Eva a um Adão num casamento que seja um jugo desigual. Vamos pensar sobre deixar e unir-se, ficar unidos e os dois se tornarem um. No casamento, esses dois agora são um diante de Deus. Imagine estar num relacionamento conjugal ruim como esse — uma família assim tentando funcionar em conjunto. Não haverá bênção.

Mas um jugo igual traz bênção! Deus deseja que sejamos unidos em uma só carne, um só coração e uma só mente. Ele quer nos ver unidos em coração, mente e carne — todo o ser, sendo um. O plano de Deus traz bênção.

5) Deus planejou que tivéssemos filhos.

“E Deus os abençoou; e Deus lhes disse: Sede fecundos, multiplicai-vos, enchei a terra e sujeitai-a; e dominai sobre os peixes do mar, e sobre as aves dos céus, e sobre todo ser vivente que se move sobre a terra” (Gênesis 1:28). Pense na alegria e no milagre cada vez que mais uma criança nasce num lar cristão. Deus planejou assim. E, se Deus trouxe Eva a Adão, e eles deixam e se unem, tornam-se uma só carne, um só coração, uma só mente. Se estiverem unidos num mesmo jugo e Deus os abençoar com filhos, o lar se tornará um refúgio alegre onde Deus pode habitar. “E abençoou Deus a Noé e a seus filhos, e disse-lhes: Sede fecundos, multiplicai-vos e enchei a terra” (Gênesis 9:1). “E vós, sede fecundos e multiplicai-vos; produzi abundantemente na terra e multiplicai-vos nela” (Gênesis 9:7). O plano de Deus traz bênção.

6) Ordem de autoridade.

“Mas quero que saibais que Cristo é a cabeça de todo homem, e o homem a cabeça da mulher, e Deus a cabeça de Cristo” (1 Coríntios 11:3). Primeiro Deus, depois Cristo, o homem e a mulher. Deus estabeleceu uma ordem de autoridade, e essa ordem é uma bênção. É o plano de Deus, e é uma bênção.

“Filhos, obedecei a vossos pais no Senhor, porque isto é justo. Honra a teu pai e a tua mãe (que é o primeiro mandamento com promessa), para que te vá bem e vivas muito tempo sobre a terra” (Efésios 6:1-3). Filhos, obedecer a seus pais no Senhor faz parte da ordem de autoridade. Isso não é difícil de entender, não é? Um lar que segue o plano de Deus é simplesmente uma situação abençoada. Jovens, aprendam a estar sob autoridade. Façam disso sua prioridade máxima. Quanto mais cedo aprenderem a estar sob autoridade, mais bem preparados estarão para as responsabilidades da vida.

Lembro-me de pensar na vida de casado e de ter aspirações de ensinar crianças e criar uma família piedosa. Ouvi a série “Lar Piedoso” e pensei que estava pronto. Mas então chegou o dia em que chegou a minha vez e a minha responsabilidade, e, de repente, meu coração quis desfalecer. A responsabilidade não parece a mesma coisa que sonhar com ela. VOCÊ precisa fazer algo! VOCÊ é responsável. VOCÊ precisa fazer acontecer. E, aliás, não basta fazer acontecer; você precisa fazer acontecer de modo semelhante a Cristo. Você precisa fazer acontecer de tal maneira que a unção do Espírito de Deus possa descer sobre sua família. Quanto melhor aprendermos a estar sob autoridade, mais bem preparados estaremos para essas responsabilidades. Quanto mais reconhecermos que precisamos de Deus, melhor estaremos. Façamos da aprendizagem de estar sob autoridade, como crianças e jovens, uma prioridade máxima. “Meu filho, não te esqueças da minha lei; e o teu coração guarde os meus mandamentos; porque eles aumentarão os teus dias e te acrescentarão anos de vida e paz” (Provérbios 3:1-2).

Deus acrescentará sua bênção se permanecermos nessa ordem de autoridade. Quanto mais você aprender a estar sob autoridade, mais será abençoado quando estabelecer seu lar. O plano de Deus traz bênçãos.

7) Um casamento piedoso.

Efésios 5:21,22,24 diz: “Sujeitando-vos uns aos outros no temor de Deus. Vós, mulheres, sujeitai-vos a vosso próprio marido, como ao Senhor. . . Portanto, assim como a igreja está sujeita a Cristo, assim também as mulheres o sejam em tudo a seus próprios maridos.”

Antes de tudo, observem o versículo 21: “sujeitando-vos uns aos outros”. Há uma união que precisa acontecer num lar piedoso. Essa união deve acontecer no temor de Deus. Se nos sujeitarmos uns aos outros no temor de Deus, obedeceremos a Deus porque queremos suas bênçãos.

Efésios 5:22,24: “Vós, mulheres, sujeitai-vos a vosso próprio marido, como ao Senhor. . . Portanto, assim como a igreja está sujeita a Cristo, assim também as mulheres o sejam em tudo a seus próprios maridos.” Jovens mulheres, podem contar com isto: submeter-se ao pai equivale a submeter-se ao marido. Vocês podem praticar enquanto são solteiras. Isso ajudará a formar o caráter de vocês. Ser uma mulher rebelde e obstinada não trará a bênção de Deus.

O texto prossegue, em Efésios 5:25,28,29: “Maridos, amai vossas mulheres, como também Cristo amou a igreja e se entregou por ela . . . Assim devem os maridos amar as suas próprias mulheres como a seus próprios corpos. Quem ama a sua mulher ama a si mesmo. Porque nunca ninguém odiou a sua própria carne; antes a alimenta e dela cuida, assim como o Senhor cuida da igreja.” Jovens homens, isso diz que os maridos devem amar suas mulheres. Então, quem vocês acham que Deus colocou na vida de vocês para prepará-los a amar a esposa? A mãe de vocês! Querem aprender a amar a futura esposa? Aprendam a conviver com a mãe de vocês, a amá-la e a se importar com ela. Querem praticar amar a futura esposa? Amem a mãe de vocês.

Versículo 33: “Todavia, cada um de vós ame também a sua mulher como a si mesmo; e a mulher reverencie o marido.” O plano de Deus traz bênçãos.

8) Ser herdeiros juntos da graça da vida.

1 Pedro 3:7: “Igualmente vós, maridos, vivei com elas com conhecimento, dando honra à mulher, como ao vaso mais fraco, e como herdeiros juntos da graça da vida, para que não sejam impedidas as vossas orações.” Como maridos, honramos a esposa. Ela é o vaso mais fraco e a que deu à luz os filhos! Ela passou por muitas mudanças traumáticas na vida. É ela quem se desgasta e se cansa mais depressa.

E ele diz: “Maridos, vivei com elas com conhecimento.”

Jovens homens, aprendam a compreender a mãe e as irmãs de vocês. Isso os ajudará depois que se casarem. Não concluam: “Ah, isso é coisa de mulher.” Não; vocês querem a bênção de Deus. Aprendam a conhecê-las e compreendê-las.

“Herdeiros juntos da graça da vida.” Deus quer que sejamos herdeiros juntos da graça da vida. Se não formos herdeiros juntos da graça da vida, poderemos ser herdeiros separados da graça da vida? Não creio. Ele diz que devemos ser herdeiros juntos para que nossas orações não sejam impedidas. Então, se formos herdeiros separados, poderíamos dizer que nossas orações serão impedidas? Sim, nossas orações serão impedidas. Honremos a esposa como ao vaso mais fraco. Cada pequeno progresso que vocês fizerem nesta área só os abençoará mais tarde. Vale a pena. O plano de Deus traz bênção.

9) Um lar abençoado e seguro.

Isto vem em parte de 1 Pedro 3:7, mas também do Salmo 144:12: “Que nossos filhos sejam como plantas crescidas na sua juventude; que nossas filhas sejam como pedras angulares, polidas à semelhança de um palácio.” A graça de Deus está sobre um lar seguro onde há unidade. Onde o pai compreende a mãe e se importa com ela. O pai serve e está presente para ajudar e orientar. Está presente para dar direção com um coração compassivo. O plano de Deus para o homem e a mulher — o plano de Deus traz bênçãos.

10) Como Cristo e a igreja.

“Portanto, assim como a igreja está sujeita a Cristo, assim também as mulheres o sejam em tudo a seus próprios maridos. Maridos, amai vossas mulheres, como também Cristo amou a igreja e se entregou por ela; para santificá-la e purificá-la com a lavagem da água, pela palavra; para apresentá-la a si mesmo como igreja gloriosa, sem mancha, nem ruga, nem coisa semelhante, mas santa e irrepreensível. Assim devem os maridos amar as suas próprias mulheres como a seus próprios corpos. Quem ama a sua mulher ama a si mesmo. Porque nunca ninguém odiou a sua própria carne; antes a alimenta e dela cuida, assim como o Senhor cuida da igreja” (Efésios 5:24-29).

“Maridos, amai vossas mulheres, como também Cristo amou a igreja e se entregou por ela.” Deus procura homens dispostos a dar a vida. Jovens solteiros dispostos a atender ao chamado e dar a vida. Este é um alto chamado de Deus. É o plano de Deus.

Jovens homens, estão dispostos a abrir mão da vida de vocês, dos seus planos e das coisas independentes de que gostam? Estão dispostos a ser pacientes, gentis e compreensivos? Estão dispostos a perder o sono e continuar, mesmo quando estiverem cansados? Estão dispostos a manter a calma e não reagir em circunstâncias estressantes? Estão dispostos a liderar e guiar uma esposa e filhos, almas eternas, ao longo desta vida?

Mas meu apelo é que vocês se ofereçam e digam: “Estou disposto a me dedicar à Palavra de Deus, à vontade de Deus, ao plano de Deus, e darei a minha vida. Estou disposto a colocá-la sobre o altar.” Jesus deu a vida por nós, e Ele compara o casamento com a igreja e consigo mesmo.

Também há necessidade de mães submissas e sujeitas à autoridade. Mães que não sigam a liberação feminina dos nossos dias, mas que estejam contentes em cuidar do lar.

Jovens mulheres, estão dispostas a se alistar? Entregarão o coração para serem guiadas e conduzidas? Estão dispostas a seguir e a se submeter alegremente à autoridade de vocês? Estão dispostas a servir e a se despender pela família? Estão dispostas a servir e a se despender pela SUA família? Se algum dia se casarem, será a SUA família que vocês servirão e pela qual se despenderão. Estão dispostas a suportar dor e desconforto? Estão dispostas a ser uma ajudadora idônea, dedicando-se ao fardo e à visão dele?

Ao considerarmos o plano e as bênçãos de Deus, vocês querem a bênção de Deus, jovens! Mas isso significa que precisam fazer escolhas de acordo com esse propósito. Levantem-se e tomem decisões que conduzam à maturidade. A maturidade vem no processo de buscar a Deus. Comprometam-se, no coração, a se abrirem às bênçãos e aos princípios de Deus. Encorajo vocês a andar com Deus, a ter um relacionamento com Jesus Cristo e a fazer isso com humildade.

Busquem um caráter semelhante ao de Cristo, e façam isso intencionalmente. É muito fácil simplesmente viver a vida como ela acontece. Mas, se tomarmos decisões intencionais, elas nos levarão a algum lugar! Essas decisões são importantes. Façam as coisas de acordo com o plano de Deus.

Deus tem um plano para o homem e a mulher, e tem um plano para vocês.
